items.text: When a supervised task has not completed an execution within its configured maximum interval, counted from the alive-supervision start instant to its first completed execution after that instant and from each later completed execution of that task to its next completed execution, the supervisor shall detect an alive fault for that task, where the alive-supervision start instant is the instant at which the start-up integrity checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 that follow a reset have both passed while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is not held.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-018). Approval of the first-completion timing: not done by the author, by disagreement with that part of the requested change. An approval is a human decision that the inputs do not contain, and the author may not invent one (forge-c-hi rule 1); the timing therefore stays an author choice recorded in blocking open point OP-SYS-032 for resolution by a human, and the requirement text is unchanged. Test criterion: changed so that each alive fault is observed for its target task before any reset that could prevent its deadline from expiring (case c is now one target task per run, and the observation condition applies to cases a to c); the existence of a test configuration meeting that condition is not given by the inputs and is added as OP-SYS-032 item (f). Rework r1 (F-sys-req-item-r1-001). Makes 'stops running' in STK-SUP-001 observable as the absence of a completed execution within a configured interval (STK-SUP-004). Start of alive supervision: the inputs do not state it. STK-SUP-007 allows the application to run only after the start-up checks have passed, so the earliest instant at which a supervised task can be expected to run is the instant at which both start-up checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 that follow a reset have passed; this is the alive-supervision start instant, after every reset, and it is the same check-pass instant used by SYS-SAF-003. It is chosen instead of the start of the first application task so that a task, or the scheduler of CON-SUP-006, that never starts after passed checks is still detected. Deadline of the first completion: the configured maximum interval counted from the alive-supervision start instant; each later deadline is counted from the preceding completed execution, as before. No alive supervision is required while no application task is allowed to run: before the checks pass, after a failed check (SYS-MEM-003) and while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is held. These choices are not given by the inputs and are recorded for confirmation in blocking open point OP-SYS-032, together with whether a separate configured first-completion limit is needed to allow for scheduler start-up. The fault instant of SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 for SYS-SUP-001 is stated there only from the preceding completed execution; the corresponding instant for the first completion is recorded in OP-SYS-032 item (d); those items are not changed here. Test criterion, once OP-SYS-032 is resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with check completions, task completions, alive-fault detections and resets instrumented, for each supervised task as the target task, each case in its own run (a) suppress its first execution after passed start-up checks and observe an alive fault for that task once the configured maximum interval has elapsed from the alive-supervision start instant; (b) suppress its completions after at least 2 completed executions and observe an alive fault once the configured maximum interval has elapsed from the last completed execution; (c) hold the scheduler of CON-SUP-006 stopped after passed start-up checks and observe an alive fault for the target task once its configured maximum interval has elapsed from the alive-supervision start instant. In cases (a) to (c) the alive fault of the target task is observed after the expiry of its deadline and before any reset of the controller; each run uses a configuration (STK-SUP-004) in which no other detected fault of the supervisor and no watchdog expiry leads to a reset before that deadline expires, so that the reset after the earliest fault of the run cannot prevent the deadline of the target task from expiring; a run in which a reset occurs before that deadline has expired counts as not passed for the target task; (d) run every supervised task completing within its configured maximum interval and observe no alive fault; (e) with the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 held, observe no alive fault.

items.text: When the configured maximum activation delay of a supervised task has elapsed after a scheduled activation time of that task without an execution of that task for that scheduled activation time having started, as defined in SYS-SUP-003, at or after that scheduled activation time, the supervisor shall detect a late-activation fault for that scheduled activation time of that task without waiting for that execution to start, where: an execution is for the scheduled activation time whose activation by the timer-driven scheduler of CON-SUP-006 it processes, as in the assignment of an execution to an expected activation instance in SYS-SUP-004; each execution is for at most one scheduled activation time; the start of an execution for any other scheduled activation time of that task, earlier or later, does not satisfy this item for that scheduled activation time, whatever the length of the configured maximum activation delay compared with the period of that task; and the instant at which that delay has elapsed is the fault instant from which SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 count the 50 ms reaction.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-019). The previous guard accepted any start of the task at or after the scheduled activation time, so when the configured maximum activation delay is longer than the task period, the start for the next scheduled activation time fell inside the delay of a missed one and satisfied it, and the missed activation escaped detection. Of the two requested options, the item now defines which start satisfies each scheduled activation time: only the start of the execution that processes the activation issued for that scheduled activation time, the same assignment rule that SYS-SUP-004 uses for expected activation instances, and one execution satisfies at most one scheduled activation time. This holds whatever the delay is compared with the period, so the item does not depend on a delay limit. The other option, a limit of the delay to less than the period, is not chosen by the author: approving it is a human decision that the inputs do not contain (forge-c-hi rule 1); whether such a limit is required in addition stays in OP-SYS-033 item (c). Matching starts to scheduled activation times by their count in time order was rejected, because after one missed activation every later start would be matched to the activation before it, and with a delay longer than the period this one-activation lag would never be detected. The assignment needs the activation processed by each execution to be identifiable on the simulator of SYS-TST-001, and the inputs do not say how an activation issued after a scheduler stall covering more than one scheduled activation time is assigned; both are recorded in OP-SYS-033 item (c). Test criterion: case (c) added for a missed activation followed by the start of the next instance, run with a delay shorter than the period and, unless OP-SYS-033 item (c) limits it, with a delay longer than the period; late-activation fault detections are now instrumented and observed for the target scheduled activation time, and each run is required to have no other detected fault and no watchdog expiry before the delay expires, since a program-flow fault of SYS-SUP-004 at the start of the next instance in the configured order, or of SYS-SUP-005 at the end of the control cycle, would otherwise lead to the safe state without showing the late-activation detection; whether such a configuration exists is OP-SYS-033 item (e). Rework r1 (F-sys-req-item-r1-002). Covers 'runs too late' in STK-SUP-002 against configured timing (STK-SUP-004). Trigger: the previous wording ('starts later than') made the fault known only once the task started, so a task that stays unstarted could be detected late or never. The trigger is now the expiry of the configured maximum activation delay counted from the scheduled activation time with no start of that task at or after that time; this covers both a task that starts late and a task that never starts, and the item requires detection without waiting for a start. Relation to the reaction deadline: the expiry instant is the same fault instant that SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 already state for SYS-SUP-002, so the 50 ms of STK-SUP-009 counts from it and the supervisor detection latency lies inside the 50 ms; the configured maximum activation delay itself lies before the fault instant and is not part of the 50 ms (confirmation of this reading is OP-SYS-029 item a). Scheduled activation times are the instants of the timer-driven schedule of CON-SUP-006 for the period of that task, so they exist whether or not the scheduler actually activates the task. Not given by the inputs and recorded in blocking open point OP-SYS-033 rather than decided here: the reference instant from which the scheduled activation times are counted after each reset; the states in which late-activation supervision applies (related OP-SYS-032 item c); and, superseded by rework r2, the overlap of a delay longer than the task period with the next activation, now handled by the assignment of each start to one scheduled activation time (related SYS-SUP-005). Test criterion, once OP-SYS-029 and OP-SYS-033 are resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with scheduled activation times, execution starts each with the scheduled activation time it is for, late-activation fault detections, other fault detections, watchdog expiries, resets, control outputs and the status signal instrumented, for at least one supervised task of each period of CON-SUP-006 as the target task, each case in its own run: (a) hold the target task unstarted after a scheduled activation time and observe, without the task ever starting, a late-activation fault for that scheduled activation time, every control output in its off state per SYS-SAF-001 and the status signal at the not-operational indication per SYS-SAF-002 no later than 50 ms after the configured maximum activation delay has elapsed from that scheduled activation time; (b) delay the start for one scheduled activation time beyond the configured maximum activation delay and let it start afterwards, and observe the same outcome counted from the expiry of the delay, not from the late start; (c) suppress the execution for one scheduled activation time while letting the executions for the following scheduled activation times of the target task start at their scheduled activation times, and observe the same outcome for the missed scheduled activation time counted from the expiry of its delay, with the start for the next scheduled activation time not accepted for the missed one; run case (c) once with a configured maximum activation delay shorter than the period of the target task and, unless the resolution of OP-SYS-033 item (c) limits the delay to less than the period, once with a delay longer than the period, so that the start for the next scheduled activation time occurs before the delay of the missed one has elapsed; (d) start the target task for every scheduled activation time within its configured maximum activation delay and observe no late-activation fault. In cases (a) to (c) the late-activation fault of the target scheduled activation time is observed at or after the expiry of its delay and before any reset of the controller; each run uses a configuration (STK-SUP-004) in which no other fault is detected and no watchdog expires before that expiry, so that the observed safe state follows from the late-activation fault; a run in which another fault is detected or a reset occurs before that expiry counts as not passed for the target task; whether such a configuration exists for each target task is OP-SYS-033 item (e).

items.text: When the elapsed time counted from the start of an execution of a supervised task reaches the configured maximum execution time of that task before that execution has completed, the supervisor shall detect an execution-time fault for that task without waiting for that execution to complete, where the start and the completion of an execution are the instants at which the task begins and ends the processing of one activation by the timer-driven scheduler of CON-SUP-006, the elapsed time is wall-clock time that includes every interval in which that execution is preempted by another task or interrupted, and the instant at which the configured maximum execution time is reached is the fault instant from which SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 count the 50 ms reaction.
items.rationale: Rework r1 (F-sys-req-item-r1-003). Covers 'takes too long' in STK-SUP-002 against configured timing (STK-SUP-004). Time counted: the previous wording 'lasts longer' did not say whether the configured limit applies to elapsed time or to processor execution time. The item now counts elapsed wall-clock time from the start of the execution, including preemption by other tasks (the 10 ms tasks of CON-SUP-006 can preempt a 100 ms task) and interrupts, because that quantity is observable at the task boundary on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 from instrumented starts and completions alone, and because it bounds how late the results of the execution become available. Processor execution time excluding preemption and interrupts is the alternative reading; the inputs do not decide between them, so the choice is recorded for confirmation in blocking open point OP-SYS-034 item (a) rather than treated as given. Measurement events: start is the instant at which the task begins processing one activation of the scheduler of CON-SUP-006, completion the instant at which it ends the processing of that same activation; they are intended to be the events meant by 'started an execution' in SYS-SUP-002 and 'completed execution' in SYS-SUP-001, which are not changed here (confirmation in OP-SYS-034 item b). An execution that completes at or before the instant at which the limit is reached is not a fault. Ongoing execution: the trigger is the limit being reached while the execution has not completed, and the item requires detection without waiting for completion, so an execution that never completes (a hung task) is detected; the fault instant is the same as the one SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 already state for SYS-SUP-003 ('the execution has lasted the configured maximum execution time without completing'), so the supervisor detection latency lies inside the 50 ms of STK-SUP-009 (related OP-SYS-029 item a). Not given by the inputs and recorded in OP-SYS-034: confirmation of the start and completion events and their observation on the simulator, the controller states in which this supervision applies, and the accepted measurement resolution. Test criterion, once OP-SYS-029 and OP-SYS-034 are resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with task starts, task completions, control outputs and the status signal instrumented, for at least one supervised task of each period of CON-SUP-006 (a) hold an execution uncompleted after its start and observe, without that execution ever completing, every control output in its off state per SYS-SAF-001 and the status signal at the not-operational indication per SYS-SAF-002 no later than 50 ms after the configured maximum execution time has elapsed from the start; (b) extend an execution beyond the configured maximum execution time and let it complete afterwards, and observe the same outcome counted from the instant the limit was reached, not from the late completion; (c) for a 100 ms task, run an execution whose own processing is shorter than its limit but whose elapsed time exceeds the limit because of preemption by 10 ms tasks, and observe an execution-time fault; (d) run every execution of every supervised task completing within its configured maximum execution time, including preemption, and observe no execution-time fault.

items.text: When an execution of a supervised task starts for an expected activation instance of a control cycle before an execution has started for every expected activation instance of that same control cycle that precedes it in the configured execution order of SYS-SUP-008, the supervisor shall detect a program-flow fault, where: a control cycle is the interval from one cycle boundary, inclusive, to the next cycle boundary, exclusive, the cycle boundaries being the schedule reference instant of OP-SYS-033 item (a) and every instant a whole multiple of 100 ms after it; the expected activation instances of a control cycle are, for each supervised task, the scheduled activation times of that task as defined in SYS-SUP-002 that lie within that control cycle, which are 10 instances for a task of 10 ms period and 1 instance for a task of 100 ms period of CON-SUP-006, each identified by the task and by its position, numbered from one in time order, among the scheduled activation times of that task within that control cycle; the configured execution order is one sequence of all expected activation instances of a control cycle, identified in this way, that applies to every control cycle; an execution belongs to the expected activation instance whose activation it processes, whichever control cycle contains its start; and the execution event whose order is checked is the start of an execution as defined in SYS-SUP-003.
items.rationale: Rework r1 (F-sys-req-item-r1-004). Covers 'wrong order' in STK-SUP-003 with the order set by configuration (STK-SUP-004). The previous wording left 'control cycle' open (OP-SYS-009), so the same execution sequence could be judged differently depending on how a verifier grouped activations into cycles. The item now states one grouping rule. (Cycle boundaries) CON-SUP-006 gives periods of 10 ms and 100 ms; 100 ms is a whole multiple of 10 ms, so 100 ms is the shortest interval after which the scheduled activation pattern of both rates repeats, and every control cycle of 100 ms contains the same set of expected activation instances; one configured order can therefore apply to every cycle. The boundaries are aligned to the same schedule reference instant from which the scheduled activation times of SYS-SUP-002 are counted (OP-SYS-033 item a), so cycle boundaries and scheduled activation times use one time base. A 10 ms control cycle with the 100 ms tasks expected in one of every 10 cycles is the alternative reading; the inputs do not decide between them. (Expected activation instances) Any half-open interval of 100 ms contains exactly 100 ms divided by the period scheduled activation times of a task whose period divides 100 ms, whatever the phase of that task, so each 10 ms task has 10 instances and each 100 ms task has 1 instance per control cycle; instances are named by task and position so that the configured order can place, for example, the single 100 ms instance between two given 10 ms instances. Only supervised tasks (SYS-SUP-006) have expected instances. (Grouping) An execution is assigned to a cycle by the scheduled activation time of the activation it processes, not by the instant it starts, so an execution that starts after the next cycle boundary is still judged in the cycle of its activation; this removes the dependence on the verifier's grouping. (Events) The order checked is the order of execution starts, the event defined in SYS-SUP-003; completions are not used because a 100 ms execution preempted by 10 ms executions completes after executions that started later. Starts are also the events of the SYS-SUP-004 fault instant already stated in SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 ('the start of the first execution of a supervised task in the control cycle that is out of the configured execution order'), which are not changed here. (Relation to SYS-SUP-005) An instance that never starts does not violate this item by itself; but when a later instance of the same cycle in the configured order starts, this item detects a program-flow fault at that start. Executions of different control cycles are not ordered against each other by this item. These choices are not given by the inputs and are recorded for confirmation in blocking open point OP-SYS-035 (refines OP-SYS-009 for SYS-SUP-004), together with the first control cycle supervised after each reset and the controller states in which this supervision applies; SYS-SUP-005, SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 still cite OP-SYS-009 and are not changed here. Test criterion, once OP-SYS-033 and OP-SYS-035 are resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with scheduled activation times and execution starts instrumented and a configuration of at least two supervised 10 ms tasks and one supervised 100 ms task, (a) run every control cycle with the starts in the configured order and observe no program-flow fault; (b) exchange the starts of two instances of one cycle and observe a program-flow fault whose fault instant is the start of the first instance that starts out of the configured order; (c) start the 100 ms instance before a 10 ms instance that precedes it in the configured order and observe a program-flow fault at that start; (d) delay the start of the last instance of a cycle in the configured order past the next cycle boundary while keeping the configured order within each cycle and observe no program-flow fault from this item; (e) suppress one instance of a cycle that is not the last in the configured order and observe a program-flow fault at the start of the next instance in the configured order.

items.text: When no execution that belongs, under SYS-SUP-004, to an expected activation instance of a supervised control cycle has started, as defined in SYS-SUP-003, before the end of that control cycle, the supervisor shall detect a program-flow fault for that instance without waiting for a later start of that instance, where: the control cycles, their expected activation instances and the assignment of an execution to an instance are those defined in SYS-SUP-004, which are 10 instances for each supervised task of 10 ms period and 1 instance for each supervised task of 100 ms period of CON-SUP-006 in every control cycle; every expected activation instance of a control cycle is required in that control cycle, whatever its position in the configured execution order of SYS-SUP-008; the end of a control cycle is the cycle boundary of SYS-SUP-004 that closes it, so an execution that starts at or after that boundary does not satisfy this item for that instance; the supervised control cycles are those that begin at or after the alive-supervision start instant of SYS-SUP-001 that follows the most recent reset; and the end of that control cycle is the fault instant from which SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 count the 50 ms reaction.
items.rationale: Rework r1 (F-sys-req-item-r1-005). Covers 'one of them is skipped' in STK-SUP-003, with the order and task set from configuration (STK-SUP-004). The previous wording left the control cycle and the expected activations open (OP-SYS-009), so a verifier was unable to tell which executions were required or when a missing one became a skip. (Required instances) The item reuses the control-cycle definition of SYS-SUP-004 (100 ms cycles aligned to the schedule reference instant of OP-SYS-033 item a) and its expected activation instances, so order and skip supervision judge the same instances: each supervised 10 ms task is required 10 times and each supervised 100 ms task once per control cycle, each instance identified by task and position. Every instance is required, not only one execution per task, because a skipped 10 ms activation is a skipped task execution of that cycle. An execution counts for the instance whose activation it processes (SYS-SUP-004), so an execution of the next activation of the same task cannot stand in for a skipped one. (Cutoff) An instance is skipped when no execution belonging to it has started before the closing cycle boundary of the cycle that contains its scheduled activation time. The start event of SYS-SUP-003 is used, as in SYS-SUP-004, so a started execution that is still running at the boundary (for example a 100 ms execution preempted by 10 ms tasks) is not a skip; overrun of such an execution is the subject of SYS-SUP-003. The closing boundary is chosen as cutoff because SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 already state the SYS-SUP-005 fault instant as the end of the control cycle in which the expected task did not execute; those items are not changed here. The item requires detection without waiting for the instance to start, so an instance that never starts, including when the scheduler of CON-SUP-006 stops, is detected; the supervisor detection latency lies inside the 50 ms. (Scope) Control cycles are supervised from the first one that begins at or after the alive-supervision start instant of SYS-SUP-001 after the most recent reset, so a cycle that began before the application was allowed to run is not judged; no cycle is supervised while no alive-supervision start instant exists after a reset (failed start-up check of SYS-MEM-003, or latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 held). (Relation to other items) An instance that starts after its cycle end is a skip under this item, while SYS-SUP-004 test (d) states only that SYS-SUP-004 itself does not detect it; if the configured maximum activation delay of the task ends before that cycle end, SYS-SUP-002 detects the late activation first. A skipped instance followed by the start of a later instance in the configured order is also a program-flow fault under SYS-SUP-004 at that start (OP-SYS-035 item f); a skipped last instance in the configured order is detected only by this item. These choices are not given by the inputs and are recorded for confirmation in blocking open point OP-SYS-036 (refines OP-SYS-009 for SYS-SUP-005). Test criterion, once OP-SYS-033, OP-SYS-035 and OP-SYS-036 are resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with scheduled activation times, execution starts, cycle boundaries, control outputs and the status signal instrumented and a configuration of at least two supervised 10 ms tasks and one supervised 100 ms task, (a) start every instance of every supervised cycle before its cycle end and observe no program-flow fault from this item; (b) suppress one 10 ms instance, (c) suppress the 100 ms instance, and (d) suppress the last instance in the configured order of one cycle, and in each case observe every control output in its off state per SYS-SAF-001 and the status signal at the not-operational indication per SYS-SAF-002 no later than 50 ms after the end of that cycle; (e) delay the start of one instance to after the end of its cycle and observe the same outcome counted from the cycle end, not from the late start; (f) start one instance before its cycle end by no more than the measurement resolution of OP-SYS-036 item (g) and observe no program-flow fault from this item.

items.text: The supervisor shall take the set of supervised tasks from configuration data that can be changed without changing the supervisor program code.

The supervisor shall take the timing limits of each supervised task used by SYS-SUP-001, SYS-SUP-002 and SYS-SUP-003 from configuration data that can be changed without changing the supervisor program code.

The supervisor shall take the expected execution order of the supervised tasks used by SYS-SUP-004 and SYS-SUP-005 from configuration data that can be changed without changing the supervisor program code.
The controller shall supervise its operation with an independent watchdog that is clocked from a clock source separate from the processor clock.
items.rationale: STK-SUP-006 asks for an independent watchdog with its own clock; CON-SUP-003 makes IWDG available.

items.text: When the time elapsed since the current interval reference instant reaches the independent-watchdog timeout without a servicing of the independent watchdog of SYS-WDG-001, the independent watchdog shall reset the controller, where: the interval reference instant is, from the release of each reset of the controller as defined in OP-SYS-031, whatever the cause of that reset, until the first servicing of the independent watchdog after that release, that release, and from then on the most recent servicing of the independent watchdog; a servicing is a refresh of the independent watchdog by the controller software that the independent watchdog accepts, each servicing ending the current interval and beginning the next one; and the independent-watchdog timeout is a value in ms that lies within the approved timeout range recorded in OP-SYS-038.
items.rationale: Rework r1 (F-sys-req-item-r1-006). STK-SUP-005 requires that a failure the software does not handle still ends in a hardware reset; STK-SUP-006 requires the independent watchdog with its own clock (SYS-WDG-001). (First interval) The previous wording gave no reference for the first unserviced interval, so a controller that fails after a reset and before its first servicing (for example a hang during the start-up integrity checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002, or a failure before the scheduler of CON-SUP-006 starts) might never be reset. The first interval after every reset, whatever its cause (power-on, watchdog, supervisor or other reset of SYS-RST-001 and SYS-RST-002), is now counted from the release of that reset, the same release instant as SYS-SAF-003 (OP-SYS-031 item b), so no instant after a release lies outside a supervised interval. This choice is derived from STK-SUP-005 and is not stated by the inputs; an alternative, an interval that begins when the controller software starts the independent watchdog with an approved maximum delay after the release, leaves the failures before that start uncovered and is recorded as an alternative in OP-SYS-038 item (b), not decided here. (Restart) Each servicing accepted by the independent watchdog ends the current interval and starts the next one, counted from that servicing; when the controller software services it is the subject of SYS-WDG-005 and SYS-WDG-006, which are not changed here. (Timeout) No approved timeout value or range exists in the inputs, and the actual timeout of a watchdog clocked from its own clock source depends on platform facts not in the inputs (clock source, its frequency tolerance, prescaler and reload resolution, to be cited from CON-SUP-002 RM0486 by section and page). The approved range with its unit, and the constraints on it, are recorded in blocking open point OP-SYS-038 (refines the independent-watchdog timeout part of OP-SYS-004) rather than invented. Whether the platform can start the independent watchdog at the release of a reset without software, whether it can be stopped once started, and how this interacts with a failed start-up check (SYS-MEM-003) and the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 (SYS-REC-003), are also part of OP-SYS-038. The watchdog-event instant used by SYS-SAF-004 and SYS-SAF-005 for SYS-WDG-002 is stated there only from the last servicing; the corresponding instant for the first interval after a release, without any servicing, is recorded in OP-SYS-038 item (f); those items are not changed here. Test criterion, once OP-SYS-031 and OP-SYS-038 are resolved and subject to OP-SYS-037 item (b): on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with reset releases, independent-watchdog servicings and controller resets instrumented, (a) after a power-on, a watchdog reset and a supervisor reset, prevent every servicing of the independent watchdog from the release onwards and observe a reset of the controller whose elapsed time from the release lies within the approved range of OP-SYS-038; (b) let the controller service the independent watchdog at least 2 times and then prevent every further servicing, and observe a reset whose elapsed time from the last servicing lies within that range; (c) service the independent watchdog at intervals shorter than the lower limit of that range, the first one counted from the release, for at least 10 times the upper limit of that range, and observe no reset caused by the independent watchdog.

items.text: When the controller software makes a service attempt on the window watchdog at an instant at which the time elapsed since the current window reference instant is less than the window-opening time, the window watchdog shall reset the controller no later than the early-service reset latency recorded in OP-SYS-039 after that service attempt, where: a service attempt is a refresh request written by the controller software to the window watchdog, whether or not the window watchdog accepts it as a servicing; a servicing is a service attempt that the window watchdog accepts; the window reference instant is, after the release of each reset of the controller as defined in OP-SYS-031, whatever the cause of that reset, the window-watchdog start instant recorded in OP-SYS-039 that follows that release until the first servicing after that start instant, and from then on the most recent servicing; and the window-opening time is the configured value in ms that lies within the approved window-opening range recorded in OP-SYS-039.
items.rationale: Rework r1 (F-sys-req-item-r1-007). STK-SUP-006 requires a window watchdog that detects servicing too early; STK-SUP-005 makes the hardware reset the reaction; CON-SUP-003 makes WWDG available. (Trigger) The previous wording ('serviced before its configured window opens') made the trigger a servicing, which an early refresh is not if the window watchdog rejects it, so a tester could not tell whether a rejected early refresh had to cause a reset. The trigger is now the service attempt, the refresh request written by the controller software, whether accepted or not, so it is observable on the controller side by instrumenting refresh requests (OP-SYS-037 item f) and testable whether or not the attempt is accepted. An attempt at an elapsed time equal to or greater than the window-opening time is not early under this item; a missing or late servicing is the subject of SYS-WDG-004, which is not changed here. (Timing origin) The previous wording gave no reference event from which the opening is counted. In subsequent windows the reference is the most recent servicing, each servicing ending one window and starting the next. In the start-up window after every reset, whatever its cause (power-on, watchdog, supervisor or other reset of SYS-RST-001 and SYS-RST-002), there is no servicing yet; the reference is the window-watchdog start instant that follows the release of that reset (release as in OP-SYS-031 item b, also used by SYS-WDG-002 and SYS-SAF-003). The inputs do not state whether the window watchdog of the STM32N657X0 starts at the release of a reset without software or only when the controller software enables it, so the start instant, and an approved maximum delay from the release if the software starts it, are recorded in blocking open point OP-SYS-039 item (b) rather than assumed. (Opening) No approved window-opening value or range exists in the inputs, and the achievable opening depends on platform facts not in the inputs (window-watchdog clock, prescaler, counter and window resolution, behaviour on an early refresh, reset latency, to be cited from CON-SUP-002 RM0486 by section and page); the approved range in ms, the configuration holding the value, and the reset latency are recorded in OP-SYS-039 (refines the window-opening part of OP-SYS-004) rather than invented. (Related items) SYS-SAF-004 and SYS-SAF-005 state the SYS-WDG-003 watchdog-event instant as 'the instant at which the window watchdog is serviced before its configured window opens'; reading it as the instant of the early service attempt is recorded in OP-SYS-039 item (f); those items are not changed here. Test criterion, once OP-SYS-031 and OP-SYS-039 are resolved and subject to OP-SYS-037 items (b) and (c): on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with reset releases, window-watchdog start, service attempts, servicings and controller resets instrumented, (a) after a power-on, a watchdog reset and a supervisor reset, make the first service attempt after the window-watchdog start instant at an elapsed time below the lower limit of the approved window-opening range and observe a reset of the controller no later than the early-service reset latency after that attempt; (b) let the controller make at least 2 servicings, then make a service attempt at an elapsed time below that lower limit counted from the last servicing, and observe the same outcome; (c) in (a) and (b), record whether the window watchdog accepted the early attempt and observe the reset in either case; (d) make service attempts at elapsed times at or above the upper limit of the approved window-opening range and before the window closes under SYS-WDG-004, in the start-up window and in at least 10 subsequent windows, and observe no reset caused by the window watchdog.

items.text: When the time elapsed since the current window reference instant reaches the window-closing time without a servicing of the window watchdog, the window watchdog shall reset the controller no later than the late-service reset latency recorded in OP-SYS-040 after the instant at which the window-closing time is reached, where: a servicing is a refresh request written by the controller software to the window watchdog that the window watchdog accepts, each servicing ending the current window and beginning the next one; the window reference instant is, after the release of each reset of the controller as defined in OP-SYS-031, whatever the cause of that reset, the window-watchdog start instant recorded in OP-SYS-039 that follows that release until the first servicing after that start instant, and from then on the most recent servicing; and the window-closing time is the configured value in ms, held in the configuration data recorded in OP-SYS-040, that lies within the approved window-closing range recorded in OP-SYS-040.
items.rationale: Rework r1 (F-sys-req-item-r1-008). STK-SUP-006 requires a window watchdog that detects servicing too late; STK-SUP-005 makes the hardware reset the reaction to a failure the software does not handle; CON-SUP-003 makes WWDG available. (Window closing) The previous wording ('before its configured window closes') relied on a window-closing value that OP-SYS-004 does not define and named no configuration holding it. The item now refers to the window-closing time as a configured value in ms within an approved window-closing range, and to the configuration data that holds it; neither the range nor that configuration exists in the inputs, so both are recorded in blocking open point OP-SYS-040 items (a) and (b) (refines the window-closing part of OP-SYS-004) rather than invented. (Timing reference) The previous wording gave no event from which the closing is counted. The item uses the same window reference instant as SYS-WDG-003, so the opening and the closing of one window are counted from one event: in the start-up window after every reset, whatever its cause (power-on, watchdog, supervisor or other reset of SYS-RST-001 and SYS-RST-002), the window-watchdog start instant of OP-SYS-039 item (b) that follows the release of that reset (release as in OP-SYS-031 item b, also used by SYS-WDG-002 and SYS-SAF-003); in each subsequent window, the most recent servicing, each accepted servicing ending one window and starting the next. A refresh request that the window watchdog rejects is not a servicing and does not start a window; an early service attempt is the subject of SYS-WDG-003, which is not changed here. (Reset deadline) A late-service reset latency in ms, counted from the instant the window-closing time is reached, makes the reset instant measurable; its approved value and the platform facts on which it depends (to be cited from CON-SUP-002 RM0486 by section and page) are recorded in OP-SYS-040 items (c) and (d). (Related items) SYS-SAF-004 and SYS-SAF-005 state the SYS-WDG-004 watchdog-event instant as 'the instant at which the configured window of the window watchdog closes without servicing'; reading it as the instant at which the window-closing time of this item is reached, in the start-up window and in subsequent windows, is recorded in OP-SYS-040 item (e); SYS-WDG-003 test (d) refers to the window closing under this item; those items are not changed here. Test criterion, once OP-SYS-031, OP-SYS-039 and OP-SYS-040 are resolved and subject to OP-SYS-037 items (b) and (c): on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with reset releases, window-watchdog start, service attempts, servicings and controller resets instrumented, (a) after a power-on, a watchdog reset and a supervisor reset, prevent every service attempt from the window-watchdog start instant onwards and observe a reset of the controller no later than the late-service reset latency after the configured window-closing time has elapsed from that start instant; (b) let the controller make at least 2 servicings, then prevent every further service attempt and observe the same outcome counted from the last servicing; (c) make service attempts after the window opens under SYS-WDG-003 and before the configured window-closing time is reached, in the start-up window and in at least 10 subsequent windows, and observe no reset caused by the window watchdog.

items.text: While the task-health condition holds, the controller software shall service the independent watchdog of SYS-WDG-001 so that the time elapsed since the current interval reference instant of SYS-WDG-002 does not reach the lower limit of the approved independent-watchdog timeout range recorded in OP-SYS-038, where: the task-health condition holds at an instant when every supervised task of SYS-SUP-006 is healthy at that instant; a supervised task is healthy at an instant when, judged against the configured task set, timing limits and execution order of SYS-SUP-006, SYS-SUP-007 and SYS-SUP-008, all of the following hold at that instant: (a) an alive-supervision start instant of SYS-SUP-001 has occurred after the release, as defined in OP-SYS-031, of the most recent reset of the controller, (b) the task has completed at least one execution, as defined in SYS-SUP-003, after that alive-supervision start instant, (c) at least one supervised control cycle of SYS-SUP-005 has ended after that alive-supervision start instant, and (d) since that alive-supervision start instant no fault of SYS-SUP-001, SYS-SUP-002 or SYS-SUP-003 has been detected for that task and no program-flow fault of SYS-SUP-004 or SYS-SUP-005 has been detected; and a servicing and the interval reference instant are as defined in SYS-WDG-002.
items.rationale: Rework r1 (F-sys-req-item-r1-009, F-sys-req-item-r1-010). Split: this item keeps the independent-watchdog service obligation and defines the task-health condition; the window-watchdog service obligation is split into SYS-WDG-007 and the service condition before task health is first established into SYS-WDG-008; all three use this one task-health condition. (F-009, health evidence) The previous guard, the absence of a detected task fault, held before any supervision had run, for example at start-up, while STK-SUP-005 permits servicing only while every supervised task is healthy. Health is now positive evidence, judged against the configuration of STK-SUP-004 (SYS-SUP-006 to SYS-SUP-008): (a) supervision has started after the most recent reset, the alive-supervision start instant of SYS-SUP-001 existing only after both start-up checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 have passed and while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is not held; (b) the task has shown a completed execution, the event of SYS-SUP-001 and SYS-SUP-003; (c) one whole supervised control cycle has been judged by the skip supervision of SYS-SUP-005, so every expected activation instance of the task has started at least once in that cycle; (d) no task fault has been detected since supervision started. A program-flow fault of SYS-SUP-004 or SYS-SUP-005 removes the health of every task, because SYS-SUP-004 does not attribute it to one task (related OP-SYS-014). Health is not regained until the next reset, consistent with SYS-WDG-006 and the recovery of SYS-REC-001. Memory-integrity faults are not part of the condition, because STK-SUP-005 names only task health (OP-SYS-004; SYS-REC-001 relies on this). These choices are not given by the inputs and are recorded for confirmation in blocking open point OP-SYS-041. (F-010, separate obligations) The obligation is stated against the independent watchdog only, as a bound on the elapsed time since the interval reference instant of SYS-WDG-002 below the lower limit of the approved timeout range of OP-SYS-038, so it is judged from independent-watchdog servicings alone, whatever the window-watchdog servicing. Using the lower limit of the range keeps the obligation met for every timeout within the range; whether a further margin for clock tolerance is needed is OP-SYS-041 item (e). At the instant the condition is first met after a reset, the elapsed time since the release already counts; the feasibility constraint on the timeout range that follows is OP-SYS-038 item (a) and OP-SYS-041 item (b). Test criterion, once OP-SYS-031, OP-SYS-038 and OP-SYS-041 are resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with reset releases, check-pass instants, task completions, control-cycle boundaries, detected faults and independent-watchdog servicings instrumented, and a configuration of at least two supervised 10 ms tasks and one supervised 100 ms task of CON-SUP-006, (a) after a power-on, a watchdog reset and a supervisor reset, run every supervised task fault-free for at least 10 times the upper limit of the approved timeout range of OP-SYS-038 counted from the first instant the task-health condition holds; compute that instant from the records under items (a) to (d) of this item and observe, at every instant from then on, an elapsed time since the current interval reference instant below the lower limit of that range and no reset caused by the independent watchdog; (b) repeat (a) with the window-watchdog servicing of the controller unchanged and observe that the verdict of (a) is reached from independent-watchdog records alone.

items.text: While the task-health condition of SYS-WDG-005 holds, the controller software shall service the window watchdog so that the time elapsed since the current window reference instant of SYS-WDG-003 does not reach the lower limit of the approved window-closing range recorded in OP-SYS-040 and each service attempt that it makes on the window watchdog is made at an elapsed time since the current window reference instant at or above the upper limit of the approved window-opening range recorded in OP-SYS-039, where a service attempt, a servicing and the window reference instant are as defined in SYS-WDG-003 and SYS-WDG-004.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-WDG-005 (F-sys-req-item-r1-010). STK-SUP-005 requires servicing while every supervised task is healthy and STK-SUP-006 requires a window watchdog that detects servicing too early and too late. The window-watchdog obligation is stated separately from the independent-watchdog obligation of SYS-WDG-005, so a controller that meets the independent-watchdog timeout but misses the window-watchdog service band fails this item alone. It references the same task-health condition, defined once in SYS-WDG-005 (F-sys-req-item-r1-009). The service band is bounded by the approved ranges, not by single configured values: the earliest permitted attempt is at the upper limit of the window-opening range of OP-SYS-039 and the deadline is the lower limit of the window-closing range of OP-SYS-040, so the obligation is met for every opening and closing value within those ranges; OP-SYS-039 item (a) and OP-SYS-040 item (a) already require the opening upper limit to lie below the closing lower limit, so the band is not empty. The item uses the service attempt of SYS-WDG-003, whether accepted or not, so a rejected early refresh request is a violation. One verb (service) with one compliance criterion, the band, is stated; the early and the late bound are both observable from the same records. Whether a margin for clock tolerance is needed inside the band, and the reading of OP-SYS-038 to OP-SYS-040 references to SYS-WDG-005 for the window watchdog as references to this item, are recorded in OP-SYS-041. Test criterion, once OP-SYS-031, OP-SYS-039, OP-SYS-040 and OP-SYS-041 are resolved and subject to OP-SYS-037 item (b): on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with reset releases, the window-watchdog start instant, service attempts, servicings, task completions, control-cycle boundaries and detected faults instrumented, and the configuration of the SYS-WDG-005 test, (a) after a power-on, a watchdog reset and a supervisor reset, run every supervised task fault-free over at least 10 windows counted from the first instant the task-health condition of SYS-WDG-005 holds and observe, at every instant from then on, an elapsed time since the current window reference instant below the lower limit of the window-closing range, every service attempt at an elapsed time at or above the upper limit of the window-opening range, and no reset caused by the window watchdog; (b) observe that the verdict of (a) is reached from window-watchdog records alone, whatever the independent-watchdog servicing.

items.text: From the release, as defined in OP-SYS-031, of each reset of the controller until the first instant after that release at which the task-health condition of SYS-WDG-005 holds, the controller software shall not service the independent watchdog of SYS-WDG-001 or the window watchdog, where any service attempt on the window watchdog as defined in SYS-WDG-003 counts as servicing it.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-WDG-005 (F-sys-req-item-r1-009). STK-SUP-005 permits watchdog servicing only while every supervised task is healthy, so a failure the software does not handle still ends in a hardware reset. Before the task-health condition of SYS-WDG-005 is first met after a reset, task health has not been established, so this item states the service condition for that interval as no servicing of either watchdog, taken from the wording of STK-SUP-005 and not from an approved start-up allowance, of which none exists in the inputs. The interval covers the start-up integrity checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002, a failed check (SYS-MEM-003) and the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002, in which no alive-supervision start instant of SYS-SUP-001 exists, so the condition is not met and no servicing occurs; repeated watchdog resets in those states follow. After the condition has been met and is later lost, SYS-WDG-006 applies, which is not changed here. Consequences not decided here and recorded in blocking open point OP-SYS-041 items (b) and (c): the independent-watchdog timeout of OP-SYS-038 and the window-closing time of OP-SYS-040 must then exceed the time from the release of a reset to the first instant of the task-health condition in a healthy start-up, which includes both start-up checks and at least one whole control cycle; an approved start-up service condition, for example servicing during the start-up checks, is the alternative that would replace this item; and the behaviour after a failed check and while latched is to be confirmed against OP-SYS-038 item (e), OP-SYS-039 item (g), OP-SYS-040 item (f) and OP-SYS-023 item (d). Test criterion, once OP-SYS-031 and OP-SYS-041 are resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with reset releases, check-pass instants, task completions, control-cycle boundaries, independent-watchdog servicings and window-watchdog service attempts instrumented, (a) after a power-on, a watchdog reset and a supervisor reset with a healthy configuration, observe no servicing of either watchdog from the release until the first instant the task-health condition holds; (b) suppress the first completed execution of one supervised task after passed start-up checks and observe no servicing of either watchdog from the release onwards; (c) inject a start-up check failure under SYS-TST-004 and observe no servicing of either watchdog from the release until the next reset.

items.text: From the detection instant of a fault specified in SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005, whether detected for one supervised task or as a program-flow fault, until the start, as defined in OP-SYS-031, of the next reset of the controller, whatever the cause of that reset, the controller software shall not service the independent watchdog of SYS-WDG-001 or the window watchdog, where: the detection instant is the instant at which the supervisor detects that fault, which is the detection referred to in item (d) of the task-health condition of SYS-WDG-005; a servicing of the independent watchdog is as defined in SYS-WDG-002; any service attempt on the window watchdog as defined in SYS-WDG-003 counts as servicing it; the inhibit is not ended by the fault ceasing to be present, by any later start, completed execution or in-order execution of a supervised task, by the safe state of SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002, or by the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002; and after that reset, servicing is permitted only as stated in SYS-WDG-008, SYS-WDG-005 and SYS-WDG-007.
items.rationale: Rework r1 (F-sys-req-item-r1-011). STK-SUP-005 permits watchdog servicing only while every supervised task is healthy, so that a failure the software does not handle still ends in a hardware reset. The previous wording ('while a fault ... is detected') left the duration of the inhibit open: a fault detected briefly and followed by resumed servicing could satisfy one reading while defeating the reset fallback of STK-SUP-005. (Start) The inhibit starts at the detection instant, the same detection that ends task health in SYS-WDG-005 item (d), so the two items use one event and no instant exists at which SYS-WDG-005 requires servicing and this item forbids it. The fault instant of SYS-SAF-001 is not used as the start because the supervisor cannot act before it detects the fault; whether an approved maximum delay in ms from that fault instant to the detection instant, and hence to the start of the inhibit, is required is recorded in OP-SYS-042 item (b). (End) The only event that ends the inhibit is the start of the next reset of the controller, whatever its cause (supervisor reset of SYS-REC-001, watchdog reset of SYS-WDG-002 to SYS-WDG-004, power-on or other reset of SYS-RST-001 and SYS-RST-002); no state transition or recovery inside the same run permits servicing again, so a fault that disappears, a task that resumes, or entry into the safe state or the latched safe state does not end it. This keeps the watchdog reset available as the fallback when the supervisor reset of SYS-REC-001 does not occur: with servicing stopped, the timeout of SYS-WDG-002 and the window closing of SYS-WDG-004 run out. After the reset, SYS-WDG-008 forbids servicing until the task-health condition of SYS-WDG-005 is established again, and SYS-WDG-005 and SYS-WDG-007 then govern servicing; while the latched safe state is held no alive-supervision start instant exists, so SYS-WDG-008 keeps servicing stopped (related OP-SYS-041 item c). These items are not changed here. (Actor) The obligation is stated on the controller software, as in SYS-WDG-005, SYS-WDG-007 and SYS-WDG-008, so that no other software services a watchdog during the inhibit; a rejected window-watchdog service attempt also counts, as in SYS-WDG-008. (Scope) Memory-integrity faults of SYS-MEM-004 are not part of the trigger because STK-SUP-005 names only task health (OP-SYS-041 item d, OP-SYS-004). The resulting precedence between the supervisor reset and the watchdog reset is open in OP-SYS-022 item (b) and OP-SYS-004. These choices are not given by the inputs and are recorded for confirmation in blocking open point OP-SYS-042. Test criterion, once OP-SYS-031, OP-SYS-041 and OP-SYS-042 are resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with fault detections, independent-watchdog servicings, window-watchdog service attempts and reset starts instrumented, and the configuration of the SYS-WDG-005 test, after the task-health condition of SYS-WDG-005 holds (a) inject each fault type of SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005 under SYS-TST-002 and observe no independent-watchdog servicing and no window-watchdog service attempt from the detection instant until the start of the next reset; (b) suppress one completed execution of one supervised task so that a fault of SYS-SUP-001 is detected, then let every supervised task run fault-free, and observe the same outcome, the resumed task executions not restoring servicing; (c) with the latch condition of SYS-REC-002 met, observe no servicing of either watchdog from the detection instant of the fault that causes the latched safe state until the start of the next reset; (d) in (a) to (c), observe that a reset of the controller starts, so that the inhibited interval is bounded.

items.text: When the program code of the controller holds, at the release of a reset as defined in OP-SYS-031, a corruption that lies within the program-code areas recorded in OP-SYS-052 item (a) and belongs to a corruption class recorded in OP-SYS-052 item (b), the controller shall detect that corruption by a failed result of its start-up program-code integrity check given no later than the earlier of the start of the first application task after that release and the start-up detection deadline recorded in OP-SYS-052 item (c) after that release, where the detection event is the instant of that failed result, observed by the means recorded in OP-SYS-052 item (d), and the deadline applies whether or not an application task starts after that release.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-004). STK-SUP-007 requires the integrity outcome (program code found intact before the application runs) and does not prescribe a mechanism, so no stored reference is mandated. (Coverage and classes) The finding asks for approved code regions and corruption classes. The inputs give neither, and the author cannot approve them (hi-core rule 1): naming memory regions of the STM32N657X0 (CON-SUP-001) or a detection capability would invent hardware facts and requirements. They are recorded as blocking open point OP-SYS-052 items (a) and (b), which refines the non-blocking OP-SYS-012 for this item, so the stage cannot be accepted until a reviewer decides them; OP-SYS-012 is not changed and stays for SYS-MEM-002 and SYS-TST-004. (Observed detection event) The item now defines the detection event as the instant at which the start-up program-code integrity check gives its failed result. This is the same instant used as the detection instant of SYS-DIAG-001 and as the failed check of SYS-MEM-003, SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002. The previous bound 'before the first application task starts' is vacuous in a corrupted start-up, where SYS-MEM-003 forbids any task start, so a test could never conclude that detection was missing. The bound is now the earlier of the first application-task start and a deadline counted from the release of the reset (OP-SYS-031), which gives a closed observation window in every start-up. The deadline value is not in the inputs and is recorded in OP-SYS-052 item (c). How the failed result is observed is recorded in OP-SYS-052 item (d) for confirmation; the author's proposal is instrumentation accepted under OP-SYS-037 item (f), with the fault report of SYS-DIAG-001 as boundary evidence. The status signal (SYS-SAF-003) and the absence of task starts (SYS-MEM-003) are not accepted as the detection event, because a start-up that hangs without detecting anything shows the same outcomes. A corruption that stops the check from giving any result, for example one in the code executed before or by the check, cannot produce this event; how it is treated is recorded in OP-SYS-052 item (e). Test criterion, once OP-SYS-052 is resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001, for each corruption of the accepted set (OP-SYS-037 item e), placed under SYS-TST-004 in the areas of item (a) before the release of a reset, the record of SYS-TST-006 shows a failed result of the start-up program-code check, observed as in item (d), no later than the earlier of the first application-task start and the deadline of item (c) after that release. The run fails if no failed result is recorded within that window, including when no application task ever starts. Control case: with the same memory not corrupted, no failed result is recorded.

items.text: When the configuration data of the controller holds, at the release of a reset as defined in OP-SYS-031, a corruption that lies within the configuration data recorded in OP-SYS-053 item (a) and belongs to a corruption class recorded in OP-SYS-053 item (b), the controller shall detect that corruption by a failed result of its start-up configuration-data integrity check given no later than the earlier of the start of the first application task after that release and the start-up detection deadline recorded in OP-SYS-053 item (c) after that release, where the detection event is the instant of that failed result, observed by the means recorded in OP-SYS-053 item (d), and the deadline applies whether or not an application task starts after that release.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-005). Rework r1 (F-014) removed the stored-reference mechanism because STK-SUP-007 requires the integrity outcome (configuration data found intact before the application runs) and no input prescribes a mechanism; that remains. (Covered data and classes) The finding asks for approved configuration data and corruption classes. The inputs give neither, and the author cannot approve them (hi-core rule 1): naming memory regions of the STM32N657X0 (CON-SUP-001), the contents of the configuration or a detection capability would invent hardware facts and requirements. STK-SUP-004 only says that the supervised tasks, their timing and their order are set by configuration; whether other data (for example watchdog or diagnostic-line settings) counts as configuration data is not stated. They are recorded as blocking open point OP-SYS-053 items (a) and (b), which refines the non-blocking OP-SYS-012 for this item, so the stage cannot be accepted until a reviewer decides them; OP-SYS-012 is not changed and stays for SYS-TST-004. (Observed detection event) The item now defines the detection event as the instant at which the start-up configuration-data integrity check gives its failed result, the same form as SYS-MEM-001, and the instant used as the failed check of SYS-MEM-003. The previous bound 'before the first application task starts' is vacuous in a corrupted start-up, where SYS-MEM-003 forbids any task start, so a test could never conclude that detection was missing. The bound is now the earlier of the first application-task start and a deadline counted from the release of the reset (OP-SYS-031), which gives a closed observation window in every start-up. The deadline value is not in the inputs and is recorded in OP-SYS-053 item (c). How the failed result is observed is recorded in OP-SYS-053 item (d) for confirmation; the author's proposal is instrumentation accepted under OP-SYS-037 item (f), with the fault report of SYS-DIAG-001 as boundary evidence. The status signal (SYS-SAF-003) and the absence of task starts (SYS-MEM-003) are not accepted as the detection event, because a start-up that hangs without detecting anything shows the same outcomes. Corruptions that alter the check's own inputs (for example a coverage descriptor or reference value held in the configuration data) or are used before the check gives a result are recorded in OP-SYS-053 item (e); the interaction with a failed program-code check of SYS-MEM-001 in the same start-up is recorded in item (f). Test criterion, once OP-SYS-053 is resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001, for each corruption of the accepted set (OP-SYS-037 item e), placed under SYS-TST-004 in the configuration data of item (a) before the release of a reset, with the program code not corrupted, the record of SYS-TST-006 shows a failed result of the start-up configuration-data check, observed as in item (d), no later than the earlier of the first application-task start and the deadline of item (c) after that release. The run fails if no failed result is recorded within that window, including when no application task ever starts. Control case: with the same configuration data not corrupted, no failed result is recorded.

items.text: When a start-up integrity check of SYS-MEM-001 or SYS-MEM-002 fails, the controller shall not start any application task.
items.rationale: STK-SUP-007 requires the check before the application runs; a failed check is a detected fault under STK-SUP-009.

items.text: While the application tasks are running, the controller shall check the integrity of its program code in successive full passes, where a full pass is a pass in which every program-code memory address within the run-time coverage of OP-SYS-020 has been read by the integrity check since the start event of that pass, the start event of the first full pass is the start of the first application task after start-up, the start event of each later full pass is the completion of the preceding full pass, and each full pass completes within the full-pass time bound of OP-SYS-019 counted from its start event.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-006). Pass bound and coverage: the inputs give neither a full-pass time bound (STK-SUP-008 says only 'in a bounded time') nor the program code the run-time check covers. The author cannot resolve either value without inventing it (core rule 1), so both remain blocking open points for a human decision: OP-SYS-019 for the bound and OP-SYS-020 for the coverage. The item cannot be accepted until both are resolved. What the item now fixes is how a full pass is decided against those values. A pass counts as full only when every program-code address within the OP-SYS-020 coverage has been read by the integrity check since the pass's start event. The pass's completion is the instant at which that becomes true. So a partial pass never counts as a completion, and a sequence of partial passes cannot satisfy the time bound. Retained from r1: STK-SUP-008 asks for the check to repeat in the background, so the passes follow each other for as long as the application tasks run (F-016). Detection of corruption is split into SYS-MEM-006 (F-017). A detection under SYS-MEM-006 is a failed integrity check of SYS-MEM-004 for SYS-SAF-001, SYS-SAF-002 and SYS-DIAG-001. Test criterion, applicable once OP-SYS-019 and OP-SYS-020 are resolved: (1) On the simulator of SYS-TST-001, the program-code memory addresses read by the integrity check are recorded with time stamps, together with the start of the first application task. The record distinguishes these reads from instruction fetches and from reads by the application. (2) From this record alone, the tester derives each pass completion. The completion is the earliest instant at which every address within the OP-SYS-020 coverage has been read since the start event of that pass. Completion reports from the controller are cross-checked against the derived instants and are not accepted as evidence on their own. (3) The observation run contains at least 3 consecutive derived pass completions, which shows the passes repeat. (4) The test fails in any of 3 cases. First, the time from a start event to its derived completion exceeds the OP-SYS-019 bound. Second, the run passes the OP-SYS-019 bound after a start event and no completion has been derived. Third, the controller reports a pass completion while at least one covered address has not been read since the current start event. (5) Supporting evidence that each covered area is actually checked, not only read, comes from the fault-injection test of SYS-MEM-006. A corruption injected in each covered program-code area before a pass starts is detected by that pass's completion.

items.text: When a corruption of the program code that lies within the run-time program-code areas recorded in OP-SYS-055 item (a) and belongs to a corruption class recorded in OP-SYS-055 item (b) is present at the start event of a pass of the run-time program-code integrity check of SYS-MEM-004 and remains present until the full-pass time bound of OP-SYS-019 after that start event has elapsed, the controller shall detect that corruption by a failed result of that run-time check given no later than the full-pass time bound of OP-SYS-019 after that start event, where the detection event is the instant of that failed result, observed by the means recorded in OP-SYS-055 item (c), a pass ends at its completion as defined in SYS-MEM-004 when the check gives no failed result in that pass and at the detection event when it gives one, and the deadline applies whether or not that pass reaches its completion.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-033). Split from SYS-MEM-004 (F-017); STK-SUP-008 requires the run-time program-code check to find program-code corruption, and the item states the detection outcome without prescribing a mechanism. (Coverage and classes) The finding asks for approved run-time coverage and corruption classes. The inputs give neither, and the author cannot approve them (hi-core rule 1): naming memory regions of the STM32N657X0 (CON-SUP-001) or a detection capability would invent hardware facts and requirements. They are recorded as blocking open point OP-SYS-055 items (a) and (b), which refines OP-SYS-020 for this item, in the same lettered form as OP-SYS-052 for SYS-MEM-001, so the stage cannot be accepted until a reviewer decides them. OP-SYS-020 is not changed and stays for SYS-MEM-004. (Observed detection event) The detection event is now the instant at which the run-time check gives its failed result. This is the failed integrity check of SYS-MEM-004 used by SYS-SAF-001, SYS-SAF-002 and SYS-DIAG-001. How it is observed is recorded in OP-SYS-055 item (c); the author's proposal is instrumentation of the check result accepted under OP-SYS-037 item (f), with the SYS-DIAG-001 fault report as boundary evidence. The status signal and the control outputs are not accepted as the detection event, because other faults produce the same outcomes. (Pass endpoint) The previous bound, the completion of the full pass, was vacuous for a pass that ends on detection: SYS-MEM-004 defines completion as every covered address having been read, which a pass that stops at its failed result never reaches, so a test could not decide whether detection was late or missing. The item now fixes both endpoints: a clean pass ends at its completion as defined in SYS-MEM-004, a failed pass ends at the detection event. The deadline is the full-pass time bound of OP-SYS-019 counted from the start event of the pass, so the observation window is closed in both cases. Confirmation of these endpoints, and how the timing criterion of SYS-MEM-004 treats a pass that ends at a failed result, are recorded in OP-SYS-055 item (d); SYS-MEM-004 is not changed in this item rework. (Precondition) The corruption must be present at a start event and stay present until the deadline, so a tester can place it deterministically. A corruption that appears during a pass in an area already read in that pass is present at the next start event and is covered by the same obligation for the next pass; the resulting worst case of up to twice the OP-SYS-019 bound after its first presence is the latency used by SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 (OP-SYS-029 item c). Corruptions that stop or divert the check before it gives a result are recorded in OP-SYS-055 item (e). Test criterion, once OP-SYS-019 and OP-SYS-055 are resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001, for each corruption of the accepted set (OP-SYS-037 item e) within items (a) and (b), placed under SYS-TST-004 at a start event of a pass as stated in OP-SYS-055 item (f), the record of SYS-TST-006 shows a failed result of the run-time check, observed as in item (c), no later than the OP-SYS-019 bound after that start event. The run fails if no failed result is recorded within that window, whether the pass completes clean or no completion and no failed result are recorded. Control case: in a run with the same program code not corrupted and at least 3 consecutive full passes derived as in SYS-MEM-004, no failed result of the run-time check is recorded.

items.text: While a full pass of the run-time program-code integrity check of SYS-MEM-004 is in progress and the application tasks of CON-SUP-006 run under the reference workload recorded in OP-SYS-054 item (b), the controller shall keep each timing quantity recorded in OP-SYS-054 item (c) of each application task recorded in OP-SYS-054 item (a) within the timing-interference limit recorded in OP-SYS-054 item (e) for that task and timing quantity, measured against the baseline recorded in OP-SYS-054 item (d).
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-007). (Scope, kept from rework r1, F-sys-req-item-r1-018) STK-SUP-008 protects the application timing without restricting it to supervised tasks, and the supervised task set is configurable (STK-SUP-004), so the author's proposal remains every application task run by the scheduler of CON-SUP-006, supervised or not; it is recorded for confirmation in OP-SYS-054 item (a). The supervision limits of SYS-SUP-007 are fault-detection thresholds and are not used as an interference allowance. (Approval) The finding asks for approval of the protected timing quantities, workload, baseline, limits and accepted evidence for target timing. The inputs give none of them and the author cannot approve them (hi-core rule 1): choosing quantities or limits would invent requirements, and stating that the Renode simulator of CON-SUP-005 does or does not represent the timing of the STM32N657X0 (CON-SUP-001) would invent a platform fact. Each decision is now a separate lettered entry of blocking open point OP-SYS-054, items (a) to (g). OP-SYS-054 refines OP-SYS-021 for this item and adds the workload (item b) and the paired-run test design (item g), which OP-SYS-021 did not name. OP-SYS-021 is not changed because OP-SYS-025 also refers to it. The item text cites each entry by letter, so a reviewer's decision completes the item without rewording, and the stage cannot be accepted until OP-SYS-054 is decided. (Workload) The obligation is now bound to the reference workload of item (b), because the interference caused by the check depends on what the tasks and the supervisor execute at the same time. Item (b) asks whether this is the reference workload of OP-SYS-025 item (b). (Baseline) SYS-MEM-004 runs full passes back to back from the first application-task start, so in operation every task activation after that start falls within a pass. A baseline without the check therefore exists only in a test configuration in which the check does not run. Item (d) asks whether that paired baseline, a configuration different from the target build (OP-SYS-037 item c), or absolute limits are approved. (Evidence and test alignment) The previous rationale named a simulator paired-run comparison as the verdict. The inputs do not establish that simulator timing represents the target, so that comparison is no longer stated as the verdict on its own. Item (f) asks which evidence is accepted for target timing and item (g) asks for the paired-run design; the test criterion below is written against those entries. The verification method stays test pending item (f). If item (f) accepts only analysis, or a combination of test and analysis, the method is changed when OP-SYS-054 is resolved. Test criterion, once OP-SYS-054 is resolved: in the environment accepted in item (f), under the workload of item (b), with the time source and resolution of item (g), a run with full passes of SYS-MEM-004 in progress is compared with the baseline of item (d) over the observation interval of item (g). For every task of item (a), every quantity of item (c) and every task activation in that interval, paired as stated in item (g), the measured value minus the baseline value does not exceed the limit of item (e); with absolute limits the baseline value is zero. The run with the check fails if, as recorded under SYS-TST-006, no full pass of SYS-MEM-004 both starts and completes within the observation interval. If item (f) accepts the simulator for only part of the evidence, the paired-run verdict covers only that part and the remainder is verified by the evidence item (f) names. Allocation includes hardware because the check of SYS-MEM-004 may use the CRC peripheral of CON-SUP-003, whose memory accesses can affect task timing.

items.text: When a fault specified in SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005 is detected or an integrity check of SYS-MEM-001, SYS-MEM-002 or SYS-MEM-004 fails, the controller shall reach, no later than 50 ms after the fault instant, a state in which every control output listed in OP-SYS-028 is simultaneously in the off state recorded for that output in OP-SYS-028, observed at the GPIO pin of CON-SUP-003 that drives that output, where: that state is reached at the first instant at or after the fault instant at which every control output is in its off state, which is the fault instant itself when every control output is already in its off state at the fault instant; and the fault instant is: for SYS-SUP-001, the instant at which the configured maximum interval of the task has elapsed without a completed execution of that task, counted from the alive-supervision start instant of SYS-SUP-001 when the task has completed no execution since that instant, and otherwise from the most recent completed execution of that task; for SYS-SUP-002, the instant at which the configured maximum activation delay has elapsed after the scheduled activation time without the task having started; for SYS-SUP-003, the instant at which the execution has lasted the configured maximum execution time without completing; for SYS-SUP-004, the start of the first execution of a supervised task in the control cycle that is out of the configured execution order; for SYS-SUP-005, the end of the control cycle, as defined in SYS-SUP-005, before which no execution belonging to the expected activation instance has started; for SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002, the release, as defined in OP-SYS-031, of the reset that precedes the failed check; for SYS-MEM-004, the instant at which the corruption detected under SYS-MEM-006 is first present in the program code.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-013, F-sys-req-item-r2-014); keeps the rework r1 structure (F-sys-req-item-r1-019, F-sys-req-item-r1-020). (Alive-fault start events, F-sys-req-item-r2-013) SYS-SUP-001 detects an alive fault from two reference events: the alive-supervision start instant, for the first completed execution after each reset, and each later completed execution. The previous text counted the SYS-SUP-001 fault instant only from a preceding completed execution, so a task, or the scheduler of CON-SUP-006, that never completes after passed start-up checks had no fault instant and the 50 ms of STK-SUP-009 had no start event. The fault instant now uses both: the configured maximum interval counted from the alive-supervision start instant while the task has completed no execution since that instant, otherwise from its most recent completed execution.
