This is the instant at which SYS-SUP-001 is first violated in each case, so the detection latency stays inside the 50 ms. It is the instant proposed in OP-SYS-032 item (d); whether a separate first-completion limit replaces the configured maximum interval for the first completion is still OP-SYS-032 item (b) and is restated in OP-SYS-064 item (b). (Other fault instants) SYS-SUP-002 and SYS-SUP-003 state their own fault instants, which this item repeats unchanged. For SYS-SUP-005 the previous reference to the control cycle of OP-SYS-009 is replaced by the end of the control cycle defined in SYS-SUP-005, which that item already names as the fault instant. For SYS-SUP-004 the fault instant is the out-of-order start, as before. For a failed start-up check the corruption already exists when the controller starts, so the fault instant is the release of the preceding reset, with the release defined in OP-SYS-031. For run-time corruption the fault instant is its first presence; on the simulator it is the injection instant of SYS-TST-005 recorded under SYS-TST-006. A corruption that appears just after its area was checked is detected no later than the full-pass bound of OP-SYS-019 after the start of the next pass (SYS-MEM-006), and each pass starts no later than that bound after the start of the preceding one (SYS-MEM-004), so detection takes less than twice that bound. The item is feasible only if that latency plus the output reaction fits in 50 ms (OP-SYS-029 item c). (Outputs already off, F-sys-req-item-r2-014) The state is defined by the pin states and not by a change: it is reached at the first instant at or after the fault instant at which every control output is in its off state, which is the fault instant itself when all are already off. This is the same rule SYS-REC-001 uses for the safe-state entry instant and SYS-SAF-002 uses for the status signal. The verdict for such an injection is therefore a measured reaction of 0 ms, a pass. This applies to a failed start-up check, where at the release of the reset the outputs have the reset-time pin state of OP-SYS-028 item (d). It can also apply to a missing first completion, where no application task has yet switched an output on. The unqualified precondition 'control outputs initially on' is removed. Such an injection does not show a switch-off, so the test needs at least one injection per fault class with an output not off at the fault instant where the application under test allows it (OP-SYS-064 item e). (Approval requested, F-sys-req-item-r2-014) The finding asks for approval of the output-off criteria and the fault instants. The inputs give no control-output list, no off state and no approved fault-instant definition, and hi-core rule 1 forbids the author to approve or invent them. That part of the finding therefore cannot be resolved by the author. The item states every rule as the author's proposal and cites the open values by open point: the output list and off states in OP-SYS-028, the fault instants in OP-SYS-029 and the proposals of this rework in OP-SYS-064 (refines OP-SYS-028, OP-SYS-029 and OP-SYS-032 item d for this item). A decision completes the item without rewording, but the stage cannot be accepted until they are decided. (Stimuli) Task faults are caused under SYS-TST-002, start-up memory corruptions under SYS-TST-004 and run-time memory corruptions under SYS-TST-005; the previous reference to SYS-TST-002 for corruption is replaced (OP-SYS-037 item h, for this item). (Peer alignment not made here) SYS-SAF-002 still states the SYS-SUP-001 fault instant only from a preceding completed execution and still cites OP-SYS-009 for SYS-SUP-005. SYS-REC-001 and SYS-REC-002 take the fault instant from this item and therefore use the new instants. Aligning SYS-SAF-002 is a change to another item, which is not made in this item rework, and is recorded in OP-SYS-064 item (g). (Kept from rework r1) The stop event is observed at the driving GPIO pin of CON-SUP-003. Watchdog events of STK-SUP-006 are in SYS-SAF-004. This item requires reaching the off state; whether it must also be held until the next reset is OP-SYS-064 item (d). Test criterion, once OP-SYS-028, OP-SYS-029 and OP-SYS-064 are resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with the records of SYS-TST-006, the control-output pins sampled continuously, including through any reset, and the fault instant computed from the stimuli, the records and the configured limits of SYS-SUP-007 and SYS-SUP-008 independently of the controller's own reports: (a) for each supervised task, suppress its completions after at least 2 completed executions (SYS-TST-002), fault instant counted from the last completed execution; (b) for each supervised task, suppress its first execution after passed start-up checks while the other supervised tasks run (SYS-TST-002), fault instant counted from the alive-supervision start instant; (c) stop the scheduler of CON-SUP-006 after passed start-up checks (SYS-TST-002), fault instant counted from the alive-supervision start instant for every supervised task; (d) cause each fault of SYS-SUP-002 to SYS-SUP-005 with the stimuli of SYS-TST-002; (e) place each corruption of SYS-TST-004 in the program code and in the configuration data before the release of a reset, fault instant at that release; (f) place each corruption of SYS-TST-005 once before the start of a full pass and once just after its area was checked in the current pass, fault instant at the recorded injection instant. In (a), (b), (d) and (f), run at least one injection per fault class with at least one control output not in its off state at the fault instant, by the means of OP-SYS-064 item (e). For each injection, the stop event is the first sample at or after the fault instant at which every control-output pin shows its off state, which is the fault instant when all pins already show it. Pass when the stop event is no later than 50 ms after the fault instant for every injection, and when the number of injections with an output not off at the fault instant meets OP-SYS-064 item (e).

items.text: When a fault specified in SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005 is detected or an integrity check of SYS-MEM-001, SYS-MEM-002 or SYS-MEM-004 fails, the controller shall reach, no later than 50 ms after the fault instant, a state in which the status signal is at the not-operational indication recorded in OP-SYS-030, observed at the GPIO pin of CON-SUP-003 that drives the status signal, where: that state is reached at the first instant at or after the fault instant at which the status signal is at the not-operational indication, which is the fault instant itself when the status signal is already at the not-operational indication at the fault instant; and the fault instant is the one stated for the same fault in SYS-SAF-001, namely: for SYS-SUP-001, the instant at which the configured maximum interval of the task has elapsed without a completed execution of that task, counted from the alive-supervision start instant of SYS-SUP-001 when the task has completed no execution since that instant, and otherwise from the most recent completed execution of that task; for SYS-SUP-002, the instant at which the configured maximum activation delay has elapsed after the scheduled activation time without the task having started; for SYS-SUP-003, the instant at which the execution has lasted the configured maximum execution time without completing; for SYS-SUP-004, the start of the first execution of a supervised task in the control cycle that is out of the configured execution order; for SYS-SUP-005, the end of the control cycle, as defined in SYS-SUP-005, before which no execution belonging to the expected activation instance has started; for SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002, the release, as defined in OP-SYS-031, of the reset that precedes the failed check; for SYS-MEM-004, the instant at which the corruption detected under SYS-MEM-006 is first present in the program code.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-015, F-sys-req-item-r2-016); keeps the rework r1 structure (F-sys-req-item-r1-021, F-sys-req-item-r1-022). (Alive-fault start events, F-sys-req-item-r2-015) SYS-SUP-001 detects an alive fault from two reference events: the alive-supervision start instant, for the first completed execution after each reset, and each later completed execution. The previous text counted the SYS-SUP-001 fault instant only from a preceding completed execution, so a task, or the scheduler of CON-SUP-006, that never completes after passed start-up checks had no start event for the 50 ms of STK-SUP-009. The fault instant now uses both expiry events: the configured maximum interval counted from the alive-supervision start instant while the task has completed no execution since that instant, otherwise from its most recent completed execution. This is the instant at which SYS-SUP-001 is first violated in each case, so the supervisor detection latency stays inside the 50 ms. Whether a separate first-completion limit replaces the configured maximum interval for the first completion is still OP-SYS-032 item (b) and OP-SYS-064 item (b), and applies to this item unchanged. Status signal before the first completion: SYS-SAF-003 holds the not-operational indication only until both start-up checks have passed, and no item requires the operational indication between that instant and the first completed execution; at a missing-first-completion fault instant the signal can therefore be at either indication. If it is already at the not-operational indication, the state is reached at the fault instant and the measured reaction is 0 ms; otherwise it must be reached within 50 ms. Whether the controller shows the operational indication in that interval is not given by the inputs and is OP-SYS-065 item (c). (Same fault instants as SYS-SAF-001, F-sys-req-item-r2-016) The fault instants are now word for word those of SYS-SAF-001, so the output switch-off and the status indication of one injection are judged from one fault instant. This also replaces the reference to the control cycle of OP-SYS-009 for SYS-SUP-005 by the end of the control cycle defined in SYS-SUP-005, and adds the release definition of OP-SYS-031 for a failed start-up check; together with the SYS-SUP-001 change this resolves OP-SYS-064 item (g) for this item. The reached-state rule (first instant at or after the fault instant, the fault instant itself when already shown) is the rule of SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-REC-001, now stated in the text instead of only in the rationale. For a failed start-up check SYS-SAF-003 already holds the not-operational indication at the release of the reset, so the measured reaction is 0 ms. For run-time corruption the fault instant is its first presence, on the simulator the injection instant of SYS-TST-005 recorded under SYS-TST-006; detection takes less than twice the full-pass bound of OP-SYS-019 (SYS-MEM-004, SYS-MEM-006), so the item is feasible only if that latency plus the status-signal reaction fits in 50 ms (OP-SYS-029 item c). (Stimuli, F-sys-req-item-r2-016) Task faults are caused under SYS-TST-002, start-up memory corruptions under SYS-TST-004 and run-time memory corruptions under SYS-TST-005; the previous reference to SYS-TST-002 for corruption is replaced (OP-SYS-037 item h, for this item). (Approval requested, F-sys-req-item-r2-016) The finding asks for approval of the status indication and the fault instants. The inputs give no status-signal pin, no indications and no approved fault-instant definition, and hi-core rule 1 forbids the author to approve or invent them, so that part of the finding cannot be resolved by the author. The item states every rule as the author's proposal and cites the open values by open point: the pin and indications in OP-SYS-030, the fault instants in OP-SYS-029, and the decisions this rework needs in OP-SYS-065 (refines OP-SYS-029, OP-SYS-030 item f and OP-SYS-064 item g for this item). A decision completes the item without rewording, but the stage cannot be accepted until they are decided. (Kept from rework r1) The stop event is observed at the driving GPIO pin of CON-SUP-003 and is also the status-signal change instant used by SYS-REC-001 and SYS-REC-002. Watchdog events of STK-SUP-006 are in SYS-SAF-005. This item requires reaching the not-operational indication; whether it must also be held until the next reset is OP-SYS-065 item (f). Test criterion, once OP-SYS-029, OP-SYS-030 and OP-SYS-065 are resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with the records of SYS-TST-006, the status-signal pin sampled continuously, including through any reset, in the same injection runs as the test criterion of SYS-SAF-001 and with the fault instant of each injection computed as there, from the stimuli, the records and the configured limits of SYS-SUP-007 and SYS-SUP-008 independently of the controller's own reports: (a) for each supervised task, suppress its completions after at least 2 completed executions (SYS-TST-002), fault instant counted from the last completed execution; (b) for each supervised task, suppress its first execution after passed start-up checks while the other supervised tasks run (SYS-TST-002), fault instant counted from the alive-supervision start instant; (c) stop the scheduler of CON-SUP-006 after passed start-up checks (SYS-TST-002), fault instant counted from the alive-supervision start instant for every supervised task; (d) cause each fault of SYS-SUP-002 to SYS-SUP-005 with the stimuli of SYS-TST-002; (e) place each corruption of SYS-TST-004 in the program code and in the configuration data before the release of a reset, fault instant at that release; (f) place each corruption of SYS-TST-005 once before the start of a full pass and once just after its area was checked in the current pass, fault instant at the recorded injection instant. In (a), (d) and (f), and in (b) and (c) by the means of OP-SYS-065 item (c), run at least one injection per fault class with the status signal at the operational indication at the fault instant. For each injection, the stop event is the first sample at or after the fault instant at which the status-signal pin shows the not-operational indication, which is the fault instant when the pin already shows it. Pass when the stop event is no later than 50 ms after the fault instant for every injection, including every injection of (b) and (c), and when the number of injections with the operational indication at the fault instant meets OP-SYS-065 item (e).

items.text: From the release of each reset of the controller, whatever the class that SYS-RST-001 or SYS-RST-002 assigns to that reset, where the release is the instant recorded for that class in OP-SYS-066 item (b), until the earlier of the instant at which the start-up integrity checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 that follow that release have both passed, observed by the means recorded in OP-SYS-066 item (f), and the start of the next reset, the controller shall hold the status signal at the not-operational indication recorded in OP-SYS-066 item (a) at every instant, including the instants before the controller software has configured the GPIO pin of CON-SUP-003 that drives the status signal, observed at that pin.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-017); keeps the rework r1 structure (F-sys-req-item-r1-023). Derived from STK-SUP-007 and STK-SUP-009: the status signal must not show the controller as operational before the application is allowed to run, otherwise a controller that fails its start-up checks would report itself operational for the time before the failed result. (Decisions the author cannot make, F-sys-req-item-r2-017) The finding asks to resolve the not-operational indication, the reset boundaries and the evidence accepted for the interval before software configures the pin. The inputs give no status-signal pin, no indication, no board circuitry, no reset-time pin state and no definition of the release of a reset, and the author cannot approve evidence; stating any of them would invent hardware facts or approvals (hi-core rule 1). That part of the finding therefore cannot be resolved by the author. Each decision this item needs is now a separate lettered entry of blocking open point OP-SYS-066, and the item text cites the entries by letter, so a reviewer's decision completes the item without rewording; the stage cannot be accepted until OP-SYS-066 is decided. OP-SYS-066 refines OP-SYS-030 items (a) to (e) and OP-SYS-031 items (a) to (e) for this item; OP-SYS-030 and OP-SYS-031 are not changed because SYS-SAF-002, SYS-SAF-005, SYS-SAF-006, SYS-MEM-001, SYS-MEM-002 and SYS-WDG-008 also cite them. (Indication) Item (a) asks for the pin and the not-operational indication, and for confirmation that this indication is a static state the pin presents without software, because an indication that needs software (for example a pattern) cannot be held from the release of the reset; if only a pattern is approved, item (a) asks for the approved treatment of the interval before software configures the pin. (Reset boundaries) The start event is the release of every reset, whatever its class under SYS-RST-001 or SYS-RST-002 (power-on reset, watchdog reset, supervisor reset, other reset), because the start-up checks follow every reset. Item (b) asks for the release instant of each class as observable at the board and on the simulator of SYS-TST-001, including the supply level in V for a power-on; it refines OP-SYS-031 item (b) per class (related OP-SYS-026, OP-SYS-027 item f). The end event is both checks passed, observed by the means of item (f) (related OP-SYS-032 item e, OP-SYS-037 item f), or the start of the next reset if a check fails (SYS-MEM-003). The hold during the reset itself is SYS-SAF-006, so the two items together cover every instant from the start of a reset to passed start-up checks. (Before software configures the pin) In that interval the pin state comes from the platform reset state of the pin and the board circuitry, so the item is allocated to hardware as well as software. Item (c) asks for those facts, cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page, and for confirmation that no transient away from the not-operational indication occurs after the release; if a transient cannot be avoided, the approved maximum in ms is recorded there and this item is reworded to state it. Item (d) asks which evidence is accepted for this interval: board and platform analysis, the simulator pin state, or both. (Reset classes covered) Item (e) asks, for each class of SYS-RST-001 and SYS-RST-002 and each cause of other reset confirmed in OP-SYS-026 item (a), whether it can be produced on the simulator and which evidence covers it otherwise. (Stimuli) Both failed start-up checks are now caused under SYS-TST-004, which places the corruption in the memory content before the release; the previous reference to SYS-TST-002 is replaced (OP-SYS-037 item h, for this item). Watchdog resets are caused under SYS-TST-003 and supervisor resets by a task fault of SYS-TST-002 followed by the reset of SYS-REC-001. After the checks pass the item does not require any indication; SYS-REC-003 still requires the hold while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is held, and SYS-SAF-002 relies on this item when a start-up check fails. The verification method stays test pending item (d); if item (d) accepts only analysis for the interval before software configures the pin, the method is changed when OP-SYS-066 is resolved. Test criterion, once OP-SYS-066 is resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with the records of SYS-TST-006, the status-signal pin sampled continuously through each reset and the instant at which each start-up check passes recorded by the means of item (f), for each reset class and cause that item (e) accepts on the simulator, namely power-on reset by applying the simulated supply, watchdog reset caused under SYS-TST-003 once by the independent watchdog and once by the window watchdog, supervisor reset by SYS-REC-001 after a task fault of SYS-TST-002, and each cause of other reset accepted in item (e), run three cases: (1) program code and configuration data intact; (2) a corruption of the set of OP-SYS-037 item (e) placed under SYS-TST-004 in the program code before the release of that reset, so that the check of SYS-MEM-001 fails; (3) a corruption of that set placed under SYS-TST-004 in the configuration data before the release of that reset, with the program code intact, so that the check of SYS-MEM-002 fails. Pass when every sample from the release of item (b) for that class until both checks have passed in case (1), and until the start of the next reset, or the end of the observation window of item (g) when no reset starts, in cases (2) and (3), shows the not-operational indication of item (a). For each class or cause that item (e) does not accept on the simulator, and for the interval before software configures the pin where item (d) requires analysis, the evidence is the analysis of item (d): from the pin reset state cited from RM0486 by section and page and the board circuitry on the status signal, show that the pin presents the not-operational indication from the release until software configures the pin.

items.text: For each reset of the controller, whatever the class that SYS-RST-001 or SYS-RST-002 assigns to that reset, from the instant at which the transition allowance of OP-SYS-069 item (c) has elapsed after the start of that reset until the release of that reset, the start being, for a power-on reset, the instant at which the controller supply reaches the level in V of OP-SYS-069 item (b) and, for every other class or cause, the instant defined for it in OP-SYS-069 item (b), and the release being the instant defined for that class or cause in OP-SYS-069 item (b), the controller shall hold the status signal at the not-operational indication of OP-SYS-069 item (a) at every instant, observed at the GPIO pin of CON-SUP-003 that drives the status signal, the transition allowance being 0 ms when OP-SYS-069 item (c) confirms that no transition time is allowed.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-040). (Decisions the author cannot make) The finding asks to approve the indication, the reset boundaries and any transition allowance. The inputs give no status-signal pin, no indication, no supply threshold, no reset-time pin behaviour and no board circuitry, and hi-core rule 1 forbids the author to invent or approve them, so that part cannot be resolved by the author. Each decision this item needs is now a separate lettered entry of blocking open point OP-SYS-069, and the text cites the entries by letter, so a reviewer's decision completes the item without rewording; the stage cannot be accepted until OP-SYS-069 is decided. OP-SYS-069 refines OP-SYS-030 items (a) to (e) and OP-SYS-031 items (b) to (e) for this item; OP-SYS-030 and OP-SYS-031 are not changed because other items also cite them. (Transition and supply threshold now explicit) The previous text required the indication from the start of the reset with the transition allowance only implied by an open point. The text now states the hold interval from the start plus the transition allowance of item (c), and states the start of a power-on reset as the instant the supply reaches the level of item (b), so both decisions enter the obligation; with no approved allowance the hold starts at the start of the reset (0 ms). (Release) The release is that of OP-SYS-069 item (b), which asks for confirmation that it is the same instant as the release of OP-SYS-066 item (b) used by SYS-SAF-003, so the two items meet without a gap. (Verification of the transition and the full interval) A reset-state pin value alone is no longer the evidence: the criterion below requires, for each reset class and cause, the platform pin behaviour from the start of the reset (item d) and the board circuitry (item e) to show the transition from the worst-case preceding indication (item g) within the allowance and the hold until the release. (Kept from rework r1) Split from SYS-SAF-003 (F-sys-req-item-r1-023). Derived from STK-SUP-007 and STK-SUP-009: while a reset is in progress the application is not running and the start-up checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 have not passed, so the status signal must not show the controller as operational; together with SYS-SAF-003 this covers every instant from the start of a reset to passed start-up checks. No software runs during a reset, so the obligation falls on the platform pin behaviour and the board circuitry, and the item is allocated to hardware. A reset that starts while the status signal shows the operational indication requires a transition, which is why the allowance of OP-SYS-069 item (c) is part of the text. Consistent with SYS-REC-003, which requires the same indication through every reset while latched. Analysis criterion, once OP-SYS-069 is resolved, for each class of SYS-RST-001 and SYS-RST-002 (power-on reset, watchdog reset by the independent watchdog, watchdog reset by the window watchdog, supervisor reset, other reset) and each cause of other reset confirmed in OP-SYS-026 item (a): (1) transition: from the platform behaviour of the status-signal pin from the start of that reset, cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page (OP-SYS-069 item d), and the board circuitry on the status signal (item e), derive the worst-case time from the start of the reset until the pin presents the not-operational indication of item (a), starting from the indication of item (g) for that cause, and show that it does not exceed the allowance of item (c); for a power-on reset, show that the pin presents the not-operational indication from the instant the supply reaches the level of item (b); (2) hold: from the same facts, show that the pin presents the not-operational indication at every instant from the end of the transition until the release of item (b), with no transient away from it. A reset-time pin value without the timing of items (d) and (e) does not meet (1). Supporting test, for each class and cause for which item (f) accepts simulator evidence: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with the records of SYS-TST-006, the status-signal pin sampled continuously, with the pin at the indication of item (g) at the start of the reset by the means of item (g), cause the reset (power-on by applying the simulated supply, watchdog reset under SYS-TST-003 once by the independent watchdog and once by the window watchdog, supervisor reset by SYS-REC-001 after a task fault of SYS-TST-002, and each accepted other-reset cause); pass when every sample from the start of the reset plus the allowance of item (c) until the release of item (b) shows the not-operational indication. The item passes when (1) and (2) hold for every class and cause and every supporting test required by item (f) passes.

items.text: When a watchdog event of SYS-WDG-002, SYS-WDG-003 or SYS-WDG-004 occurs, the controller shall reach, no later than 50 ms after the watchdog-event instant, a state in which every control output listed in OP-SYS-028 is simultaneously in the off state recorded for that output in OP-SYS-028, observed at the GPIO pin of CON-SUP-003 that drives that output, where: that state is reached at the first instant at or after the watchdog-event instant at which every control output is in its off state, which is the watchdog-event instant itself when every control output is already in its off state at that instant; and the watchdog-event instant is: for SYS-WDG-002, the instant at which the time elapsed since the current interval reference instant of SYS-WDG-002 reaches the independent-watchdog timeout of SYS-WDG-002 without a servicing of the independent watchdog, the interval reference instant being, as defined in SYS-WDG-002, the release of the most recent reset of the controller until the first servicing after that release, and from then on the most recent servicing; for SYS-WDG-003, the instant of the service attempt of SYS-WDG-003 made while the time elapsed since the current window reference instant of SYS-WDG-003 is less than the window-opening time, whether or not the window watchdog accepts that attempt; for SYS-WDG-004, the instant at which the time elapsed since the current window reference instant of SYS-WDG-004 reaches the window-closing time of SYS-WDG-004 without a servicing of the window watchdog.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-038); keeps the rework r1 structure (split from SYS-SAF-001, F-sys-req-item-r1-020). (First-interval timeout, F-sys-req-item-r2-038) The previous SYS-WDG-002 event instant counted the timeout from the last servicing of the independent watchdog. SYS-WDG-002 also resets the controller when no servicing has occurred since the release of a reset, so a controller that fails after a reset and before its first servicing had no event instant and the 50 ms of STK-SUP-009 had no start event. The event instant now uses the interval reference instant of SYS-WDG-002: the release of the most recent reset (OP-SYS-031) until the first servicing after it, then the most recent servicing. It is the instant at which SYS-WDG-002 requires the reset, in the first interval and in every later interval. (Rejected early attempt, F-sys-req-item-r2-038) The previous SYS-WDG-003 event instant was the instant at which the window watchdog 'is serviced' before its window opens. SYS-WDG-003 triggers on a service attempt, accepted or not, so an early attempt that the window watchdog rejects caused a reset but had no event instant. The event instant is now the instant of the early service attempt of SYS-WDG-003, whether or not it is accepted, counted against the window reference instant of SYS-WDG-003, so the start-up window is covered too. The trigger no longer says the watchdog 'detects' the event, because a rejected attempt is not a servicing; the events are the trigger conditions of SYS-WDG-002 to SYS-WDG-004. (Window closing) For the same reason the SYS-WDG-004 event instant ('the configured window closes without servicing') had no reference in the start-up window; it is now the instant at which the window-closing time of SYS-WDG-004 is reached from the window reference instant of SYS-WDG-004, the reading proposed in OP-SYS-040 item (e). (Outputs already off) The reached-state rule of SYS-SAF-001 (first instant at or after the event instant, the event instant itself when all outputs are already off) is now stated in the text. After a first-interval timeout or an early attempt in the start-up window no application task may yet have switched an output on, so the measured reaction can be 0 ms, a pass; the precondition 'control outputs initially on' is removed and replaced by a minimum number of injections with an output not off (OP-SYS-067 item e). (Approval requested, F-sys-req-item-r2-038) The finding asks for verification against the approved output-off indication. The inputs give no control-output list, no off state and no approved watchdog-event instants, and hi-core rule 1 forbids the author to approve or invent them, so that part cannot be resolved by the author. The item cites the off states of OP-SYS-028 and states every event instant as the author's proposal; the decisions needed are in blocking open point OP-SYS-067 (refines OP-SYS-028, OP-SYS-029 item e, OP-SYS-038 item f, OP-SYS-039 item f and OP-SYS-040 item e for this item). A decision completes the item without rewording, but the stage cannot be accepted until they are decided. (Kept from rework r1) STK-SUP-009 applies to 'any fault above', and STK-SUP-006 makes a missed independent-watchdog timeout and window-watchdog servicing too early or too late detected watchdog events. STK-SUP-005 makes the hardware reset the reaction to a failure the software does not handle, so no software action before the reset is required: the off state is reached through the watchdog reset, by the reset-time pin state of OP-SYS-028 item (d) or by the restart before the deadline. A watchdog event that follows a fault of SYS-SAF-001 (servicing stopped under SYS-WDG-006) does not relax the SYS-SAF-001 deadline counted from that fault. (Peer alignment not made here) SYS-SAF-005 and SYS-TST-003 still state the SYS-WDG-002 event from the last servicing and the SYS-WDG-003 event as a servicing before the window opens; aligning them is a change to other items, not made in this item rework, and is recorded in OP-SYS-067 item (h). Test criterion, once OP-SYS-028, OP-SYS-031, OP-SYS-038 to OP-SYS-040 and OP-SYS-067 are resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with the records of SYS-TST-006, with reset releases, independent-watchdog servicings, window-watchdog start instants and every window-watchdog service attempt with its acceptance or rejection recorded (OP-SYS-037 item f), the control-output pins sampled continuously, including through the reset and restart, each watchdog event caused by the means of SYS-TST-003 and OP-SYS-067 item (e), and each event instant computed from these records and the configured values as stated in this item, independently of the controller's own reports: (a) first-interval timeout: after a power-on, a watchdog reset and a supervisor reset, prevent every servicing of the independent watchdog from the release onwards, event instant at the release plus the independent-watchdog timeout as decided in OP-SYS-067 item (b); (b) later-interval timeout: let the controller service the independent watchdog at least 2 times, then prevent every further servicing, event instant at the last servicing plus that timeout; (c) early attempt in the start-up window, after a power-on, a watchdog reset and a supervisor reset, and (d) early attempt after at least 2 servicings: make a service attempt at an elapsed time below the lower limit of the window-opening range of OP-SYS-039 item (a), event instant at that attempt; across (c) and (d), make at least one attempt that the window watchdog rejects and at least one that it accepts where the platform behaviour of OP-SYS-039 item (e) allows it, otherwise use the evidence of OP-SYS-067 item (f); (e) late servicing in the start-up window and after at least 2 servicings: prevent every service attempt, event instant at the window reference instant plus the window-closing time. In each of (a) to (e), run at least one injection with at least one control output not in its off state at the event instant, by the means of OP-SYS-067 item (e). For each injection, the stop event is the first sample at or after the event instant at which every control-output pin shows its off state of OP-SYS-028, which is the event instant when all pins already show it. Pass when the stop event is no later than 50 ms after the event instant for every injection, including every first-interval timeout of (a) and every rejected early attempt of (c) and (d), and when the number of injections with an output not off at the event instant meets OP-SYS-067 item (e).

items.text: When a watchdog event of SYS-WDG-002, SYS-WDG-003 or SYS-WDG-004 occurs, the controller shall reach, no later than 50 ms after the watchdog-event instant, a state in which the status signal is at the not-operational indication recorded in OP-SYS-030, observed at the GPIO pin of CON-SUP-003 that drives the status signal, where: that state is reached at the first instant at or after the watchdog-event instant at which that pin shows the not-operational indication, which is the watchdog-event instant itself when the pin already shows it at that instant; and the watchdog-event instant is the one defined for that event in SYS-SAF-004, namely: for SYS-WDG-002, the instant at which the time elapsed since the current interval reference instant of SYS-WDG-002 reaches the independent-watchdog timeout of SYS-WDG-002 without a servicing of the independent watchdog, the interval reference instant being, as defined in SYS-WDG-002, the release of the most recent reset of the controller until the first servicing after that release, and from then on the most recent servicing; for SYS-WDG-003, the instant of the service attempt of SYS-WDG-003 made while the time elapsed since the current window reference instant of SYS-WDG-003 is less than the window-opening time, whether or not the window watchdog accepts that attempt; for SYS-WDG-004, the instant at which the time elapsed since the current window reference instant of SYS-WDG-004 reaches the window-closing time of SYS-WDG-004 without a servicing of the window watchdog.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-039); keeps the rework r1 structure (split from SYS-SAF-002, F-sys-req-item-r1-022). (Shared event definitions, F-sys-req-item-r2-039) The previous item took its start events from the earlier SYS-SAF-004 wording, which counted the SYS-WDG-002 event from the last servicing, giving no origin for a first independent-watchdog timeout after a reset without any servicing, and stated the SYS-WDG-003 event as a servicing before the window opens, excluding an early attempt that the window watchdog rejects although SYS-WDG-003 resets on it. The item now states the watchdog-event instants of SYS-SAF-004 as reworked in r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-038), word for word, so the output switch-off of SYS-SAF-004 and the status indication of this item are measured from one start event per watchdog event: for SYS-WDG-002 the interval reference instant of SYS-WDG-002 (release of the most recent reset, OP-SYS-031, until the first servicing, then the most recent servicing); for SYS-WDG-003 the instant of the early service attempt, accepted or not, counted from the window reference instant of SYS-WDG-003, which covers the start-up window; for SYS-WDG-004 the instant the window-closing time is reached from the window reference instant of SYS-WDG-004. The trigger no longer says a watchdog 'detects' the event, because a rejected attempt is not a servicing; the events are the trigger conditions of SYS-WDG-002 to SYS-WDG-004. This resolves OP-SYS-067 item (h) for SYS-SAF-005; SYS-TST-003 is not changed here. (Indication already shown) The reached-state rule of SYS-SAF-004 is applied to the status signal: in the start-up window SYS-SAF-003 holds the not-operational indication until both start-up checks have passed, so a first-interval timeout or an early attempt before then gives a measured reaction of 0 ms, a pass; the precondition 'status signal initially at the operational indication' is replaced by a minimum number of injections with the operational indication shown at the event instant (OP-SYS-068 item d). (Approval requested, F-sys-req-item-r2-039) The finding asks for verification against the approved not-operational indication. The inputs give no status-signal pin, no indication and no approved event instants, and hi-core rule 1 forbids the author to approve or invent them; the item cites the indication of OP-SYS-030 and the decisions needed are in blocking open point OP-SYS-068 (refines OP-SYS-030 items a to f and OP-SYS-067 items b to d, f and h for this item). A decision completes the item without rewording, but the stage cannot be accepted until they are decided. (Kept from rework r1) STK-SUP-009 applies to 'any fault above' and its safe state includes a status signal showing that the controller is not operational; STK-SUP-006 makes a missed independent-watchdog timeout and window-watchdog servicing too early or too late watchdog events. STK-SUP-005 makes the hardware reset the reaction to a failure the software does not handle, so no software action before the reset is required: the indication is reached through the reset-time state of the status-signal pin (OP-SYS-030 item d, OP-SYS-066 item c) or after the restart, where SYS-SAF-003 holds it until the start-up checks have passed. A later return to the operational indication after passed start-up checks is not a failure of this item. A watchdog event that follows a fault of SYS-SAF-002 (servicing stopped under SYS-WDG-006) does not relax the SYS-SAF-002 deadline counted from that fault. Test criterion, once OP-SYS-030, OP-SYS-031, OP-SYS-038 to OP-SYS-040, OP-SYS-066, OP-SYS-067 and OP-SYS-068 are resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with the records of SYS-TST-006, with reset releases, start-up check-pass instants, independent-watchdog servicings, window-watchdog start instants and every window-watchdog service attempt with its acceptance or rejection recorded (OP-SYS-037 item f), the status-signal pin sampled continuously, including through the reset and restart, each watchdog event caused by the means of SYS-TST-003 and OP-SYS-068 item (d), and each event instant computed from these records and the configured values as stated in this item, independently of the controller's own reports: (a) first-interval timeout: after a power-on, a watchdog reset and a supervisor reset, prevent every servicing of the independent watchdog from the release onwards, event instant at the release plus the independent-watchdog timeout as decided in OP-SYS-067 item (b); (b) later-interval timeout: let the controller service the independent watchdog at least 2 times, then prevent every further servicing, event instant at the last servicing plus that timeout; (c) early attempt in the start-up window, after a power-on, a watchdog reset and a supervisor reset, and (d) early attempt after at least 2 servicings: make a service attempt at an elapsed time below the lower limit of the window-opening range of OP-SYS-039 item (a), event instant at that attempt; across (c) and (d), make at least one attempt that the window watchdog rejects and at least one that it accepts where the platform behaviour of OP-SYS-039 item (e) allows it, otherwise use the evidence of OP-SYS-067 item (f); (e) late servicing in the start-up window and after at least 2 servicings: prevent every service attempt, event instant at the window reference instant plus the window-closing time. In each of (a) to (e), run at least one injection with the status-signal pin at the operational indication at the event instant, by the means of OP-SYS-068 item (d). For each injection, the stop event is the first sample at or after the event instant at which the status-signal pin shows the not-operational indication of OP-SYS-030, which is the event instant when the pin already shows it. Pass when the stop event is no later than 50 ms after the event instant for every injection, including every first-interval timeout of (a) and every rejected early attempt of (c) and (d), and when the number of injections with the operational indication at the event instant meets OP-SYS-068 item (d).

items.text: When a fault specified in SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005 is detected or an integrity check of SYS-MEM-001, SYS-MEM-002 or SYS-MEM-004 fails, and the latch condition of SYS-REC-002 is not met for that fault, the controller shall start its first reset after the fault instant, as a reset that SYS-RST-001 classifies as a supervisor reset or a watchdog reset, no later than the recovery time bound recorded in OP-SYS-056 item (a) after the safe-state entry instant, whether or not the fault report of SYS-DIAG-001 for that fault has been completely transmitted, where: the fault instant is the one defined for that fault in SYS-SAF-001; the safe-state entry instant is the first instant at or after the fault instant at which every control output listed in OP-SYS-028 is in the off state recorded for it in OP-SYS-028 and the status signal is at the not-operational indication recorded in OP-SYS-030, both at the same time and observed at the GPIO pins of CON-SUP-003 that drive them, so that it is the fault instant itself when both are already in those states at the fault instant; the start of a reset is as defined in OP-SYS-031; and a first reset that starts after the fault instant and before the safe-state entry instant meets this obligation.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-008, F-sys-req-item-r2-009); replaces the start event of rework r1 (F-sys-req-item-r1-024). (Start of the recovery clock, F-sys-req-item-r2-008) The previous start event, the later of the output switch-off of SYS-SAF-001 and the status-signal change of SYS-SAF-002, relied on change events. After a failed start-up check SYS-SAF-003 already holds the status signal at the not-operational indication, and the board may hold the control outputs off from the release of the reset (OP-SYS-028 item d), so neither change event need exist. The clock now starts at the safe-state entry instant, defined by the state of both indications and not by their change: the first instant at or after the fault instant of SYS-SAF-001 at which both indications are in their required states at the same time, which is the fault instant itself when both are already in those states. The tester computes it from the fault instant and the continuously recorded pin states of SYS-TST-006. When both indications change after the fault instant and neither leaves its required state in between, it equals the later of the stop events of SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002, so the rework r1 meaning is kept for those cases. SYS-SAF-001, SYS-SAF-002 and SYS-REC-002 describe safe-state entry by the two change events in their rationale or text; aligning them with this instant is a set-level change not made in this item rework, recorded in OP-SYS-056 item (f). (Recovery bound, F-sys-req-item-r2-009) The inputs give no recovery bound and the author cannot approve one (hi-core rule 1), so this part of the finding cannot be resolved by the author. The bound stays a blocking decision, now in OP-SYS-056 item (a), cited by letter so that the decision completes the item without rewording; the stage cannot be accepted until it is decided. OP-SYS-056 item (a) also asks how the bound applies to a failed start-up check, whose fault instant is the release of the preceding reset, so the bound then includes the duration of the start-up checks. (Watchdog reset before safe-state entry, F-sys-req-item-r2-009) The disposition is now stated in the item: the obligation is on the first reset after the fault instant, so a watchdog reset that starts after the fault instant and before the safe-state entry instant is the recovery reset and meets the item when SYS-RST-001 classifies it as a watchdog reset. It does not relax the 50 ms obligations of SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002, which are counted from the fault instant and are then met through the reset state of the pins (OP-SYS-028 item d, OP-SYS-030 item d). Such a reset is possible because SYS-WDG-006 stops watchdog servicing at fault detection (OP-SYS-004). This disposition is the author's proposal; its confirmation is OP-SYS-056 item (c). (Kept from rework r1) Either a supervisor reset or a watchdog reset is a recovery path, since STK-SUP-010 does not name the reset kind and STK-SUP-011 names both causes; power-on and other reset causes (OP-SYS-008) are not. No precedence between the two paths is required. With memory-integrity faults the watchdogs remain serviced (SYS-WDG-005 names task health only), so the design must provide the supervisor reset for them. The bound applies whatever the state of the SYS-DIAG-001 report; a report interrupted by the reset is completed after restart under SYS-DIAG-006 (OP-SYS-016). OP-SYS-056 refines OP-SYS-022 for this item; OP-SYS-022 is not changed because SYS-WDG-006 and other open points also refer to it. (Verification, F-sys-req-item-r2-009) Task faults are caused under SYS-TST-002, start-up memory faults under SYS-TST-004 and run-time memory faults under SYS-TST-005. Test criterion, once OP-SYS-056 is resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001, with supply maintained, no external reset request, the latch condition of SYS-REC-002 not met and the records of SYS-TST-006: (a) task faults: cause each fault of SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005 with the stimuli of SYS-TST-002, with the control outputs on and the status signal at the operational indication, including cases where the fault report is still in transmission; (b) start-up memory faults: place each corruption of SYS-TST-004, in the program code and in the configuration data, before the release of a reset, so that a start-up check fails while the status signal is already held at the not-operational indication under SYS-SAF-003; (c) run-time memory faults: place each corruption of SYS-TST-005 once before the start of a full pass and once after its area was checked in the current pass; (d) watchdog reset before safe-state entry: by the means accepted in OP-SYS-056 item (e), combine a task fault of SYS-TST-002 with an independent-watchdog timeout of SYS-TST-003 whose reset starts after the fault instant and before the safe-state entry instant. For each injection compute the fault instant as defined in SYS-SAF-001 and the safe-state entry instant from the pin records. Pass when the first reset after the fault instant starts no later than the bound of OP-SYS-056 item (a) after the safe-state entry instant and SYS-RST-001 classifies it as a supervisor reset or a watchdog reset, and, in (b), when the safe-state entry instant equals the fault instant wherever both pins already show their required states at that instant.

items.text: When a counted entry occurs that is the last of N consecutive counted entries, where N is the latch threshold recorded in OP-SYS-057 item (a), that are all equivalent to each other and that have no run-clearing event between the first and the last of them, the controller shall hold every control output listed in OP-SYS-028 in the off state recorded for it in OP-SYS-028 and the status signal at the not-operational indication recorded in OP-SYS-030, both observed at the GPIO pins of CON-SUP-003 that drive them, at every instant from the safe-state entry instant of that last counted entry until the power-cycle release condition recorded in OP-SYS-024 item (a) is met, where: a counted entry exists for each interval from the release of a reset to the start of the next reset, both as defined in OP-SYS-031, in which at least one fault specified in SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005 is detected or at least one integrity check of SYS-MEM-001, SYS-MEM-002 or SYS-MEM-004 fails, and for no other interval; the faults of a counted entry are those detected faults and failed checks of its interval whose fault instant, as defined in SYS-SAF-001, is the earliest among them; the safe-state entry instant of a counted entry is the one defined in SYS-REC-001 for those faults, so that for a failed start-up check of SYS-MEM-001 or SYS-MEM-002 it is the release of the preceding reset itself when every control output and the status signal are already in the states named above at that release; two counted entries are equivalent when their faults, each identified by the requirement among SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005, SYS-MEM-001, SYS-MEM-002 and SYS-MEM-004 under which it is detected and by the tasks or memory area named in the affected-entity field of its SYS-DIAG-001 report, form identical sets; a run-clearing event is the start of a reset that SYS-RST-001 classifies as a power-on reset, or the meeting of the power-cycle release condition recorded in OP-SYS-024 item (a); a watchdog event of SYS-WDG-002 to SYS-WDG-004 is neither a counted entry nor a run-clearing event; and consecutive means that no other counted entry lies between any two of them.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-010); replaces the counting definitions of rework r1 (F-sys-req-item-r1-025, F-sys-req-item-r1-026). (What the author cannot approve) The finding asks for approval of the latch threshold, the fault-equivalence rule, the counted entries, the run-clearing events and the release condition. The inputs give none of these as approved values: STK-SUP-010 says only that the same fault repeats a number of times in a row without the number, and that the safe state lasts until a power cycle without defining one. hi-core rule 1 forbids the author to approve or invent them, so approval cannot be given in this rework. To give a test oracle, the item now fixes every rule except two values: each rule that follows from a literal reading of the inputs is stated in the item text as the author's proposal, and each proposal and the two values are listed by letter in blocking open point OP-SYS-057 (refines OP-SYS-023 for this item), so a decision completes the item without rewording. The two values left open are the threshold N (OP-SYS-057 item a) and the power-cycle release condition (OP-SYS-024 item a, restated in OP-SYS-057 item f). OP-SYS-023 and OP-SYS-024 are not changed because SYS-REC-003, SYS-REC-004 and other open points also refer to them. (Counted entries, OP-SYS-057 item d) One counted entry per interval from a reset release to the next reset start in which a fault of SYS-SAF-001 is detected or a check fails. STK-SUP-010 counts repetitions of the sequence 'safe state, then recovery reset', so further detections in the same interval, for example alive faults of more than one task when the scheduler stops, do not add entries or break the run; detections that occur at the same earliest fault instant form one entry with a set of faults. Only faults detected or checks failed in the interval count, so a run-time corruption present but not yet detected when a task fault resets the controller does not become the fault of that entry. (Failed start-up with the safe state already shown, OP-SYS-057 item e) The entry instant is state-based, as in SYS-REC-001: for a failed start-up check of SYS-MEM-001 or SYS-MEM-002 the fault instant is the release of the preceding reset (SYS-SAF-001); SYS-SAF-003 already holds the status signal at the not-operational indication from that release, and the board may hold the control outputs off from it (OP-SYS-028 item d). When both are in their required states at that release, the safe-state entry instant is that release itself, and the counted entry exists even though no output switch-off or status-signal change occurs. Such an entry counts like any other: a corruption that persists over N start-ups therefore latches the controller at the Nth failed check, with the hold starting at that release. (Fault-equivalence, OP-SYS-057 item b) STK-SUP-012 identifies a detected fault by its fault code and the affected task or memory area, so 'the same fault' is read as the same detecting requirement and the same named tasks or memory area. This is independent of the fault-code encoding of OP-SYS-043 item (b); it depends on the affected-entity rule of OP-SYS-043 items (c) and (d) and on the memory areas of OP-SYS-052, OP-SYS-053 and OP-SYS-055. (Run-clearing events, OP-SYS-057 item c) 'In a row' is read as consecutive counted entries: a counted entry with a non-equivalent set of faults ends a run by the definition of consecutive. A reset classified as power-on reset, and the power-cycle release, also end a run, since STK-SUP-010 ends the latch by a power cycle and the inputs give no storage that survives one (OP-SYS-051 item b). No time-based clearing is stated because the inputs give no period of fault-free operation; supervisor, watchdog and other resets do not clear a run. (Watchdog events, OP-SYS-057 item d) A watchdog reset with no detected fault in its interval creates no entry and does not clear the run, so a run is neither counted twice nor broken by the watchdog reset that follows a task fault under SYS-WDG-006; the task fault itself is the entry, its safe-state entry instant being reached through the reset state of the pins (OP-SYS-056 item c). (Retention) The run must survive supervisor, watchdog and other resets; the platform memory for that is not in the inputs (OP-SYS-023 item e, OP-SYS-057 item g). (Kept from rework r1) The hold ends only on the power-cycle release condition, not on a power-on reset classification; continuity of the hold across non-releasing resets is SYS-REC-003; the end of the latch on release is SYS-REC-004. 'The latch condition of SYS-REC-002' used by SYS-REC-001 is the condition stated before 'shall' in this item. Test criterion, once OP-SYS-057 and OP-SYS-024 are resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with the records of SYS-TST-006, starting after a power-on with supply maintained afterwards, determine each counted entry, its faults, its safe-state entry instant and each run-clearing event from the injected stimuli and the pin records, independently of the controller. Cases: (1) N task faults of SYS-TST-002 with identical sets of faults, one per interval; pass when both pins stay in their required states at every sample from the safe-state entry instant of the Nth entry until the release condition is applied, and no application task starts. (2) N-1 such entries; pass when the first reset after the safe-state entry instant of the last entry starts as SYS-REC-001 requires and the application tasks start after the restart that follows it. (3) N entries with one non-equivalent entry, or with a power-on reset, between the first and the last; pass as in (2). (4) N entries of case (1) with watchdog resets of SYS-TST-003 that have no detected fault in their interval between them; pass as in (1). (5) a program-code or configuration-data corruption of SYS-TST-004 placed before the release of a reset and kept over N start-ups, with both pins already in their required states at each release; pass as in (1), the hold starting at the Nth release. (6) N entries alternating between the task fault of case (1) and a corruption of case (5) that is removed before the next release, these being non-equivalent; pass when the first reset after each safe-state entry instant starts as SYS-REC-001 requires.

items.text: When a reset of the controller starts while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is held, whatever the class that SYS-RST-001 or SYS-RST-002 assigns to that reset, the controller shall hold every control output listed in OP-SYS-028 in the off state recorded for that output in OP-SYS-028, observed at the GPIO pin of CON-SUP-003 that drives that output, at every instant from the start of that reset to the earlier of the release of that reset and the instant at which the power-cycle release condition recorded in OP-SYS-024 item (a) is met, where the start and the release of a reset are as defined in OP-SYS-031.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-034); split from the rework r1 item (F-sys-req-item-r1-026). STK-SUP-010 requires the controller to stay in the safe state of STK-SUP-009 until it is power-cycled, so no reset that is not that power cycle may end the safe state, not even for one instant. (Split) The previous item joined two indications and two intervals with different evidence: the interval of the reset itself, in which no software runs and only the platform reset state of the pins and the board circuitry act, and the interval after the release, in which retention of the latch and the controller software also act. It is split by indication and interval: this item keeps the control outputs during the reset (hardware, analysis); SYS-REC-005 keeps the control outputs from the release to the next reset and SYS-REC-006 the status signal over the same interval (software and hardware, test); the status signal during the reset is already required for every reset, whatever its class, by SYS-SAF-006 and is not duplicated here. (Power-cycle boundary) The inputs define no power cycle, and the author cannot approve one (hi-core rule 1), so the release condition stays the blocking decision of OP-SYS-024 item (a). The boundary is now determinate by state and not by reset class: the hold applies to every reset that starts while the latch is held and lasts from its start until its release or, if earlier, until the release condition is met. A reset that reaches its release without the condition having been met is non-releasing whatever its class: supervisor or watchdog reset of SYS-RST-001, other reset of SYS-RST-002 (for example an external reset pin, OP-SYS-026 item a), and a reset classified as power-on reset whose supply interruption does not meet the condition (for example a brown-out). The tester therefore needs no reset classification to judge the item, only the start, release and release-condition instants. Confirmation is OP-SYS-058 item (a); whether the off state is given at the pin while the supply is below its operating range is OP-SYS-058 item (b). (Evidence) No software runs during a reset, so the item is allocated to hardware and verified by analysis for every reset cause, including causes outside simulator coverage: the platform pin reset state cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page and the board circuitry of each control output are board and platform facts not in the inputs, recorded in OP-SYS-058 item (c) (refines OP-SYS-024 item c and OP-SYS-028 item d), not invented here. Analysis criterion, once OP-SYS-024 item (a), OP-SYS-026, OP-SYS-028, OP-SYS-031 and OP-SYS-058 are resolved: for each reset cause confirmed in OP-SYS-026 item (a), whatever its class under OP-SYS-026 item (b), including every cause of the other-reset class of SYS-RST-002 and every supply interruption that does not meet the release condition, show from the cited pin reset state and the board circuitry that each control-output pin presents its off state at every instant from the start of the reset to its release, and for a supply interruption at every supply level from the start of the reset until the earlier of the release and the release-condition instant, or within the transient approved in OP-SYS-058 item (c); pass when this is shown for every such cause and every control output. Where OP-SYS-058 item (e) accepts it, sample the control-output pins continuously on SYS-TST-001 through each modelled cause with the latch held, as supporting evidence only.

items.text: When a reset of the controller that started while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 was held reaches its release, as defined in OP-SYS-031, without the power-cycle release condition recorded in OP-SYS-024 item (a) having been met between the start of that reset and that release, whatever the class that SYS-RST-001 or SYS-RST-002 assigns to that reset, the controller shall hold every control output listed in OP-SYS-028 in the off state recorded for that output in OP-SYS-028, observed at the GPIO pin of CON-SUP-003 that drives that output, at every instant from that release to the earlier of the start of the next reset of the controller and the instant at which that release condition is met, including the instants before the controller software has configured that pin.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-REC-003 (F-sys-req-item-r2-034). STK-SUP-010 keeps the safe state until a power cycle, so after the release of a non-releasing reset the control outputs must stay off and no application behaviour may switch them on. Non-releasing resets while latched: watchdog resets, servicing being stopped under SYS-WDG-006 and SYS-WDG-008 (OP-SYS-041 item c); a supervisor reset, if one occurs; other resets of SYS-RST-002; and power-on-classified resets whose supply interruption does not meet the release condition; the boundary is that of SYS-REC-003, confirmed in OP-SYS-058 item (a). Together with SYS-REC-003 (during the reset) the item covers every instant across every non-releasing reset. The hold after a release needs the latch to survive the reset and the pins to be off before software configures them; both are platform and board facts not in the inputs, recorded in OP-SYS-058 items (c) and (d) (related OP-SYS-057 item g), so the item is allocated to software and hardware. (Evidence outside simulator coverage) Verification is by test; for each confirmed cause the simulator does not model, the test is selected by an analysis that shows, from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) cited by section and page, that the post-release platform state of that cause equals that of a modelled cause; where no such equivalent exists, a target-board test is needed, which conflicts with CON-SUP-005 and is the decision of OP-SYS-058 item (g). Test criterion, once OP-SYS-024 item (a), OP-SYS-026, OP-SYS-028, OP-SYS-031, OP-SYS-057 and OP-SYS-058 are resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with the records of SYS-TST-006, establish the latched safe state as in case (1) of SYS-REC-002; then (a) for each non-releasing reset cause that OP-SYS-058 item (f) accepts as modelled, including each modelled cause of the other-reset class of SYS-RST-002, by the means accepted there, cause at least two successive resets of that cause with the release condition not met, and sample every control-output pin continuously from each release to the start of the next reset; (b) for each cause confirmed in OP-SYS-026 item (a) and not modelled, apply the analysis above and run (a) with the equivalent modelled cause, or the target-board test decided in OP-SYS-058 item (g). Pass when, for every confirmed non-releasing cause, every sample from each release to the start of the next reset shows each control output in its off state, within the measurement resolution of OP-SYS-058 item (h).

items.text: When a reset of the controller that started while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 was held reaches its release, as defined in OP-SYS-031, without the power-cycle release condition recorded in OP-SYS-024 item (a) having been met between the start of that reset and that release, whatever the class that SYS-RST-001 or SYS-RST-002 assigns to that reset, the controller shall hold the status signal at the not-operational indication recorded in OP-SYS-030, observed at the GPIO pin of CON-SUP-003 that drives the status signal, at every instant from that release to the earlier of the start of the next reset of the controller and the instant at which that release condition is met, including the instants before the controller software has configured that pin and the instants after the start-up checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 have passed.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-REC-003 (F-sys-req-item-r2-034). STK-SUP-009 makes the not-operational status signal part of the safe state and STK-SUP-010 keeps the safe state until a power cycle. SYS-SAF-003 holds the indication after every release only until the start-up checks pass; while latched it must also hold after they pass, until the next reset or the release condition, which this item adds. The status signal during the reset itself is SYS-SAF-006, which applies to every reset whatever its class, with analysis evidence for every reset cause of OP-SYS-026; with SYS-REC-003 and SYS-REC-005 for the control outputs, both indications are covered at every instant across every non-releasing reset. Boundary, non-releasing reset causes, retention and pre-software pin state are as in SYS-REC-005 (OP-SYS-058 items a, d; OP-SYS-031 item c for the status-signal pin), so the item is allocated to software and hardware. Evidence outside simulator coverage is selected as in SYS-REC-005 (OP-SYS-058 items f and g). Test criterion, once OP-SYS-024 item (a), OP-SYS-026, OP-SYS-030, OP-SYS-031, OP-SYS-057 and OP-SYS-058 are resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with the records of SYS-TST-006, establish the latched safe state as in case (1) of SYS-REC-002 with program code and configuration data intact, so that the start-up checks pass after each release; then (a) for each non-releasing reset cause that OP-SYS-058 item (f) accepts as modelled, including each modelled cause of the other-reset class of SYS-RST-002, cause at least two successive resets of that cause with the release condition not met, and sample the status-signal pin continuously from each release to the start of the next reset, recording the start-up check completions; (b) for each cause confirmed in OP-SYS-026 item (a) and not modelled, apply the equivalence analysis of SYS-REC-005 and run (a) with the equivalent modelled cause, or the target-board test decided in OP-SYS-058 item (g). Pass when, for every confirmed non-releasing cause, every sample from each release to the start of the next reset, before and after the start-up checks pass, shows the not-operational indication, within the measurement resolution of OP-SYS-058 item (h).

items.text: When the power-cycle release condition recorded in OP-SYS-024 item (a) is met between the start and the release, as defined in OP-SYS-031, of a reset of the controller that started while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 was held, the controller shall end that latched safe state at the release of that reset, called the restart event, so that from the restart event the controller holds the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 again only after a counted entry that is the last of N consecutive equivalent counted entries all lying after the restart event, where N is the latch threshold recorded in OP-SYS-057 item (a) and counted entries, equivalence and consecutive are as defined in SYS-REC-002.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-035); split, the start authorisation after the restart event now being SYS-REC-007. Origin: split from SYS-REC-002 (F-sys-req-item-r1-026). STK-SUP-010 keeps the safe state until the controller 'is power-cycled', so the power cycle ends the latch. (What the author cannot approve) The finding asks to approve the power-cycle signature and the restart event. The inputs define neither, and hi-core rule 1 forbids the author to approve or invent them (a supply level in V, a duration in ms, or a platform reset indication of the STM32N657X0 of CON-SUP-001). They are recorded for decision as blocking open point OP-SYS-059 items (a) and (b), which refines OP-SYS-024 items (a), (b) and (d) for this item; OP-SYS-024 is not changed because SYS-REC-002, SYS-REC-003, SYS-REC-005 and SYS-REC-006 cite its item (a). The item cannot be accepted until they are decided. (Restart event) The item now names the event at which the latch ends: the release (OP-SYS-031) of the reset during which the condition is met, instead of 'the restart that follows'. The pin holds of SYS-REC-002, SYS-REC-003, SYS-REC-005 and SYS-REC-006 already end at the instant the condition is met; this item fixes when the latch itself, its effect on the start-up and on later faults, ends. (Release judged apart from start authorisation) The previous test accepted an eventual application start after passed checks, which neither ties the end of the latch to the restart event nor separates it from the start authorisation of SYS-MEM-003. The end of the latch is now defined by its effect on the run of SYS-REC-002: only counted entries after the restart event can latch again. With N of 2 or more, a failed start-up check at the restart event is the first entry of a new run and gets the recovery reset of SYS-REC-001 instead of the hold, and the hold returns only at the Nth equivalent entry counted from the restart event; this is observed through releases followed by failed integrity checks, cases (2) and (3) below, in which no application task starts. That the restart event authorises no application start on its own, and that a failed check after it still prevents the start, is SYS-REC-007. Confirmation of this meaning, and the case N equal to 1, is OP-SYS-059 item (c) (related OP-SYS-057 items a and c); a direct report of the latch state on the diagnostic line, which the inputs do not require, is OP-SYS-059 item (g). Allocation includes hardware because recognising after the release that the condition was met depends on platform facts (OP-SYS-059 item a). Test criterion, once OP-SYS-024, OP-SYS-031, OP-SYS-056, OP-SYS-057 and OP-SYS-059 are resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with the records of SYS-TST-006, determine the condition instant, the restart event, each reset start and release, each counted entry and each application-task start from the injected stimuli and simulator instrumentation, independently of the controller. In each case latch the controller as in case (5) of SYS-REC-002, with a program-code corruption of SYS-TST-004 kept over N start-ups, then apply the release condition by the means of OP-SYS-059 item (f). (1) Restart with intact memory: remove the corruption before the restart event; pass when both start-up checks after the restart event give a passed result and an application task starts after the restart event and before the start of the next reset. (2) Release followed by failed checks: for each k from 1 to N minus 1, keep the corruption over the k releases counted from and including the restart event and remove it before the next release; pass when, after each of those k releases, no application task starts before the next reset and the first reset after the safe-state entry instant of that failed check starts within the bound that SYS-REC-001 requires, and, after the release that follows the kth, both start-up checks pass and an application task starts before the next reset. (3) Re-latch counted from the restart event: keep the corruption over N releases counted from and including the restart event; pass as in (2) for the first N minus 1 of them and as in case (5) of SYS-REC-002 from the Nth, the hold starting at the Nth release counted from the restart event. (4) Control, non-releasing: from the latched state, remove the corruption and cause a supply interruption that does not meet the condition (OP-SYS-058 item f); pass when no application task starts and the pins show the states of SYS-REC-005 and SYS-REC-006 from its release to the start of the next reset or to the end of the observation interval of OP-SYS-059 item (f). A run fails (1) or (2) if the controller holds the latched safe state after the restart event, and fails (3) if the hold starts before the Nth release counted from the restart event. Cases (1) and (4) differ only in whether the condition is met, so together they show that the end of the latch follows the condition and occurs at the restart event.

items.text: When the restart event of SYS-REC-004 occurs, the controller shall start no application task in the interval from that restart event to the start of the next reset of the controller, as defined in OP-SYS-031, before the start-up program-code integrity check of SYS-MEM-001 and the start-up configuration-data integrity check of SYS-MEM-002 that follow that restart event have both given a passed result, so that no application task starts in that interval when either of these checks gives a failed result.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-REC-004 (F-sys-req-item-r2-035). The finding asks to verify the latch release separately from the authorisation of application start, including a release followed by a failed integrity check. STK-SUP-007 requires the program code and the configuration data to be found intact before the application runs; STK-SUP-010 makes the restart event a start-up after which the latch no longer prevents the application. A release path that recognises the power cycle and ends the latch is a separate path towards application start, so this item requires that it authorises nothing on its own: after the restart event, application tasks start only after both start-up checks have given a passed result, and not at all before the next reset when either check fails. SYS-MEM-003 forbids a task start after a failed check but does not order the start after both passed results; this item states that order for the restart event only, and SYS-MEM-003 is not changed. When a check fails after the restart event, the protection is that of every failed start-up: the status signal at the not-operational indication from the release (SYS-SAF-003), every control output off within 50 ms of the release as fault instant (SYS-SAF-001), and the recovery reset of SYS-REC-001 or, at the Nth equivalent entry, the hold of SYS-REC-002 (SYS-REC-004). Whether the control outputs must instead stay off from the restart event until both checks have passed is not stated in the inputs and is recorded in OP-SYS-059 item (e), not decided here. The observation of passed results and of task starts is recorded in OP-SYS-059 item (d) (author's proposal: instrumentation accepted under OP-SYS-037 item f). Test criterion, once OP-SYS-028, OP-SYS-030, OP-SYS-031, OP-SYS-052, OP-SYS-053, OP-SYS-057 and OP-SYS-059 are resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with the records of SYS-TST-006, latch the controller as in case (5) of SYS-REC-002 and apply the release condition by the means of OP-SYS-059 item (f), with at the restart event (a) a program-code corruption of SYS-TST-004 within OP-SYS-052 items (a) and (b), configuration data intact, (b) a configuration-data corruption within OP-SYS-053 items (a) and (b), program code intact, (c) both corruptions, (d) program code and configuration data intact; record the start-up check results, every application-task start and the control-output and status-signal pins. Pass when, in (a) to (c), no application-task start is recorded from the restart event to the start of the next reset and, as supporting evidence for SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-003 after a release from the latch, the status-signal pin shows the not-operational indication at every sample in that interval and every control output is in its off state of OP-SYS-028 no later than 50 ms after the restart event; and, in (d), the first application-task start after the restart event is recorded after both passed results. A run fails if any application task starts after the restart event before both passed results are recorded.

items.text: After each reset, the controller shall classify the cause of that reset as watchdog reset when the independent watchdog of SYS-WDG-001 or the window watchdog caused that reset, as supervisor reset when the supervisor requested that reset, and as power-on reset when the application of the controller supply caused that reset, where a reset requested by software other than the supervisor is not a supervisor reset, a cause applies to a reset only when it caused that reset and not an earlier reset, and, when more than one of these three causes applies to the same reset, the class assigned is the one that the precedence rule recorded in OP-SYS-061 item (c) gives for that combination of causes.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-012). The finding asks to confirm the cause evidence, the precedence and the observation contract, and to verify supervisor-reset discrimination and every combination that invokes precedence. The cause evidence is a platform fact (the reset indications of RCC on the STM32N657X0, to be cited from CON-SUP-002 RM0486 by section and page) and the precedence and observation contract are stakeholder decisions; none is in the inputs, so the author cannot confirm them (hi-core rule 1). They are recorded, cited by letter so that the decisions complete the item without rewording, in blocking open point OP-SYS-061: item (a) cause evidence, item (b) supervisor-reset evidence and the other software-requested resets, item (c) precedence per combination, item (d) the combinations that can apply to one reset, item (e) observation contract (through OP-SYS-027), item (f) accepted evidence per test case. OP-SYS-061 refines OP-SYS-026 items (a) to (d) and (f) and OP-SYS-027 for this item; neither is changed. The item text now states three points that were implicit: a reset requested by software other than the supervisor is not a supervisor reset, so the discrimination STK-SUP-011 needs is an obligation with a test; only the causes of that reset count, so an indication left from an earlier reset does not change the class; and the class for a combination is the one OP-SYS-061 item (c) gives. Kept from rework r1 (F-sys-req-item-r1-027, F-sys-req-item-r1-028): the item states the class for each of the three causes named by STK-SUP-011; resets to which none of them applies are other reset under SYS-RST-002; the classification is observed on the diagnostic serial line through the reset-cause response of SYS-RST-003.
