Supervisor reset is the reset requested by the supervisor, for example under SYS-REC-001. CON-SUP-003 makes RCC (reset flags) available. Test criterion, once OP-SYS-026, OP-SYS-027 and OP-SYS-061 are resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001, or by the evidence OP-SYS-061 item (f) accepts for a case, with the actual causes of each reset identified from instrumentation independent of the controller and, after each restart, one reset-cause request per SYS-RST-003 completely received after the classification-availability time; cases: (A) single causes: an independent-watchdog timeout (servicing stopped, SYS-WDG-002), early and late window-watchdog servicing (SYS-WDG-003, SYS-WDG-004), each caused under SYS-TST-003, expected watchdog reset; a supervisor reset under SYS-REC-001 with the latch condition of SYS-REC-002 not met after a task fault of SYS-TST-002, after a start-up corruption of SYS-TST-004 and after a run-time corruption of SYS-TST-005, expected supervisor reset; a start from supply off, expected power-on reset; (B) supervisor-reset discrimination: each software-requested reset not requested by the supervisor that OP-SYS-061 item (b) lists, expected the class it is given there and in no case supervisor reset; and an independent-watchdog timeout that starts a reset after a task fault is detected and before the supervisor requests its reset, expected watchdog reset; (C) precedence: each combination of two or more of the three causes that OP-SYS-061 item (d) lists as able to apply to one reset, caused so that every cause of the combination applies to that reset, expected the class OP-SYS-061 item (c) gives; a combination that OP-SYS-061 item (d) records as unable to occur is verified by the analysis cited there, not by test; (D) earlier indications: for each ordered pair of different single causes of (A), the first reset followed by the second, expected for the second reset the class of its own cause. A run passes when every response carries the expected class and fails when a response is missing or carries another class. The list of reset causes and the class of each cause outside the three named classes (for example whether a brown-out counts as power-on) stay in OP-SYS-026 items (a), (b) and (e).

items.text: After each reset to which none of the causes classified by SYS-RST-001 applies, the controller shall classify the cause of that reset as other reset, where a cause applies to a reset only when it caused that reset and not an earlier reset.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-RST-001 (F-sys-req-item-r1-027). STK-SUP-011 applies 'after any reset' but names only three causes, and OP-SYS-008 records that further reset causes may exist; without this item such a reset would have to be forced into watchdog, supervisor or power-on reset, which the inputs do not support. The item is derived: the other-reset class is not named by STK-SUP-011; it is the class that keeps every reset classified without claiming an unsupported cause. Which reset causes fall in this class, confirmation of this class, and its effect on SYS-DIAG-008, SYS-REC-003 and OP-SYS-024 (which refer to the classes of SYS-RST-001) are recorded in blocking open point OP-SYS-026. Observation: through the reset-cause response of SYS-RST-003. Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-036). The finding asks to approve the cause-to-class mapping and the evidence that distinguishes the causes, and to verify each applicable other-reset cause through SYS-RST-003 or by accepted evidence where the simulator cannot reproduce it. The list of reset causes, their mapping to classes and their reset indications are platform, board and stakeholder facts not in the inputs; the author cannot supply or approve them (hi-core rule 1). They are recorded, cited by letter, in blocking open point OP-SYS-062: item (a) applicable causes, item (b) cause-to-class mapping, item (c) distinguishing evidence and combinations with the causes of SYS-RST-001, item (d) accepted evidence per cause. OP-SYS-062 refines OP-SYS-026 items (a), (b) and (f) for this item; OP-SYS-026 is not changed, and its item (e) (effect on SYS-DIAG-008, SYS-REC-003 and OP-SYS-024) still applies. The item text now states, as SYS-RST-001 does, that an indication left from an earlier reset does not make a cause apply. The test criterion no longer limits coverage to the causes the simulator models: every cause assigned to other reset is verified by simulator test or by the evidence OP-SYS-062 item (d) accepts for it, and a cause covered by neither fails the verification. Test criterion, once OP-SYS-026, OP-SYS-027 and OP-SYS-062 are resolved, with the actual cause of each reset identified by the instrumentation independent of the controller of OP-SYS-062 item (d) and, after each restart, one reset-cause request per SYS-RST-003 completely received after the classification-availability time of OP-SYS-027: (A) single causes: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001, each cause that OP-SYS-062 item (b) assigns to other reset and that OP-SYS-062 item (d) records as reproducible there with its reset indication, expected other reset; (B) earlier indications: for each cause of (A), a reset of each single cause of SYS-RST-001 test case (A) followed by a reset of that cause, expected other reset for the second reset; (C) boundary with SYS-RST-001: each combination of a cause of (A) with a cause of SYS-RST-001 that OP-SYS-062 item (c) lists as able to apply to one reset, caused so that both causes apply to that reset, expected the class SYS-RST-001 assigns and not other reset; a combination recorded there as unable to occur is verified by the analysis cited there; (D) causes not reproducible on the simulator: for each cause that OP-SYS-062 item (b) assigns to other reset and item (d) records as not reproducible on the simulator, the evidence OP-SYS-062 item (d) accepts for that cause, with the reset-cause response of SYS-RST-003 as the observed result wherever that evidence includes a reset of the controller. A run passes when every response carries the expected class and every case of (D) gives its expected result; it fails when a response is missing or carries another class, or when a cause that OP-SYS-062 item (b) assigns to other reset is covered by none of (A) and (D).

items.text: When the controller has completely received on the diagnostic serial line a reset-cause request encoded as defined by the service-interface contract of OP-SYS-027, at an instant later than the classification-availability time of OP-SYS-027 counted from the release, as defined in OP-SYS-031, of the most recent reset of the controller that started before that instant, the controller shall complete the transmission on the same line of one reset-cause response to that request, encoded as defined by that contract, that contains the class assigned under SYS-RST-001 or SYS-RST-002 to that most recent reset, within the response time of OP-SYS-027 counted from the complete reception of that request, where: a reset-cause response is completed when the last byte of one response frame of that contract has been transmitted with no reset of the controller between the transmission of its first byte and its last byte, a frame interrupted by a reset not counting as a response; a response is a response to that request when its first byte is transmitted after the complete reception of that request and before the complete reception of any later reset-cause request; and the obligation lapses for that request when a reset of the controller starts after its complete reception, before a reset-cause response to it is completed and before the end of that response time, the outcome for such a request being given by SYS-RST-004.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-037); split, the outcome of a request interrupted by a reset now being SYS-RST-004. The finding notes that a request completely received just before the next reset was eligible for a complete response even when the reset interrupts the transmission, that OP-SYS-027 leaves that outcome undefined, and that the test sent requests only without a further reset. (Eligibility) The window 'earlier than the next reset' is removed: a request is eligible when it is completely received later than the classification-availability time counted from the release (OP-SYS-031, instead of the undefined 'restart') of the most recent reset, and the obligation lapses for that request when a reset starts after its complete reception and before both the completion of a response to it and the end of the response time. A reset that starts after a completed response, or after the response time has ended, does not remove the obligation, so a late or missing response before such a reset still fails. (Completion and attribution) As in SYS-DIAG-001, a response is completed only when its whole frame is transmitted with no reset between its first and last byte, so a frame truncated by a reset is never a response; a response belongs to the request after whose complete reception and before the next request's complete reception its first byte is transmitted. (Outcome of an interrupted request) The interrupted request receives no response after the restart (SYS-RST-004), because a response then would carry the class of the earlier reset while the most recent reset is the interrupting one; the service tool repeats the request after the release and receives the class of the interrupting reset under this item. (What the author cannot approve) The finding asks for the approved observation and timing contract. The inputs contain none and hi-core rule 1 forbids the author to approve or invent one; the eligibility and lapse rule, the outcome of SYS-RST-004, response attribution and truncation recognition, the feasibility of an observation between resets that recur without watchdog servicing (SYS-WDG-008), the absence-observation interval and the means and resolution for placing a reset relative to the request and response bytes are recorded, cited by letter, in blocking open point OP-SYS-063, which refines OP-SYS-027 items (b), (c) and (f) for this item; OP-SYS-027 is not changed because SYS-RST-001 and SYS-RST-002 cite it. Test criterion, once OP-SYS-027, OP-SYS-031 and OP-SYS-063 are resolved and subject to OP-SYS-037 item (c): on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with the records of SYS-TST-006 (every byte on the diagnostic serial line, every reset with its source, its start and its release, determined independently of the controller), decode the byte record into response frames per the contract and discard every frame interrupted by a reset. (a) Nominal: after each reset cause of the tests of SYS-RST-001 and SYS-RST-002, send one valid request completely received after the classification-availability time and cause no reset until the end of the response time; pass when exactly one complete response to it is completed within the response time and carries the class expected for that reset. (b) Reset after a completed response: as (a), then start a supervisor reset of SYS-REC-001 within the measurement resolution of OP-SYS-063 item (f) after the last byte of the response and before the end of the response time; pass when that response carries the class of the reset before the request, not of the following reset. (c) Request received just before a reset: send a valid eligible request and start, by the means of OP-SYS-063 item (f), a supervisor reset of SYS-REC-001 and, in separate runs, a watchdog reset of SYS-WDG-002 or SYS-WDG-004 and a power-on reset, (c1) after the complete reception of the request and before the first byte of a response and (c2) between the first and the last byte of the response; pass when no complete response to that request is recorded before the reset, the truncated frame of (c2) being discarded, and when a new valid request completely received after the classification-availability time counted from the release of the interrupting reset, with no further reset until the end of the response time, receives exactly one complete response within the response time carrying the class SYS-RST-001 or SYS-RST-002 expects for the interrupting reset; the absence of a response after that release before the new request is judged under SYS-RST-004. A run fails when, for a request on which the obligation does not lapse, the response is missing, incomplete, late, duplicated or carries another class. Origin: split from SYS-RST-001 (F-sys-req-item-r1-028). STK-SUP-011 requires the controller to be able to tell the reset cause after restart, and the needs context requires it to tell the outside world what happened. Of the external interfaces in the inputs, the status signal carries only the operational or not-operational indication (STK-SUP-009) and the control outputs carry no information; the diagnostic serial line (STK-SUP-012, STK-SUP-013, CON-SUP-007) is the only interface that can carry the classes of SYS-RST-001 and SYS-RST-002. A service-tool request gives a defined observation point and time after every reset, including power-on and other resets for which no fault report exists (SYS-DIAG-005 covers only watchdog resets). Observation window: from the classification-availability time after the release of a reset; its end is given by the lapse rule of this item. Whether this request is the approved observation point, or a report after restart is required instead or in addition, or the class is carried by the supervision-status response of SYS-DIAG-003, together with the encoding, the classification-availability time, the response time and the controller states in which the item applies, are not in the inputs and are recorded as blocking open point OP-SYS-027 (refines the observability part of OP-SYS-008) rather than invented. Line settings are fixed by SYS-DIAG-002.

items.text: When a reset of the controller starts after the complete reception of a reset-cause request of SYS-RST-003 and before a reset-cause response to that request is completed, the controller shall begin no reset-cause response on the diagnostic serial line at any instant after the release, as defined in OP-SYS-031, of that reset at which no reset-cause request has been completely received since the release of the most recent reset of the controller, where a reset-cause request, a reset-cause response, a response to a request and its completion are as defined in SYS-RST-003.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-RST-003 (F-sys-req-item-r2-037). The finding asks to define the outcome of a request received just before a reset that interrupts its response. SYS-RST-003 makes its obligation lapse for such a request; this item fixes what a tester then observes: no reset-cause response is begun after the release of the interrupting reset, or of any further reset that starts before a new request, until a new request has been completely received after the release of the most recent reset. Without it, a response to the pre-reset request transmitted after the restart would carry the class of the reset before the request while the most recent reset is the interrupting one, so a service tool could read a wrong class for the most recent reset, which defeats STK-SUP-011; and the tester of SYS-RST-003 could not attribute a response after the restart to a request. The item is derived: no need states the outcome of an interrupted request; it follows from making the observation of STK-SUP-011 through the service line of STK-SUP-013 unambiguous across resets. It is an author choice recorded for confirmation in blocking open point OP-SYS-063 item (b), together with the alternative of answering the interrupted request after the restart, and its interaction with any report after restart without a request that OP-SYS-027 item (a) may require (such a report is not a reset-cause response of the request and response contract and is not restricted by this item if a separate frame is decided). Allocation is software: the restriction acts on frames the controller transmits. Test criterion, once OP-SYS-027, OP-SYS-031 and OP-SYS-063 are resolved and subject to OP-SYS-037 item (c): on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with the records of SYS-TST-006, decode the byte record into frames per the contract of OP-SYS-027 and record the first byte of every reset-cause response frame, complete or interrupted. (a) In each run of case (c) of the SYS-RST-003 test criterion (supervisor, watchdog and power-on resets started after the complete reception of the request and before the first byte, and between the first and last byte, of its response), send no request after the release of the interrupting reset for the absence-observation interval of OP-SYS-063 item (e); pass when no reset-cause response frame begins from that release to the end of that interval, and the request then sent is answered as SYS-RST-003 case (c) requires. (b) Chained reset: as (a) with a supervisor reset, then, before any request is sent, start a second reset by a task fault of SYS-TST-002 after that release; pass when no reset-cause response frame begins from the first release to the end of the absence-observation interval counted from the release of the second reset. (c) Control: as SYS-RST-003 case (b), with the reset started after a completed response; this item does not apply, and the run records whether any reset-cause response frame begins after that release without a request, for review against OP-SYS-063 item (b). A run fails when a reset-cause response frame begins in an interval in which this item forbids it.

items.text: When the supervisor detects a fault specified in SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005, or an integrity check of SYS-MEM-001, SYS-MEM-002 or SYS-MEM-004 gives a failed result, the controller shall complete the transmission on the diagnostic serial line of exactly one fault report for that detection no later than the reporting deadline recorded in OP-SYS-044 after the detection instant, whether or not a reset of the controller starts between that detection instant and that completion, where: a detection is a fault of SYS-SUP-001, SYS-SUP-002 or SYS-SUP-003 detected for one supervised task, a program-flow fault detected under SYS-SUP-004, a program-flow fault detected under SYS-SUP-005 for one expected activation instance, or one failed result of one integrity check, each being a separate detection whether or not other detections occur at the same instant; the detection instant is the instant at which the supervisor detects that fault, as in SYS-WDG-006, or at which that integrity check gives its failed result; a fault report is completed when the last byte of one frame of the fault-report contract recorded in OP-SYS-043 has been transmitted with no reset of the controller between the transmission of its first byte and its last byte, a frame interrupted by a reset not counting as a fault report; the fault report contains the fault code that the contract maps to the requirement under which the detection is made, the affected-entity value that the contract maps to the involved tasks or to the memory area, and a time stamp that gives the detection instant in the time reference and resolution of the contract; the involved tasks are, for SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-003, the task for which the fault is detected, for SYS-SUP-004, the task whose execution started and the task of every expected activation instance that precedes it in the configured execution order of SYS-SUP-008 and has not started, and for SYS-SUP-005, the task of the skipped instance; the memory area is the area of OP-SYS-012 or OP-SYS-020 covered by the failed check; and the obligation lapses for a detection when a reset that SYS-RST-001 classifies as a power-on reset starts before its fault report is completed.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-001). STK-SUP-012 requires every detected fault to be reported with a fault code, the affected task or memory area and a time stamp; CON-SUP-007 gives only the line settings. (Why OP-SYS-014 and OP-SYS-016 are not resolved here) The frame encoding, the fault-code and affected-entity values, the time-stamp reference and resolution, and the reporting deadline are not in the inputs; supplying them would invent values (hi-core rule 1, IQ-02). They stay blocking and are refined for this item into OP-SYS-043 (fault-report contract) and OP-SYS-044 (reporting deadline), each listing the individual decisions a reviewer has to make; OP-SYS-014 and OP-SYS-016 remain for SYS-DIAG-005 and SYS-DIAG-006, which are not changed here. (What this rework makes determinate without new values) The finding asks how to verify one complete report per detected fault. The item now fixes: the counting unit, one detection per fault per task for SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-003, one per program-flow fault of SYS-SUP-004, one per skipped instance of SYS-SUP-005 and one per failed check, simultaneous detections counting separately; the meaning of complete, the whole frame with no reset between its first and last byte, so a frame truncated by a reset is not a report and the retransmission of SYS-DIAG-006 is what completes it; the field semantics, the code per detecting requirement, the time stamp as the detection instant (the controller cannot know the fault instant of a run-time corruption, OP-SYS-029 item c), and for multi-task program-flow faults the involved tasks, which for SYS-SUP-004 are the task that started out of order and the tasks of every preceding unstarted instance, so one report names every task whose activation broke the configured order; and the reset case, the deadline counted from the pre-reset detection instant across supervisor and watchdog resets, the obligation lapsing only for a power-on reset, consistent with SYS-DIAG-006 and SYS-DIAG-008, because the inputs give no non-volatile storage. These are author choices not given by the inputs and are recorded for confirmation in OP-SYS-043 items (d) to (f) and OP-SYS-044 items (e) to (g). Watchdog events are reported by SYS-DIAG-005. Test criterion, once OP-SYS-043 and OP-SYS-044 are resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with the records of SYS-TST-006 (every byte on the diagnostic serial line, every reset with its source, every injection) and with detection instants and failed check results made observable as decided in OP-SYS-043 item (h), with a configuration of at least two supervised 10 ms tasks and one supervised 100 ms task of CON-SUP-006, decode the byte record into frames per the contract, discard every frame interrupted by a reset, and judge every detection in the record: (a) inject each fault of SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005 under SYS-TST-002, a start-up corruption of program code and of configuration data under SYS-TST-004 and a run-time corruption under SYS-TST-005, and observe for every detection exactly one complete fault report whose last byte is transmitted no later than the reporting deadline after the detection instant, whose fault code is the code mapped to the detecting requirement, whose affected-entity value is the value mapped to the involved tasks or memory area, and whose time stamp, converted per the contract, equals the detection instant within the contract resolution and the measurement resolution of OP-SYS-043 item (h); (b) multi-task faults: exchange the starts of instances of two different 10 ms tasks in one control cycle (SYS-SUP-004 test b) and observe one report naming both tasks; start the 100 ms instance before a preceding 10 ms instance (SYS-SUP-004 test c) and observe one report naming the 100 ms task and the task of every preceding unstarted instance; suppress one instance of each of two different tasks in one control cycle (SYS-SUP-005) and observe one report per skipped instance, each naming its task; stop the scheduler of CON-SUP-006 (SYS-SUP-001 test c) and observe one report per detection, each alive-fault report naming one task; (c) reports completed after a reset: by the means accepted in OP-SYS-037 item (c), make a supervisor reset of SYS-REC-001 and, in a separate run, a watchdog reset of SYS-WDG-002 or SYS-WDG-004 start (c1) after the detection instant and before the first byte of the report and (c2) after the first byte and before the last byte of the report, and in each case observe after the restart exactly one complete report for that detection, its last byte no later than the reporting deadline counted from the pre-reset detection instant, its time stamp giving that pre-reset detection instant, and in (c2) the truncated frame discarded by the decoder; (d) run every supervised task fault-free with no corruption for at least 10 control cycles of SYS-SUP-004 after the alive-supervision start instant of SYS-SUP-001 and observe no fault report.

items.text: When a reset of the controller is caused by a watchdog event of SYS-WDG-002, SYS-WDG-003 or SYS-WDG-004, the controller shall complete the transmission on the diagnostic serial line of exactly one fault report for that watchdog event no later than the post-restart reporting deadline recorded in OP-SYS-048 after the release of that reset, where: a reset is caused by a watchdog event when it is the first reset of the controller that starts after that watchdog event and it is produced by the independent watchdog of SYS-WDG-001 or by the window watchdog, as in SYS-TST-003; the release of a reset is as defined in OP-SYS-031; the watchdog-event instant is, for SYS-WDG-002, the instant at which the time elapsed since the interval reference instant of SYS-WDG-002 reaches the independent-watchdog timeout, for SYS-WDG-003, the instant of the early service attempt, and for SYS-WDG-004, the instant at which the window-closing time of SYS-WDG-004 is reached; a fault report is completed when the last byte of one frame of the fault-report contract recorded in OP-SYS-043 has been transmitted with no reset of the controller between the transmission of its first byte and its last byte, a frame interrupted by a reset not counting as a fault report; the fault report contains the fault code that the watchdog-report mapping recorded in OP-SYS-047 assigns to the requirement under which the watchdog event occurred, one distinct code for each of SYS-WDG-002, SYS-WDG-003 and SYS-WDG-004, the affected-entity value that this mapping assigns to the watchdog that produced the reset, which is the independent watchdog for SYS-WDG-002 and the window watchdog for SYS-WDG-003 and SYS-WDG-004, and a time stamp that gives the watchdog-event instant in the time reference of OP-SYS-043 within the time-stamp tolerance recorded in OP-SYS-047; and the obligation applies when no further reset of the controller starts between that release and the end of that deadline.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-DIAG-001 (F-029). Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-029). STK-SUP-012 requires every detected fault to be reported with a fault code, the affected task or memory area and a time stamp; STK-SUP-006 makes the independent-watchdog timeout, early window-watchdog servicing and late window-watchdog servicing detected events; each ends in a hardware reset (STK-SUP-005, SYS-WDG-002 to SYS-WDG-004), so the report is required after the restart. (Why the approvals are not made here) The finding asks to approve the report mapping, the pre-reset event evidence and the post-restart deadline. Approval is a human decision; the inputs hold no code values, no affected-entity encoding, no platform fact on which watchdog event the controller can identify after a reset, and no deadline, and supplying them would invent values (hi-core rule 1, IQ-02). They stay blocking and are refined for this item into OP-SYS-047 (watchdog-report mapping, pre-reset evidence, time-stamp tolerance, independent test oracle) and OP-SYS-048 (post-restart deadline and its feasibility); OP-SYS-015 and OP-SYS-016 are not changed, OP-SYS-016 remaining for SYS-DIAG-006. (What this rework makes determinate without new values) Trigger: the actual watchdog event that produced the reset, as defined in SYS-TST-003, not the single watchdog-reset class of SYS-RST-001, so the expected report is fixed by an event a tester observes on the simulator independently of the controller. Event subtypes: one distinct fault code for each of SYS-WDG-002, SYS-WDG-003 and SYS-WDG-004, because STK-SUP-006 names too-early and too-late servicing as distinct detections and SYS-DIAG-001 maps one code per detecting requirement; whether the platform lets the controller tell the three apart after the reset (reset indications of RCC, CON-SUP-003, cited only through CON-SUP-002 RM0486; or pre-reset information held in memory retained across the reset) is a platform fact recorded in OP-SYS-047 item (c), with the scope decision if it cannot. Affected entity: the watchdog that produced the reset, the only entity known for every watchdog event, since a watchdog reset can follow a failure the software does not handle with no task identified (STK-SUP-005). Time stamp: the watchdog-event instant, stated here with the same events as the triggers of SYS-WDG-002 to SYS-WDG-004 and consistent with SYS-SAF-004 as read in OP-SYS-038 item (f), OP-SYS-039 item (f) and OP-SYS-040 item (e); because the actual timeout depends on watchdog clock tolerance, a time-stamp tolerance in ms is required and recorded in OP-SYS-047 item (e). Deadline event: the release of the watchdog reset (OP-SYS-031), the same release used by SYS-WDG-002 and SYS-SAF-003. Completion and count: as in SYS-DIAG-001, exactly one complete frame per watchdog event, a frame truncated by a reset not counting. Further reset before the deadline: excluded from this obligation pending OP-SYS-048 item (d). A watchdog reset that follows a detected task fault (SYS-WDG-006) is reported here in addition to the SYS-DIAG-001 report of that fault (OP-SYS-047 item g). These are author choices not given by the inputs and are recorded for confirmation in OP-SYS-047 and OP-SYS-048. Test criterion, once OP-SYS-031, OP-SYS-043, OP-SYS-047 and OP-SYS-048 are resolved and subject to OP-SYS-037 items (b), (c) and (f): on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with the records of SYS-TST-006 and window-watchdog service attempts instrumented as in the SYS-WDG-003 test, decode the byte record into frames per the contract and discard every frame interrupted by a reset; for each run determine the expected report independently of the controller's reports: the event kind from the stimulus applied under SYS-TST-003 and the reset source identified by the simulator, and the expected watchdog-event instant from the simulator records by the method accepted in OP-SYS-047 item (f). (a) After the task-health condition of SYS-WDG-005 holds, in separate runs cause (a1) an independent-watchdog timeout, (a2) an early window-watchdog service attempt and (a3) a window closing without servicing, and for each observe exactly one complete fault report for that event whose last byte is transmitted no later than the post-restart reporting deadline after the release of the resulting reset, whose fault code is the code mapped to SYS-WDG-002, SYS-WDG-003 and SYS-WDG-004 respectively and differs from the codes of the other two events, whose affected-entity value is the value mapped to the independent watchdog in (a1) and to the window watchdog in (a2) and (a3), and whose time stamp, converted per the contract, differs from the expected watchdog-event instant by no more than the time-stamp tolerance; (b) repeat (a1) to (a3) in the first interval or window after the release of a power-on reset, by the means accepted in OP-SYS-037 item (c), and observe the same outcome; (c) inject a task fault under SYS-TST-002 with the latch condition of SYS-REC-002 not met so that servicing stops under SYS-WDG-006 and a watchdog reset occurs, by the means accepted in OP-SYS-037 item (c), and observe the report of (a1) or (a3) for the watchdog event in addition to the SYS-DIAG-001 report of the task fault; (d) after a supervisor reset of SYS-REC-001 and after a power-on reset, with no watchdog event, observe no fault report carrying any of the three watchdog fault codes.

items.text: When a reset of the controller that SYS-RST-001 classifies as a supervisor reset or a watchdog reset, or that SYS-RST-002 classifies as an other reset, starts after the detection instant of a detection of SYS-DIAG-001 and before the fault report for that detection is completed, the controller shall transmit that fault report on the diagnostic serial line again in full, beginning with its first byte, after the release of that reset and after the release of each further reset of those classes that starts before that fault report is completed, whatever the controller state after that release, until one fault report for that detection is completed, after which no further frame is begun for that detection, where: a detection, its detection instant, a fault report, its completion and a frame interrupted by a reset are as defined in SYS-DIAG-001, and the release of a reset is as defined in OP-SYS-031; every frame transmitted for that detection, before and after any number of interrupting resets, is a frame of the fault-report contract of OP-SYS-043 that carries the fault code, the affected-entity value and the time stamp that SYS-DIAG-001 specifies for that detection, the time stamp giving the detection instant before the first interrupting reset; where two or more detections give frames of identical content, each completed frame with that content counts as the fault report of one of those detections only; the transmission begun after a release is completed no later than the later of the reporting deadline of OP-SYS-044 counted from the detection instant and the post-restart retransmission deadline recorded in OP-SYS-049 counted from that release, when no further reset starts before that instant; the reporting deadline of SYS-DIAG-001 remains counted from the detection instant and is not extended by any number of interrupting resets; and the obligation lapses when a reset that SYS-RST-001 classifies as a power-on reset starts before that fault report is completed.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-DIAG-001 (F-030). Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-030). STK-SUP-012 requires every detected fault to be reported; the supervisor reset of SYS-REC-001 and the watchdog resets of SYS-WDG-002 to SYS-WDG-004 (servicing stopped under SYS-WDG-006, or not yet started under SYS-WDG-008) can interrupt a report or precede its first byte, and SYS-WDG-008 makes repeated watchdog resets possible after a failed start-up check (SYS-MEM-003), while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is held and when task health is not established. The previous wording required transmission after 'the restart' and left open the outcome when the next reset interrupts the retry. (Successive interruptions) The obligation now applies after the release of every interrupting reset of the covered classes, not only the first, and ends only with one completed fault report for that detection or with a power-on reset; it continues after the SYS-DIAG-001 deadline has passed, because a late report still serves STK-SUP-012, while SYS-DIAG-001 is judged failed in that case. Each retransmission is a full frame from its first byte, consistent with SYS-DIAG-001 (a frame interrupted by a reset is not a report) and OP-SYS-044 item (g). Once one frame is completed, no further frame is begun for that detection, so SYS-DIAG-001 'exactly one' holds when a reset follows the last byte closely. (Report identity) The report is identified by the detection it belongs to: every frame for it carries the same fault code, affected-entity value and time stamp as SYS-DIAG-001 specifies, the time stamp giving the pre-reset detection instant, so a tester matches frames before and after any number of resets without a new contract field. Two detections can give identical content, for example two skipped instances of one task in one control cycle under SYS-SUP-005, detected at the same cycle end; the counting rule in the text resolves this by number of frames, not by a detection identifier; whether the contract must carry a detection identifier instead is OP-SYS-049 item (b). (Reset classes) Covered are the supervisor and watchdog resets of SYS-RST-001 and the other resets of SYS-RST-002, matching SYS-DIAG-001, whose obligation lapses only for a power-on reset because the inputs give no non-volatile storage (CON-SUP-003 read as the complete peripheral set, SYS-PLT-002). Watchdog-event reports of SYS-DIAG-005 are not covered here (OP-SYS-048 item d). (Deadline) The SYS-DIAG-001 deadline stays counted from the detection instant and is not extended. After each release, the frame begun is to be completed no later than the later of that deadline and a post-restart retransmission deadline counted from the release, so the item gives a verdict for every restart that is not itself interrupted, including after the SYS-DIAG-001 deadline. (Retention) The behaviour needs, held across every covered reset, for each detection whose report is not completed: its fault code, affected-entity value and detection instant in the time reference of OP-SYS-043 item (f), and whether a frame for it has been completed, kept consistent when a reset occurs during transmission or just after the last byte; capacity for the worst-case number of pending detections (OP-SYS-043 item e). Whether the platform provides memory retained across these resets is a platform fact not in the inputs. (Feasibility) With no servicing after a failed start-up check, while latched or before task health (SYS-WDG-008), watchdog resets recur at intervals bounded below by the lower limits of OP-SYS-038 and OP-SYS-040 from each release; unless pending frames can be completed within that interval the report is never completed. The retransmission deadline, the identity rule, the reset classes, the continuation after the SYS-DIAG-001 deadline, retention and this feasibility relation are not given by the inputs and are recorded for decision in blocking open point OP-SYS-049 (refines OP-SYS-016 for this item; OP-SYS-016 is not changed). Test criterion, once OP-SYS-031, OP-SYS-043, OP-SYS-044 and OP-SYS-049 are resolved and subject to OP-SYS-037 item (c): on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with the records of SYS-TST-006 and detection instants observable as in OP-SYS-043 item (h), decode the byte record into frames per the contract and discard every frame interrupted by a reset; (a) single interruption: for a supervisor reset of SYS-REC-001 and, in a separate run, a watchdog reset of SYS-WDG-002 or SYS-WDG-004, start the reset (a1) after the detection instant and before the first byte and (a2) between the first and last byte of the report, and observe after the restart exactly one complete frame for that detection, with the fault code, affected-entity value and time stamp of SYS-DIAG-001, the time stamp giving the pre-reset detection instant, completed no later than the later of the two deadlines; (b) successive interruptions: interrupt the first frame, then interrupt the frame retransmitted after the first restart by a reset of the other covered class, then start a third reset after the second restart and before the first byte, and observe after the last restart exactly one complete frame with unchanged content, completed no later than the later of the reporting deadline from the detection instant and the retransmission deadline from the last release; (c) reset after completion: start a supervisor reset within the measurement resolution of OP-SYS-049 item (i) after the last byte of a complete frame and observe no further complete frame for that detection after the restart; (d) identical content: interrupt the reports of two detections whose frames have identical content and observe exactly two complete frames with that content after the restart; (e) repeated resets without servicing: after a start-up corruption under SYS-TST-004 whose report is interrupted, observe the outcome decided in OP-SYS-049 item (e); (f) each other reset cause of SYS-RST-002 that OP-SYS-026 confirms and the simulator models, as in (a2).

items.text: The controller shall operate the diagnostic serial line at 115200 baud with 8 data bits, no parity and 1 stop bit.

When the controller has received on the diagnostic serial line a supervision-status request encoded as defined by the service-interface contract of OP-SYS-017, and no reset of the controller occurs between the complete reception of that request and the end of the response time of OP-SYS-017, the controller shall complete the transmission on the same line of one supervision-status response that contains the status fields required by that contract, with values sampled at the instant defined by that contract, within the response time of OP-SYS-017 counted from the complete reception of the request.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-002). (1) Request received shortly before a reset: the obligation is now bounded to requests for which no reset occurs between complete reception and the end of the response time, so a test that observes a reset in that interval is outside this item and cannot be misjudged as pass or fail. The inputs (STK-SUP-010, STK-SUP-011, STK-SUP-013) do not state the expected outcome when a reset (supervisor recovery reset of SYS-REC-001, watchdog reset of SYS-WDG-002 to SYS-WDG-004, or other reset of SYS-RST-001) falls in that interval: no response, a truncated response recognisable under OP-SYS-017 item (b), or a response after restart. That outcome is recorded as blocking open point OP-SYS-045 rather than invented. (2) Approval of the status interface and timing: the author cannot approve OP-SYS-017. Approval is a human decision and the inputs hold no contract, field list, sampling instant or response time (hi-core rule 1), so this part of the finding is not resolved by rework; the item stays blocked by OP-SYS-017 and OP-SYS-045 until a human decides them. Once decided, the test criterion below is complete. Rework r1 (F-032):the valid request, the response encoding, the required status fields, the sampling instant that makes the reported status 'current', and the response-time criterion are bound to one service-interface contract. No such contract or value exists in the inputs, so it is recorded as blocking open point OP-SYS-017 rather than invented. The test criterion is: for a request valid per the contract, one response is completely transmitted within the response time, carries every required field, and each field equals the supervision state at the defined sampling instant. Line settings are fixed by SYS-DIAG-002; malformed or unknown requests are covered by OP-SYS-013.

items.text: When the controller has received on the diagnostic serial line a fault-record request encoded as defined by the fault-history contract of OP-SYS-046, and no reset of the controller occurs between the snapshot instant of that request and the end of the response time of OP-SYS-046, the controller shall complete the transmission on the same line of one fault-record response, encoded as defined by that contract, that contains exactly the K fault reports of the fault history at the snapshot instant whose last bytes were transmitted latest, in the report order defined by that contract, within the response time of OP-SYS-046 counted from the snapshot instant, where: the snapshot instant is the instant at which the last byte of that request has been received on the diagnostic serial line, and it is the one instant at which both K and the identity of the fault reports in the response are determined; the fault history at the snapshot instant consists of every fault report transmitted under SYS-DIAG-001, SYS-DIAG-005 or SYS-DIAG-006 whose last byte was transmitted on the diagnostic serial line after the start of the most recent reset that SYS-RST-001 classifies as a power-on reset and at or before the snapshot instant, each fault report counting once, at the transmission of the last byte of its complete frame, a frame interrupted by a reset not counting; K is the lesser of the retained-fault count of OP-SYS-046 and the number of fault reports in that fault history; and a fault report whose last byte is transmitted after the snapshot instant is not part of that response, even when it is recorded under SYS-DIAG-007 or transmitted before the response is completed.
items.rationale: STK-SUP-013 'read the last faults'. Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-003). (Approval of the history contract) The author cannot approve OP-SYS-018: the inputs hold no request or response encoding, no retained-fault count and no response time, and supplying them would invent values (hi-core rule 1). They stay open and are refined for this item into blocking open point OP-SYS-046 (fault-history contract), which lists each decision a reviewer has to make; OP-SYS-018 remains for SYS-DIAG-007 and SYS-DIAG-008, which are not changed here. This part of the finding is resolved only by a human decision on OP-SYS-046. (Snapshot instant, resolved here without new values) The previous wording counted reports at complete reception of the request but did not say which reports belong to the response when a report is recorded while the response is being prepared. The item now defines one snapshot instant, the reception of the last byte of the request, at which both K and the identity of the reports are fixed. Membership is decided by an event on the diagnostic serial line, the transmission of the last byte of a complete fault-report frame at or before the snapshot instant, and not by the internal recording instant of SYS-DIAG-007, which SYS-DIAG-007 bounds only from above (no later than completion of transmission); so a tester decides membership from the byte record of the line alone, with requests and reports on one time base. A report recorded or transmitted after the snapshot instant, including during response preparation or transmission, is excluded from that response and appears in the response to a later request. SYS-DIAG-007 requires each report to be recorded no later than the completion of its transmission, so every report in the history at the snapshot instant has been recorded by that instant. A report interrupted by a reset and completed after the restart under SYS-DIAG-006 counts once, at its complete frame, consistent with SYS-DIAG-001. 'Most recent' is ordered by the transmission instant of the last byte. (Reset during handling) A fault detected during handling leads to a supervisor or watchdog reset (SYS-REC-001, SYS-WDG-006) that can interrupt the response; the inputs do not state the outcome, so, as in SYS-DIAG-003, the obligation is bounded to requests with no reset between the snapshot instant and the end of the response time, and the outcome of that case is recorded in OP-SYS-046 item (g). These choices are not given by the inputs and are recorded for confirmation in OP-SYS-046 items (e) to (h). Test criterion, once OP-SYS-046 is resolved: on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with the records of SYS-TST-006 (every byte received and transmitted on the diagnostic serial line, every reset with its source, every injection), decode the byte record per the contracts of OP-SYS-043, OP-SYS-014 and OP-SYS-046, discard every frame interrupted by a reset, and for each request compute the snapshot instant and the fault history at it, then (a) empty history: after a power-on reset with no fault injected, send a request and observe one complete response with zero reports within the response time; (b) partial history: produce, by faults injected under SYS-TST-002 that do not meet the latch condition of SYS-REC-002, a number of fault reports at least 1 and below the retained-fault count, and observe a response holding exactly those reports in the contract order; (c) full history: produce the retained-fault count plus at least 2 fault reports across supervisor and watchdog resets, and observe a response holding exactly the retained-fault count of reports, the ones whose last bytes were transmitted latest; (d) report during handling: after a watchdog reset, send a request whose snapshot instant lies after the restart and before the last byte of the fault report of SYS-DIAG-005 for that reset (and, in a separate run, of a report retransmitted under SYS-DIAG-006), observe that this report is not in the response and that the response is otherwise as in (b) or (c), then send a second request after that report is complete and observe the report in the second response; (e) boundary: send a request whose snapshot instant follows the last byte of a fault report by no more than the measurement resolution of OP-SYS-046 item (h) and judge per that item; (f) in (a) to (e), observe the last byte of the response no later than the response time after the snapshot instant. Line settings are fixed by SYS-DIAG-002; malformed requests are covered by OP-SYS-013. Rework r1 (F-033): 'up to' was replaced by an exact count K; recording is defined by SYS-DIAG-007 and retention across resets by SYS-DIAG-008 (split from this item).

items.text: When a fault report for a detection of SYS-DIAG-001 or for a watchdog event of SYS-DIAG-005 is completed, the controller shall record that fault report as exactly one entry of the fault history read by SYS-DIAG-004, present in that fault history from the completion of that fault report onward, where: a fault report, its completion and a frame interrupted by a reset are as defined in SYS-DIAG-001 and SYS-DIAG-005; the completion of that fault report is the one event that commits its entry, so no entry exists for that detection or watchdog event before that completion, and neither the start of a frame, nor the transmission of any byte before the last byte of a frame, nor a frame interrupted by a reset commits an entry; every frame transmitted for one detection under SYS-DIAG-006, before and after any number of interrupting resets, shares the one entry committed at the completion of the one fault report for that detection, and no retransmission adds a further entry; the entry carries the fault code, the affected-entity value and the time stamp of the completed frame; where two or more detections give completed frames of identical content, the fault history holds one entry per completed frame, as counted in SYS-DIAG-006; and an entry committed before a reset that SYS-RST-001 does not classify as a power-on reset remains in the fault history after that reset, including a reset that starts at any instant after that completion, as retained under SYS-DIAG-008.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-DIAG-004 (F-033). Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-031). STK-SUP-013 'the last faults' requires the reported faults of STK-SUP-012 to be recorded for reading. (Commit event) The previous wording allowed recording at any instant up to completion of transmission, so an entry could be made when a frame started, the frame then be interrupted by a reset and the report be retransmitted under SYS-DIAG-006, giving one or two entries for one detection depending on implementation. The item now names one commit event, the completion of the fault report as defined in SYS-DIAG-001 (last byte of one contract frame transmitted with no reset between its first and last byte), which is the same line event by which SYS-DIAG-004 decides membership of the fault history at the snapshot instant; recording before completion is no longer permitted, so the internal record and the line record agree at every instant. (Retries) Since SYS-DIAG-006 completes exactly one fault report per detection and begins no further frame after it, and an interrupted frame commits nothing, all frames for one detection share the single entry committed at that completion and a retry never adds a second entry; detections of identical content are counted by completed frames, as in SYS-DIAG-006. (Reset at the commit boundary) A reset that starts just after the last byte stops further frames for that detection under SYS-DIAG-006, so the committed entry must survive that reset, otherwise the history would lose a report that was completed on the line; retention of the K most recent entries is SYS-DIAG-008. This resolves OP-SYS-018 item (e) as an author choice not given by the inputs; it is recorded for confirmation, with the platform facts the commit at the completion instant depends on, in blocking open point OP-SYS-050 (OP-SYS-018 is not changed). Test criterion, once OP-SYS-043, OP-SYS-046, OP-SYS-049 and OP-SYS-050 are resolved and subject to OP-SYS-037 item (c): on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with the records of SYS-TST-006, decode the byte record into frames per the contract of OP-SYS-043, discard every frame interrupted by a reset, and read the fault history with requests of SYS-DIAG-004 whose snapshot instants are chosen relative to the frames, judging boundary cases with the measurement resolution of OP-SYS-046 item (h); for every response count the entries per detection: (a) uninterrupted report: inject one fault under SYS-TST-002 with the latch condition of SYS-REC-002 not met and observe no entry for that detection in responses with snapshot instants before the first byte and between the first and last byte of its frame, and exactly one entry, with the fault code, affected-entity value and time stamp of the frame, in a response with snapshot instant after its last byte; (b) interrupted transmission and completed retry: for a supervisor reset of SYS-REC-001 and, in a separate run, a watchdog reset of SYS-WDG-002 or SYS-WDG-004, start the reset between the first and last byte of the frame, send a request with snapshot instant after the restart and before the first byte of the retransmitted frame and observe no entry for that detection, then send a request after the last byte of the retransmitted frame and observe exactly one entry for that detection, its time stamp giving the pre-reset detection instant; (c) as (b) with the reset started after the detection instant and before the first byte; (d) successive interruptions: interrupt the first frame and the frame retransmitted after the first restart, and after the completed retry observe exactly one entry for that detection; (e) reset after completion: start a supervisor reset within the measurement resolution of OP-SYS-049 item (i) after the last byte of a complete frame and observe after the restart exactly one entry for that detection and no further frame; (f) identical content: interrupt the reports of two detections whose frames have identical content and, after both are completed, observe exactly two entries with that content; (g) watchdog event: for each event of SYS-DIAG-005 test (a), observe no entry for that event before the last byte of its report and exactly one entry after it; (h) in every response of (a) to (g), observe that the number of entries for each detection or watchdog event equals the number of its completed frames in the decoded byte record, that is 0 or 1.

items.text: When a reset of the controller that SYS-RST-001 classifies as a supervisor reset or a watchdog reset starts, the controller shall store across that reset each fault-history entry of the retained set of that reset, so that from the release of that reset each entry of that retained set is available to the fault-record responses of SYS-DIAG-004 with the fault code, the affected-entity value and the time stamp of its completed frame unchanged and in the same recency order relative to the other entries of that retained set as at the start of that reset, where: a fault report, its completion and a frame interrupted by a reset are as defined in SYS-DIAG-001 and SYS-DIAG-005; a fault-history entry is the entry that SYS-DIAG-007 commits at the completion of one fault report; the recency order is the order of the transmission instants of the last bytes of the completed frames on the diagnostic serial line, as in SYS-DIAG-004; the retained set of a reset is the R fault reports of the fault history of SYS-DIAG-004 whose last bytes were transmitted latest at or before the start of that reset, or every fault report of that fault history when it holds fewer than R, a frame interrupted by that reset contributing no entry and two completed frames of identical content counting as two entries as in SYS-DIAG-007; R is the retained-fault count of OP-SYS-046 item (c), the one retained depth for both reset classes of this item as recorded for approval in OP-SYS-051 item (a); the start and the release of a reset are as defined in OP-SYS-031; and the obligation applies to each reset of these classes whatever the controller state at its start, including each of any number of successive resets of these classes with no reset that SYS-RST-001 classifies as a power-on reset between them.
items.rationale: Rework r2 (F-sys-req-item-r2-032). Split: this item keeps retention across the supervisor and watchdog resets of SYS-RST-001; retention across the other-reset class of SYS-RST-002 is split into SYS-DIAG-009, because the causes in that class are not yet confirmed (OP-SYS-026) and its verdict depends on platform evidence that is separate for each cause. Origin: split from SYS-DIAG-004 (F-033). Every detected fault leads to a supervisor reset (SYS-REC-001, STK-SUP-010) or, with servicing stopped (SYS-WDG-006, SYS-WDG-008), a watchdog reset (STK-SUP-005); without retention across these resets the service tool of STK-SUP-013 could not read the faults that caused them, and SYS-DIAG-004 already counts its fault history from the most recent power-on reset across all other resets, so this item states the retention that SYS-DIAG-004 and SYS-DIAG-007 rely on. (Why the approvals are not made here) The finding asks to approve the retained depth and the retention boundary by reset class and to confirm the platform evidence. Approval is a human decision; the inputs hold no retained count, no list of reset causes with their classes and no platform fact on memory preserved across any reset of the STM32N657X0 (CON-SUP-001; to be cited from CON-SUP-002 RM0486 by section and page), and supplying them would invent values or hardware facts (hi-core rule 1, IQ-02). They are recorded for decision in blocking open point OP-SYS-051 (refines the retention parts of OP-SYS-018 items c and f, OP-SYS-016 and OP-SYS-026 item e for SYS-DIAG-008 and SYS-DIAG-009; those are not changed). (What this rework makes determinate without new values) Retention boundary by class: this item covers exactly the supervisor-reset and watchdog-reset classes of SYS-RST-001, whose causes are the supervisor request and the independent or window watchdog, both produced by the system itself; power-on resets are outside it, consistent with the lapse at a power-on reset in SYS-DIAG-001 and SYS-DIAG-006 and with the history boundary of SYS-DIAG-004 (the inputs give no non-volatile storage: CON-SUP-003 read as the complete peripheral set, SYS-PLT-002); the other-reset class is SYS-DIAG-009. Retained depth: one value R, the retained-fault count that SYS-DIAG-004 already uses for K (OP-SYS-046 item c), so the depth stored equals the depth read and no second value is introduced; a different depth per class would contradict SYS-DIAG-004 and is listed as a consequence in OP-SYS-051 item (a). Retained set: fixed by line events only, the R completed frames whose last bytes precede the start of the reset, so a tester computes it from the byte record of SYS-TST-006 without controller instrumentation; a frame truncated by the reset contributes nothing (SYS-DIAG-001, SYS-DIAG-007) and its detection is completed later under SYS-DIAG-006. Identity and recency: each retained entry keeps the fault code, affected-entity value and time stamp of its frame (the time stamp in the reference of OP-SYS-043 item f, which spans resets) and its order relative to the other retained entries, so identity and recency are both judged against the pre-reset byte record. Successive resets and states: the obligation holds at every covered reset, including repeated watchdog resets after a failed start-up check (SYS-MEM-003), before task health (SYS-WDG-008) and while latched (SYS-REC-002). Not decided here and recorded in OP-SYS-051: the platform memory and its capacity (item c), consistency when a reset starts during a commit or an update of the stored data and protection against corruption (item d), and the evidence accepted for retention on the simulator (item e). Test criterion, once OP-SYS-026, OP-SYS-031, OP-SYS-043, OP-SYS-046, OP-SYS-050 and OP-SYS-051 are resolved and subject to OP-SYS-037 item (c): on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with the records of SYS-TST-006, decode the byte record into frames per OP-SYS-043, discard every frame interrupted by a reset, compute for each reset its retained set from the decoded frames independently of the controller, and read the history with requests of SYS-DIAG-004 whose snapshot instants follow the release; perform each case for a supervisor reset of SYS-REC-001, a watchdog reset of SYS-WDG-002 and a watchdog reset of SYS-WDG-004, with faults injected under SYS-TST-002 that do not meet the latch condition of SYS-REC-002: (a) depth and identity: produce at least R plus 2 completed fault reports, including two of identical content, start the reset and observe a response holding exactly the R entries of the retained set, each with the fault code, affected-entity value and time stamp of its pre-reset frame, in the pre-reset recency order; (b) fewer than R: produce at least 1 and fewer than R completed reports and observe every one of them in the response after the reset; (c) recency after the reset: after (a), complete one further fault report and observe it as the most recent entry followed by the R minus 1 latest entries of the retained set in unchanged order; (d) reset instants: start the reset (d1) within the measurement resolution of OP-SYS-049 item (i) after the last byte of a completed frame and observe that report in the retained set, (d2) between the first and last byte of a frame and observe the retained set without that frame, and (d3) during the transmission of a fault-record response and observe the retained set unchanged; (e) successive resets: start at least 3 successive covered resets of mixed classes with no power-on reset between them, including watchdog resets after a start-up corruption under SYS-TST-004, and observe after the last release every entry of the retained set of the first reset together with the reports completed between the resets, in recency order, up to R entries.

items.text: When a reset of the controller that SYS-RST-002 classifies as an other reset starts, the controller shall store across that reset each fault-history entry of the retained set of that reset, so that from the release of that reset each entry of that retained set is available to the fault-record responses of SYS-DIAG-004 with the fault code, the affected-entity value and the time stamp of its completed frame unchanged and in the same recency order relative to the other entries of that retained set as at the start of that reset, where: a fault-history entry, the recency order, the retained set of a reset, R, and the start and the release of a reset are as defined in SYS-DIAG-008; the reset causes in this class are those that OP-SYS-026 item (b) confirms as other resets; and the obligation applies to each such reset whatever the controller state at its start, including one that precedes or follows resets covered by SYS-DIAG-008 with no reset that SYS-RST-001 classifies as a power-on reset between them.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-DIAG-008 (F-sys-req-item-r2-032). STK-SUP-013 requires the last faults to be readable; SYS-DIAG-004 counts the fault history from the most recent power-on reset of SYS-RST-001, and SYS-DIAG-001, SYS-DIAG-006 and SYS-DIAG-007 lapse only at a power-on reset, so a reset that SYS-RST-002 classifies as other reset (STK-SUP-011 names three causes; every other cause is classified by SYS-RST-002) lies inside the history, and the entries before it must still be readable after it. The obligation is the same as in SYS-DIAG-008 and reuses its definitions, so identity, recency and depth are judged in the same way. It is stated separately because the inputs do not list the causes in this class (for example external reset pin, brown-out or supply-monitor reset, software reset not requested by the supervisor, debug or lockup reset; OP-SYS-026 items a and b), the class of a brown-out or supply-monitor reset is open (power-on or other), and whether platform memory is preserved across each such cause is a platform fact not in the inputs; so this item has its own verdict per confirmed cause, and its scope follows the confirmed classification rather than an author assumption. If platform evidence shows that a cause in this class does not preserve the memory, the decision between reclassifying that cause, an approved exclusion with the matching change to the history boundary of SYS-DIAG-004 and SYS-DIAG-007, or another approved means is recorded in OP-SYS-051 items (b) and (c), not made here. These choices are not given by the inputs and are recorded for decision in blocking open point OP-SYS-051. Test criterion, once OP-SYS-026, OP-SYS-031, OP-SYS-043, OP-SYS-046, OP-SYS-050 and OP-SYS-051 are resolved and subject to OP-SYS-037 item (c): on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 with the records of SYS-TST-006 and the oracle and request method of the SYS-DIAG-008 test, for each reset cause that OP-SYS-026 item (b) confirms as other reset and that the simulator models with its reset indication per OP-SYS-026 item (f) and OP-SYS-051 item (e), or by the other evidence accepted there, perform cases (a), (c), (d1), (d2) and (e) of the SYS-DIAG-008 test with that cause in place of the supervisor or watchdog reset, case (e) mixing that cause with a supervisor reset of SYS-REC-001 and a watchdog reset of SYS-WDG-002, and observe the outcomes stated there.

items.text: While the controller is in normal operation, which begins at the start of the first application task after a start-up in which the integrity checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 have passed and ends at the next reset or at the first detection of a fault specified in SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005 or failure of an integrity check of SYS-MEM-004, whichever occurs first, and while the application tasks of CON-SUP-006 and the diagnostic serial line operate within the reference workload of OP-SYS-060, the supervisor shall use, in every measurement window that lies entirely within that normal operation and has the window length of OP-SYS-060 measured on the processor core clock, at most 10 % of the processor core clock cycles of that window, under every sequence of application-task executions and diagnostic-line traffic that the reference workload permits, where a core clock cycle counts as supervisor use when the processor core executes software that implements a system requirement of this set allocated to software, including entry to and exit from the interrupt handlers of that software, or waits for completion of a peripheral operation started by that software.
items.rationale: Rework r2. (F-sys-req-item-r2-011, workload, window and target cycle evidence) The verdict now rests on justified upper bounds, not on observed runs: runs on the Renode simulator of SYS-TST-001 and host unit tests (CON-SUP-005) show only the paths and arrival patterns they exercise, and the inputs do not establish that the simulator reports target core clock cycles, so they cannot establish worst-case cycle counts. The reference workload, the window length, the core clock frequency, the accepted method for target cycle bounds and the platform timing facts it needs are not given by the inputs and the author cannot approve them; they are recorded for a reviewer in blocking open point OP-SYS-060, which refines OP-SYS-025 items (b), (c), (d) and (f) for this item (OP-SYS-025 is not changed; its items (a) and (e) still hold the confirmation of normal operation and of the counted activities). The text now names OP-SYS-060 and requires the limit under every sequence that the reference workload permits, so a result for one observed sequence does not meet it. Analysis criterion, once OP-SYS-025 items (a) and (e) and OP-SYS-060 are resolved: (1) Execution-count bounds. For each supervisor activity and each interrupt source whose handler is supervisor software, an upper bound on the number of executions that start or run in a window of the approved length, at any window position, is derived from its trigger: the 10 ms and 100 ms task periods of CON-SUP-006 and the supervised-task configuration limits of SYS-SUP-006 to SYS-SUP-008 in the reference workload, the pass schedule of SYS-MEM-004, the approved arrival bound for service-tool requests and, for diagnostic-line reception, the line rate of CON-SUP-007 (115200 baud with 10 bit per character, that is 8 data bits plus start and stop bit, admits at most 11520 characters per s); an execution that overlaps a window boundary counts as a whole execution in that window; each bound states its derivation and its assumptions. (2) Cycle-cost bounds. For each activity and interrupt source, an upper bound on the core clock cycles of one execution is established for the supervisor binary built for the target by the method approved in OP-SYS-060 item (d), over every feasible path and not only the paths executed in tests, with each loop bounded by a stated iteration limit justified under OP-SYS-060 item (f), and including interrupt entry and exit, the memory and bus timing of the target configuration and each wait for completion of a peripheral operation started by supervisor software, bounded by the worst-case completion time of that operation under OP-SYS-060 item (e); an activity whose cost depends on the configuration or on request content is bounded for the largest case the reference workload permits. (3) Sum. The sum over activities and interrupt sources of execution-count bound times cycle-cost bound is at most 10 % of the window length times the approved core clock frequency. (4) Supporting evidence only. Renode runs of the target binary on SYS-TST-001 and host unit tests (gcc, gcovr) may show that the analysed paths exist and that no observed execution exceeds its bound of (2); they do not replace (1) to (3). Kept from rework r1: (F-sys-req-item-r1-034, modes and workload) STK-SUP-014 applies the 10 % limit 'in normal operation' only. Normal operation is bounded by observable events: it begins when the first application task starts after start-up checks that passed, so the start-up integrity checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 and the reset-cause classification of SYS-RST-001 are outside it; it ends at a reset or at the first detected fault, so the safe-state reaction of SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002, fault reporting of SYS-DIAG-001, SYS-DIAG-005 and SYS-DIAG-006, recovery and the latched safe state of SYS-REC-001 to SYS-REC-004 are outside it. Inside it are task supervision of SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005, watchdog servicing of SYS-WDG-005, the background program-code check of SYS-MEM-004 and SYS-MEM-006 (STK-SUP-008 places it in operation) and service-tool request handling of SYS-DIAG-003 and SYS-DIAG-004. (F-sys-req-item-r1-035, measurement) Time reference: the processor core clock of the STM32N657X0 (CON-SUP-001). Denominator: all core clock cycles of the window, that is window length times core clock frequency, whatever executes in them. Numerator: the supervisor-use cycles defined in the text; application tasks and the scheduler of CON-SUP-006 do not count, and peripheral activity that proceeds while the core executes other software does not count (its effect on task timing is SYS-MEM-005). Window: every window position of the stated length within normal operation, so the verdict does not depend on window alignment. Real hardware is not required (CON-SUP-005); whether a target-board measurement is needed to confirm the bound of (2) is a stakeholder decision recorded in OP-SYS-060 item (d).

items.text: The supervisor shall be executable on the Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform description without the target board.

On the simulator of SYS-TST-001, the supervisor test environment shall be able to cause each fault condition specified in SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005 by acting only on the executions of the application tasks and on the timer-driven scheduler of CON-SUP-006, by suppressing, delaying, extending or reordering task executions or by stopping that scheduler, with no test-environment action on the supervisor's detection of those faults or on its detection results.
items.rationale: Rework r1, split (F-sys-req-item-r1-036, F-sys-req-item-r1-037). STK-SUP-015 requires simulator testing including the injection of each fault named in the needs. The previous single item covered the task faults, permitted injecting a failed integrity-check result, and omitted the watchdog events of STK-SUP-005 and STK-SUP-006. It is split: this item keeps the task faults of STK-SUP-001 to STK-SUP-003; SYS-TST-003 covers the watchdog events; SYS-TST-004 and SYS-TST-005 cover start-up and run-time memory corruption by changing memory content; SYS-TST-006 records the observable outcomes. Stimulus: each task fault is caused at the boundary between the application tasks, the scheduler and the supervisor, so the fault is detected by the supervisor under test from the altered task behaviour; injecting a detection result would bypass the detection that SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005 require (the principle of F-sys-req-item-r1-037 applied to task faults). The stimuli listed are those the test criteria of SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005 already use. SYS-SAF-001, SYS-SAF-002, SYS-SAF-003, SYS-REC-001 and SYS-RST-001 cite the faults or corruptions of SYS-TST-002; they are not changed in this rework, and the update of those references to SYS-TST-002 to SYS-TST-005 is recorded in OP-SYS-037 item (h). The accepted injection means, and whether a test configuration of the controller software is accepted, are not in the inputs and are recorded in blocking open point OP-SYS-037 items (a) and (c). Demonstration criterion, once OP-SYS-037 is resolved: on the simulator, for each of SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005 apply the stimulus of the test criterion of that item and show from the records of SYS-TST-006 that the stimulus acted on task executions or the scheduler only and that the reaction of SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 followed; with no stimulus applied, show that no task fault is detected.

items.text: On the simulator of SYS-TST-001, the supervisor test environment shall be able to cause, as the first event that resets the controller after it is caused, each watchdog event of SYS-WDG-002, SYS-WDG-003 and SYS-WDG-004, namely the lapse of the configured timeout of the independent watchdog without servicing, a servicing of the window watchdog before its configured window opens, and the closing of the configured window of the window watchdog without servicing, with the reset produced by the simulated independent watchdog or window watchdog and not by a reset requested by the test environment.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-TST-002 (F-sys-req-item-r1-036). STK-SUP-015 requires injection of each fault named in the needs; STK-SUP-005 and STK-SUP-006 make an independent-watchdog timeout, servicing of the window watchdog too early and servicing too late detected faults that end in a hardware reset (SYS-WDG-002 to SYS-WDG-004), and SYS-SAF-004, SYS-SAF-005, SYS-RST-001 and SYS-DIAG-005 already rely on causing each of them on the simulator. Each event must be the first event to reset the controller after it is caused, so that the observed reset is attributable to that event and not to a supervisor reset of SYS-REC-001 or to the other watchdog. The reset must come from the simulated watchdog and not from a reset requested by the test environment, otherwise the watchdog detection would be bypassed (the principle of F-sys-req-item-r1-037). Whether the Renode STM32N6 platform description of CON-SUP-005 models the IWDG and the WWDG of CON-SUP-003, including the early-servicing window and the reset they cause, and the means accepted to cause each event, are platform facts and decisions not in the inputs; they are not assumed here and are recorded in blocking open point OP-SYS-037 items (b) and (c), item (b) including the approved scope decision if a watchdog is not modelled. Demonstration criterion, once OP-SYS-037 is resolved: on the simulator, cause each of the three events in turn; show from the records of SYS-TST-006 the servicing instants of both watchdogs, that the event occurred as defined in SYS-SAF-004, and that the next reset followed it with the simulator identifying the corresponding watchdog as the reset source and no other reset between the cause and that reset.

items.text: On the simulator of SYS-TST-001, before the release of a reset, the supervisor test environment shall be able to place any single corruption chosen by the tester that lies within the start-up coverage and corruption-detection criteria of OP-SYS-012 into the program code or the configuration data held in the simulated memory of the controller, with no test-environment action on the start-up integrity checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 or on their results other than that change of memory content.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-TST-002 (F-sys-req-item-r1-037). STK-SUP-015 requires injection of each fault named in the needs, and STK-SUP-007 makes corruption of program code and configuration data a fault to be found at start-up. The previous item permitted injecting a failed check result, which exercises the reaction but bypasses the detection required by SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002. The stimulus is now a change of the memory content itself before the start-up that checks it, so a check outcome can only come from the check under test. A corruption may lie in the memory holding the check's own code when that memory is within the coverage of OP-SYS-012; such cases are allowed and their selection is part of OP-SYS-037 item (e). Observable outcomes of detection, recorded under SYS-TST-006: no application task starts after the corrupted start-up (SYS-MEM-003); the status signal stays at the not-operational indication (SYS-SAF-003); a fault report for the corrupted memory area is transmitted on the diagnostic serial line (SYS-DIAG-001); and, as control case, with the same memory content not corrupted both checks pass and the application tasks start. The coverage and criteria are open in OP-SYS-012; whether simulated memory can be changed before the release of a reset, the corruption set that demonstrates the criteria, and how check start and completion are observed are not in the inputs and are recorded in blocking open point OP-SYS-037 items (d) to (f). Demonstration criterion, once OP-SYS-012 and OP-SYS-037 are resolved: for each corruption of the set of OP-SYS-037 item (e), place it in the program code or the configuration data before the release of a reset and show from the records of SYS-TST-006 that it was placed, that no test-environment action reached the checks or their results, and the detection outcomes above; run the control case and show that the application tasks start.

items.text: On the simulator of SYS-TST-001, while the application tasks are running, the supervisor test environment shall be able to place any single corruption chosen by the tester that lies within the run-time coverage and corruption-detection criteria of OP-SYS-020 into the program code held in the simulated memory of the controller, at an instant chosen by the tester relative to the full passes of SYS-MEM-004, including before the start of a full pass and after the area holding that corruption has been checked in the current full pass, with no test-environment action on the run-time integrity check of SYS-MEM-004 and SYS-MEM-006 or on its results other than that change of memory content.
