items.rationale: Split from SYS-TST-002 (F-sys-req-item-r1-037). STK-SUP-015 requires injection of each fault named in the needs, and STK-SUP-008 makes corruption of program code during operation a fault for the background check; injecting a failed check result would bypass that detection. The stimulus is a change of the program code in simulated memory during operation, so a detection can only come from the check under test. The two injection instants are those required by the verification of SYS-MEM-006 (corruption present for a whole pass, detected no later than the completion of that pass) and of SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 (worst case: corruption placed just after its area was checked, detected by the next pass). Observable outcomes of detection, recorded under SYS-TST-006: the start and completion instants of the full passes; the reaction of SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 at the control-output and status-signal pins; a fault report for the corrupted area on the diagnostic serial line (SYS-DIAG-001); and, as control case, no integrity-check fault over the same number of full passes with no corruption placed. A corruption in code executed during the test can also cause a task fault; how such a case is judged is part of OP-SYS-037 item (e). Coverage and criteria are open in OP-SYS-020; whether simulated memory can be changed during operation, how the progress of a pass at the level of memory areas is made observable, and the corruption set are not in the inputs and are recorded in blocking open point OP-SYS-037 items (d) to (f). Demonstration criterion, once OP-SYS-020 and OP-SYS-037 are resolved: for each corruption of the set of OP-SYS-037 item (e), place it once before the start of a full pass and once after its area has been checked in the current pass; show from the records of SYS-TST-006 the injection instant relative to the pass, that no test-environment action reached the check or its results, and the detection outcomes above, with detection no later than the completion of the first full pass that starts after the injection; run the control case.

items.text: On the simulator of SYS-TST-001, for the whole duration of each test run, the supervisor test environment shall record with time stamps from the simulator time base the instant, the target and the change of each injection made under SYS-TST-002 to SYS-TST-005, every start and completion of an application task execution, every servicing of the independent watchdog and of the window watchdog, every reset with the reset source identified by the simulator, every start and completion of a start-up integrity check of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 and of a full pass of SYS-MEM-004, every change of state of the GPIO pins that drive the control outputs and the status signal, and every byte transmitted on the diagnostic serial line.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-TST-002 (F-sys-req-item-r1-037, observable outcomes). Derived: STK-SUP-015 requires the supervisor to be testable on a simulator; showing that a fault was detected by the item under test, and not bypassed, needs a record of what was injected and of the controller's observable reaction that does not rely on the controller's own reports. The events listed are those that the test and demonstration criteria of SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005, SYS-MEM-001 to SYS-MEM-006, SYS-SAF-001 to SYS-SAF-006, SYS-REC-001 to SYS-REC-004, SYS-RST-001 and SYS-TST-002 to SYS-TST-005 already rely on. The control-output and status-signal pins (GPIO), the diagnostic serial line (USART) and the reset source (RCC, watchdogs) are boundary observations on the peripherals of CON-SUP-003; task starts and completions, check start and completion and full-pass instants are internal to the controller software and can need instrumentation, whose acceptance in the build under test is recorded in blocking open point OP-SYS-037 item (f); the accepted time resolution is OP-SYS-037 item (g). Demonstration criterion, once OP-SYS-037 is resolved: run one injection under each of SYS-TST-002 to SYS-TST-005 and show that the record contains every listed event kind that occurred in the run, each with a time stamp.

items.text: The controller shall use the STMicroelectronics STM32N657X0 microcontroller as its processing element.
items.rationale: Platform constraint CON-SUP-001; hardware reference is CON-SUP-002 (RM0486), cited by id only.

items.text: The supervisor shall access no microcontroller peripherals other than IWDG, WWDG, CRC, TIM, USART, GPIO and RCC.
items.rationale: CON-SUP-003 lists the peripherals available to the supervisor; read as the complete set.

items.text: The supervisor software shall be written in the C11 language.
items.rationale: Implementation constraint CON-SUP-004, allocated to software and carried to sw-req.

items.text: The supervisor software shall not use dynamic memory allocation.
items.rationale: Implementation constraint CON-SUP-004.

items.text: The supervisor software shall not use recursion.
items.rationale: Implementation constraint CON-SUP-004.

open_points.text: STK-SUP-010 says 'the same fault has repeated several times in a row' without a count. Needed: the number of consecutive safe-state entries that latches the safe state (SYS-REC-002), what makes two faults 'the same' (fault code only, or fault code plus affected task or memory area), and what ends a run (power-on reset only, or a defined period of fault-free operation).
STK-SUP-008 requires the run-time program-code check to complete a full pass 'in a bounded time' but gives no bound. The full-pass time bound for SYS-MEM-004 is needed.

STK-SUP-009 sets 50 ms 'from the fault to the safe state' but does not define the fault instant per fault type. For task faults the detection itself depends on configured limits (SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005). For run-time program-code corruption, detection latency is up to the full-pass time of SYS-MEM-004 (OP-SYS-002), which cannot fit in 50 ms unless the full pass is shorter than 50 ms or the 50 ms is counted from detection. A decision on the reference instant (occurrence, configured-limit violation, or detection) is needed for SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002.

Watchdog timeout and window values are not given (SYS-WDG-002 to SYS-WDG-005). Also, SYS-WDG-006 stops watchdog servicing on a task fault, so a watchdog reset can occur before the supervisor-initiated reset of SYS-REC-001; this changes the reset cause seen by SYS-RST-001 and the time available for SYS-DIAG-001. The intended precedence is needed. STK-SUP-005 names only task health; whether servicing also stops on memory integrity faults is not stated.
STK-SUP-010 does not state how long the controller stays in the safe state before the reset of SYS-REC-001, nor whether the fault report of SYS-DIAG-001 must be fully transmitted before that reset.

STK-SUP-012 and STK-SUP-013 do not define the fault-code list, the time-stamp reference and resolution, the report and request message format, or the response time for service-tool requests. A diagnostic interface specification is needed before software requirements (SYS-DIAG-001, SYS-DIAG-003, SYS-DIAG-004).

STK-SUP-013 'the last faults' and 'current supervision status' are undefined: the number of fault reports retained (SYS-DIAG-004), whether they survive a reset, and the content of the supervision status (SYS-DIAG-003) are needed.

STK-SUP-011 says the controller 'must be able to tell' the reset cause but not how it is made observable (fault report at start-up, service-tool request, or both), whether the two watchdogs must be distinguished, or how other reset causes (external reset pin, brown-out) are classified (SYS-RST-001).

STK-SUP-003 refers to 'one control cycle', but CON-SUP-006 gives tasks at 10 ms and 100 ms periods. The definition of a control cycle and of the expected order across both rates is needed for SYS-SUP-004 and SYS-SUP-005.

The inputs do not define the number of control outputs, the electrical meaning of 'switched off', the status-signal levels for operational and not operational, or the state of outputs and status signal during and right after a hardware reset before software runs (board-level facts not in the inputs). Needed for SYS-SAF-001 to SYS-SAF-003.

STK-SUP-014 gives 10 % of processor time 'in normal operation' without a measurement window or reference clock, and CON-SUP-005 says real hardware is not required. The averaging window and the verification approach for SYS-RES-001 are needed.

STK-SUP-007 and STK-SUP-008 do not state the memory areas that count as program code and configuration data, or the error-detection capability required of the integrity checks (SYS-MEM-001, SYS-MEM-002, SYS-MEM-004).

The needs do not address: configuration data that passes the integrity check but holds inconsistent values (for example a timing limit larger than the task period), malformed or unknown service-tool requests on the diagnostic line, and controlled shutdown. Confirmation that these are out of scope, or the required behaviour, is needed.

No approved fault-report contract exists in the inputs (STK-SUP-012 names the fields only). Needed for SYS-DIAG-001, SYS-DIAG-005 and SYS-DIAG-006: the frame encoding on the diagnostic line, including how a receiver recognises a truncated report; the fault-code list mapped to each fault of SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005, SYS-MEM-001, SYS-MEM-002, SYS-MEM-004 and to watchdog events; the affected-entity mapping for each fault, including which task or tasks are named for a program-flow fault of SYS-SUP-004 or SYS-SUP-005 that involves more than one task; and the time-stamp event (detection or other), reference (since which reset or epoch) and resolution with unit.

For watchdog events reported after restart (SYS-DIAG-005), the inputs do not state: whether independent-watchdog timeout, early-window servicing and late-window servicing must be reported with distinct fault codes and whether the platform can tell them apart after reset (related OP-SYS-008); what the affected-entity field holds for a watchdog event, including whether it names the task fault that stopped servicing under SYS-WDG-006; and what instant the time stamp gives for an event that occurred before the reset.

STK-SUP-012 gives no time limit for reporting. Needed: the reporting deadline used by SYS-DIAG-001 (counted from detection, including any intervening reset, restart and start-up checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002) and by SYS-DIAG-005 (counted from restart). Also needed for SYS-DIAG-006: whether memory retained across a supervisor or watchdog reset is available to hold an untransmitted report (platform fact not in the inputs), and whether the supervisor reset of SYS-REC-001 is to be held until the report is complete (related OP-SYS-005).

No approved service-interface contract for reading the supervision status exists in the inputs (STK-SUP-013 says only 'read the current supervision status'). Needed for SYS-DIAG-003: (a) the encoding of a valid supervision-status request on the diagnostic line; (b) the encoding of the response, including how a receiver recognises a truncated response; (c) the required status fields and their value sets, for example whether the response must give the operational or safe-state indication, the fault-detection state of each supervised task of SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005, the result of the integrity checks of SYS-MEM-001, SYS-MEM-002 and SYS-MEM-004, the latch state of SYS-REC-002 and the last reset cause of SYS-RST-001; (d) the sampling instant of the reported values relative to the request, for example no earlier than complete reception of the request, or the most recent completed supervision cycle with its maximum age in ms; (e) the response time in ms counted from complete reception of the request. Refines OP-SYS-006 and OP-SYS-007 for SYS-DIAG-003.

No approved service-interface contract for reading the last faults exists in the inputs (STK-SUP-013 says only 'read ... the last faults'). Needed for SYS-DIAG-004, SYS-DIAG-007 and SYS-DIAG-008: (a) the encoding of a valid fault-record request on the diagnostic line; (b) the encoding of the fault-record response, including the order of the reports, the encoding of an empty response (K = 0) and how a receiver recognises a truncated response; (c) the retained-fault count as a number of fault reports; (d) the response time in ms counted from complete reception of the request, and the behaviour when a request arrives while a fault report is being transmitted; (e) whether a fault report retransmitted under SYS-DIAG-006 is recorded once; (f) confirmation that fault records need not survive a power-on reset, including after power-cycling the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002, and whether memory retained across supervisor and watchdog resets is available on the platform (related OP-SYS-016, OP-SYS-008). Refines OP-SYS-006 and OP-SYS-007 for SYS-DIAG-004.

STK-SUP-008 requires a full pass of the run-time program-code check 'in a bounded time' but gives no value, and no approved value exists in the inputs. Needed for SYS-MEM-004: (a) the approved full-pass time bound with its unit; (b) confirmation of the start and end events used by SYS-MEM-004: the first pass counted from the start of the first application task after start-up, each later pass counted from the completion of the preceding pass, and completion of a pass meaning the instant at which every program-code area within the run-time coverage of OP-SYS-020 has been checked in that pass; (c) whether the resulting detection latency must fit the 50 ms reaction of STK-SUP-009 (related OP-SYS-003). Refines OP-SYS-002 for SYS-MEM-004.

STK-SUP-008 does not define which program code the run-time check covers or which corruptions it must detect, and no approved criteria exist in the inputs. Needed for SYS-MEM-004 and SYS-MEM-006: (a) the program-code memory areas covered by the run-time check, and whether they equal those covered at start-up by SYS-MEM-001; (b) the corruption-detection criteria, for example the classes of corruption to be detected in every case (such as any single-bit error, or any burst error up to a stated length in bits) and any accepted residual probability of an undetected corruption. Refines OP-SYS-012 for SYS-MEM-004 and SYS-MEM-006.

STK-SUP-008 requires the run-time program-code check not to disturb 'the application timing' but gives no measurable criterion, and no approved criterion exists in the inputs. Needed for SYS-MEM-005: (a) confirmation of which application tasks must be protected: every application task run by the scheduler of CON-SUP-006, supervised or not, or a stated subset; (b) the timing quantities to be protected per task, for example activation delay after the scheduled activation time, time from scheduled activation to completion of an execution, or activation-to-activation jitter, and whether interrupt latency or the scheduler time base are also protected; (c) the timing-interference limit for each task and quantity with its unit, or confirmation that zero increase is required; (d) whether the increase is measured against the same execution sequence with the check not running, or the limits are absolute values; (e) whether timing measured on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 is accepted as evidence for the target, or which analysis is required (related OP-SYS-011).

STK-SUP-010 requires recovery by a reset after safe-state entry but gives no time limit, reset kind or coordination with fault reporting, and no approved values exist in the inputs. Needed for SYS-REC-001: (a) the recovery time bound in ms, counted from the later of the output switch-off of SYS-SAF-001 and the status-signal change of SYS-SAF-002, to the first reset; (b) confirmation that both a supervisor reset and a watchdog reset are permitted recovery paths, that no precedence between them is required and that the first reset after safe-state entry completes the recovery; (c) confirmation that the reset is not held beyond the bound to complete the SYS-DIAG-001 report, an interrupted report being completed after restart under SYS-DIAG-006, or else whether the bound must allow the report to complete before the reset (related OP-SYS-016); (d) whether a watchdog reset occurring before safe-state entry is complete is acceptable (related OP-SYS-004). Refines OP-SYS-005 and the precedence part of OP-SYS-004 for SYS-REC-001.

STK-SUP-010 ('the same fault has repeated ... in a row') gives no count, no rule for 'the same fault' and no end of a run, and no approved values exist in the inputs. Needed for SYS-REC-002: (a) the approved latch threshold N as a number of safe-state entries under SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002, or an approved different counting unit (for example recovery resets of SYS-REC-001) with its definition; (b) the fault-equivalence rule: same fault code of OP-SYS-014 only, or fault code plus affected task or memory area, and how program-flow faults of SYS-SUP-004 and SYS-SUP-005 that involve more than one task compare; (c) the run-clearing events that end a consecutive run in addition to a safe-state entry for a non-equivalent fault, for example the power-cycle release of OP-SYS-024, a reset classified as power-on reset by SYS-RST-001, or fault-free operation for a stated time in ms after a restart, and whether the release of SYS-REC-004 clears the run; (d) whether a watchdog reset not preceded by a safe-state entry (SYS-WDG-002 to SYS-WDG-004) and a failed start-up check of SYS-MEM-001 or SYS-MEM-002 count as entries of a run, end a run or are ignored; (e) whether memory retained across supervisor and watchdog resets is available on the platform to hold the run across the recovery resets of SYS-REC-001 (platform fact not in the inputs, related OP-SYS-016). Refines OP-SYS-001 for SYS-REC-002.

STK-SUP-010 requires the latched safe state to persist until the controller 'is power-cycled', but the inputs define no power cycle and give no evidence that the power-on reset classification of SYS-RST-001 corresponds to one. Needed for SYS-REC-002, SYS-REC-003 and SYS-REC-004: (a) the approved power-cycle release condition, for example removal of the controller supply below a stated voltage in V for at least a stated time in ms, and how the controller recognises after restart that it was met; (b) whether a reset classified as power-on reset by SYS-RST-001 is accepted as evidence of that condition, and how brown-out, external reset pin and other reset causes of OP-SYS-008 are treated (SYS-REC-003 treats every reset that does not meet the condition as non-releasing); (c) platform and board-level facts not in the inputs: whether the latch can be retained across supervisor, watchdog and other non-power-cycle resets, and whether the control outputs and the status signal stay switched off and not-operational during a reset and before software runs (related OP-SYS-010, OP-SYS-016), or else an approved maximum transient in ms; (d) confirmation that the release ends the latched safe state so that start-up proceeds under SYS-MEM-001 to SYS-MEM-003 (SYS-REC-004); (e) whether simulator evidence on SYS-TST-001 is accepted for the reset-continuity test of SYS-REC-003 or analysis of the board is required.

STK-SUP-014 limits the supervisor to 10 % of the processor time 'in normal operation' but defines neither normal operation, the workload, the measurement window nor the evidence, and no approved values exist in the inputs. Needed for SYS-RES-001: (a) confirmation of normal operation as stated in SYS-RES-001: it begins at the first application-task start after passed start-up checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 and ends at a reset or the first detected fault, so start-up checks, safe-state reaction, fault reporting, recovery and the latched safe state are excluded, and the background check of SYS-MEM-004 and SYS-MEM-006 and service-tool request handling of SYS-DIAG-003 and SYS-DIAG-004 are included; (b) the reference workload: the supervised-task configuration of SYS-SUP-006 to SYS-SUP-008 (number of supervised tasks per period of CON-SUP-006 and their timing and order limits), or confirmation that the limit applies to the largest configuration the supervisor supports, and the maximum service-tool request rate on the diagnostic line in requests per s; (c) the measurement window length in ms (for example the 100 ms longest task period of CON-SUP-006 is one candidate, not a decision) and confirmation that every window position is assessed; (d) the processor core clock frequency in MHz of the STM32N657X0 used for the window (platform configuration not in the inputs); (e) confirmation of the counted activities: core clock cycles executing supervisor software, its interrupt entry and exit, and core waits for peripheral operations it started, with application tasks, the scheduler of CON-SUP-006 and peripheral activity in parallel with other software excluded; (f) the accepted evidence for worst-case core clock cycles per execution: Renode execution of the target binary on SYS-TST-001 with an approved bound for converting executed instructions to core clock cycles on the Cortex-M55, static worst-case execution-time analysis, or another method; the inputs do not establish that simulator timing represents the target (related OP-SYS-021). Refines OP-SYS-011.

STK-SUP-011 names three reset causes to be told apart (watchdog, supervisor, normal power-on), but the inputs do not list the reset causes the controller can experience, and the reset indications of RCC on the STM32N657X0 (CON-SUP-001, CON-SUP-003) are not stated in the inputs; they are to be confirmed against CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page. Needed for SYS-RST-001 and SYS-RST-002: (a) the confirmed list of reset causes on the platform and board, for example external reset pin, brown-out or other supply-monitor resets, software reset requests not made by the supervisor, and debug or lockup resets; (b) for each cause, confirmation of its class under SYS-RST-001 or SYS-RST-002, in particular whether a brown-out or supply-monitor reset counts as power-on reset, and confirmation that every cause outside the three classes of STK-SUP-011 is classified as other reset; (c) whether the controller can tell after restart a reset requested by the supervisor from a software reset requested by other software, and whether the independent and window watchdogs must be told apart (related OP-SYS-015); (d) the precedence rule when more than one cause is indicated for the same reset, for example a power-on indication together with a watchdog indication; (e) the effect of the other-reset class on SYS-DIAG-008 (retention across resets not classified as power-on reset), SYS-REC-003 and OP-SYS-024; (f) whether the Renode simulator of SYS-TST-001 models each cause and its reset indication for the tests of SYS-RST-001 and SYS-RST-002, or which other evidence is accepted. Refines the reset-cause part of OP-SYS-008.

STK-SUP-011 requires the controller to be able to tell the reset cause but does not say where or when the classification is made observable, and no approved interface contract exists in the inputs. SYS-RST-003 makes it readable on the diagnostic serial line by a service-tool reset-cause request. Needed: (a) confirmation of this observation point, or whether a report transmitted after restart without a request is required instead or in addition, and whether the class is carried by the supervision-status response of SYS-DIAG-003 (OP-SYS-017 item c) instead of a separate request; (b) the encoding of a valid reset-cause request and of the response, including the code for each class of SYS-RST-001 and SYS-RST-002 and how a receiver recognises a truncated response; (c) the classification-availability time in ms counted from the restart, after which a request is answered with the class, and the behaviour for requests received earlier; (d) the response time in ms counted from complete reception of the request; (e) confirmation that SYS-RST-003 applies in every controller state after restart, including the safe state, the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 and after a failed start-up integrity check of SYS-MEM-001 or SYS-MEM-002 (SYS-MEM-003), or the states excluded; (f) the instant used as the restart, for example the release of the reset as observed on the simulator of SYS-TST-001. Refines the observability part of OP-SYS-008.

STK-SUP-009 requires the control outputs to be 'switched off', but the inputs give neither the control outputs nor their off state, and no approved board or interface description exists in the inputs. Needed for SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-004: (a) the list of control outputs and, for each, the GPIO pin of CON-SUP-003 that drives it; (b) the off state of each output at that pin, for example a stated logic level, a stated voltage range in V, or the output driver disabled (high impedance), and any board-side condition that must also hold; (c) confirmation that the off state is observed at the driving GPIO pin, or the board-level observation point to be used instead; (d) board and platform facts: the state of each control-output pin during a reset and from the release of the reset until software configures it, which decides whether the off state of SYS-SAF-004 is reached through the watchdog reset itself or by the restart software (related OP-SYS-010, OP-SYS-024 item c); (e) whether the GPIO pin state reported by the Renode simulator of SYS-TST-001 is accepted as evidence of the off state and of the reset-time pin state, or which board analysis is required. Refines OP-SYS-010 for the control outputs.

STK-SUP-009 counts the 50 ms 'from the fault to the safe state' without defining the fault instant per fault type, and no approved definition exists in the inputs. SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-004 state fault instants from the literal reading. Needed: (a) confirmation that for SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005 the fault instant is the first violation of the configured limit or order as stated in SYS-SAF-001, so that the supervisor detection latency counts within the 50 ms; (b) resolution of OP-SYS-009, without which the fault instant for SYS-SUP-005 (end of the control cycle) cannot be determined; (c) for run-time program-code corruption, confirmation that the 50 ms counts from the first presence of the corruption; worst-case detection latency is up to twice the full-pass bound of OP-SYS-019, so that bound must allow twice its value plus the output reaction to fit in 50 ms (related OP-SYS-019 item c); otherwise an approved alternative start event, for example the completion of the pass that detects the corruption, with stakeholder acceptance of the longer fault-to-safe-state time; (d) for failed start-up checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002, confirmation that the release of the reset preceding the check is the fault instant, and the definition of that instant on the simulator (related OP-SYS-027 item f); (e) confirmation that STK-SUP-009 applies to the watchdog events of STK-SUP-006 with the watchdog-event instants of SYS-SAF-004, and that reaching the off state through the watchdog reset of SYS-WDG-002 to SYS-WDG-004 is the approved behaviour; (f) the measurement resolution in ms accepted for the instants recorded on the simulator of SYS-TST-001. The same fault instants are expected to apply to the status signal of SYS-SAF-002; that item is not changed here. Refines OP-SYS-003.

STK-SUP-009 requires a status signal that shows the controller is not operational, but the inputs give neither the status signal's pin nor its indications, and no approved board or interface description exists in the inputs. Needed for SYS-SAF-002, SYS-SAF-003 and SYS-SAF-005: (a) the GPIO pin of CON-SUP-003 that drives the status signal; (b) the not-operational indication and the operational indication at that pin, for example a stated logic level or voltage range in V, or a stated pattern with its period in ms, so that a tester can tell the two apart; (c) confirmation that the indication is observed at the driving GPIO pin, or the board-level observation point to be used instead; (d) board and platform facts: the state of the status-signal pin during a reset and from the release of the reset until software configures it, and the time from a watchdog-event instant to the restart software setting the not-operational indication under SYS-SAF-003, which decide whether SYS-SAF-005 is met through the watchdog reset itself or after the restart (related OP-SYS-010, OP-SYS-024 item c, OP-SYS-028 item d); (e) whether the GPIO pin state reported by the Renode simulator of SYS-TST-001 is accepted as evidence of the indication and of the reset-time pin state, or which board analysis is required; (f) confirmation that the fault instants of SYS-SAF-002, identical to those of SYS-SAF-001 (OP-SYS-029 items a to d), and the watchdog-event instants of SYS-SAF-004 used by SYS-SAF-005 (OP-SYS-029 item e) are the approved start events for the status indication, including that the worst-case run-time detection latency of up to twice the full-pass bound of OP-SYS-019 counts within the 50 ms, or an approved alternative start event. Refines OP-SYS-010 for the status signal.

STK-SUP-007 and STK-SUP-009 imply that the status signal must not show the controller as operational before the start-up checks have passed, but the inputs give no board description and no reset-time pin behaviour. Needed for SYS-SAF-003 and SYS-SAF-006: (a) confirmation of the hold interval: from the start of every reset, whatever its cause, until both start-up checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 have passed, or until the next reset if a check fails; (b) the definition of the start and the release of a reset for each reset cause of OP-SYS-026 as observable on the board and on the simulator of SYS-TST-001, including, for a power-on, the controller supply level in V from which the not-operational indication is required (related OP-SYS-027 item f); (c) board and platform facts: the state of the status-signal pin during a reset and from the release of the reset until software configures it, cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page, and the board circuitry on that signal, and whether together they give the not-operational indication of OP-SYS-030; if not, an approved maximum transient in ms, or confirmation that none is allowed, including the transition at the start of a reset from the operational indication; (d) whether the not-operational indication chosen in OP-SYS-030 item (b) can be produced without software, for example a static level, or else how a pattern-type indication is to be treated before software runs; (e) whether the pin state reported by the Renode simulator of SYS-TST-001 is accepted as evidence for these intervals, or which board analysis is required. Refines OP-SYS-010 and OP-SYS-030 item (d) for SYS-SAF-003 and SYS-SAF-006.

STK-SUP-001 requires noticing when a supervised task stops running but does not say when alive supervision starts or what the deadline for the first completed execution is counted from, and no approved definition exists in the inputs. SYS-SUP-001 states an author choice that needs confirmation: (a) that alive supervision starts, after every reset, at the instant at which the start-up integrity checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 have both passed, rather than at the start of the scheduler of CON-SUP-006 or of the first application task; (b) that the deadline for the first completed execution of each supervised task is its configured maximum interval counted from that instant, or else that a separate configured first-completion limit (STK-SUP-004) is required, for example to allow for scheduler start-up and for the first activation of the 100 ms tasks of CON-SUP-006, with its unit; (c) that no alive supervision is required before the checks pass, after a failed check (SYS-MEM-003) or while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is held; (d) that the fault instant used by SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 for a missing first completion is the instant at which the configured maximum interval (or the first-completion limit of item b) has elapsed from the alive-supervision start instant without a completed execution, since those items currently state the SYS-SUP-001 fault instant only from a preceding completed execution (related OP-SYS-029 item a); (e) the definition of the check-pass instant as observed on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 (related OP-SYS-031 item b); (f) for the test of SYS-SUP-001, whether for each supervised task a configuration (STK-SUP-004) exists in which its alive deadline expires before any reset caused by another fault detected in the same run (for example the late-activation fault of SYS-SUP-002 when the task or the scheduler of CON-SUP-006 does not start) or by a watchdog expiry (STK-SUP-005, STK-SUP-006), since the inputs give neither the configured values nor the watchdog timeouts; if not, how the alive detection of that task is to be observed before such a reset.

STK-SUP-002 requires noticing when a supervised task runs too late, and SYS-SUP-002 makes a late-activation fault the expiry of the configured maximum activation delay after a scheduled activation time without a start of the task, but the inputs do not define the schedule reference or the scope of this supervision, and no approved definition exists in the inputs. Needed for SYS-SUP-002: (a) the reference instant from which the scheduled activation times of the timer-driven scheduler of CON-SUP-006 are counted after each reset, for example the alive-supervision start instant of SYS-SUP-001 (OP-SYS-032 item a) or the start of the scheduler time base, and confirmation that scheduled activation times continue at the task period even when the scheduler fails to activate the task; (b) the controller states in which late-activation supervision applies, for example not before the start-up checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 have passed, not after a failed check (SYS-MEM-003) and not while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is held (related OP-SYS-032 item c); (c) SYS-SUP-002 (rework r2) states an author choice that needs confirmation: a start satisfies only the scheduled activation time whose activation by the scheduler of CON-SUP-006 its execution processes (the assignment rule of SYS-SUP-004), each execution is for at most one scheduled activation time, and this applies whatever the configured maximum activation delay is compared with the period; needed in addition: how the scheduled activation time that an execution is for is identified on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 (related OP-SYS-034 item b); how an activation that the scheduler issues after a stall covering more than one scheduled activation time is assigned; and whether the configured maximum activation delay of each task must also be limited to less than its period of CON-SUP-006, with the approving party; (d) confirmation that the expiry of the configured maximum activation delay is the fault instant from which SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 count the 50 ms, the detection latency lying inside the 50 ms (related OP-SYS-029 item a); (e) for the test of SYS-SUP-002, whether for each target task a configuration (STK-SUP-004) exists in which, when one activation is held, delayed or missed while the next instance of that task starts, no other fault (for example the program-flow fault of SYS-SUP-004 at the start of the next instance in the configured order, the skip fault of SYS-SUP-005 at the end of the control cycle, or the alive fault of SYS-SUP-001) is detected and no watchdog expires (STK-SUP-005, STK-SUP-006) before the delay of the target scheduled activation time has elapsed, since the inputs give neither the configured values nor the watchdog timeouts; if not, how the late-activation detection is to be observed before such a fault or reset.

STK-SUP-002 requires noticing when a supervised task takes too long compared with its configured timing, but the inputs do not define which time counts toward the configured limit or the events that delimit an execution, and no approved definition exists in the inputs. SYS-SUP-003 states an author choice that needs confirmation: (a) that the configured maximum execution time limits elapsed wall-clock time from the start to the completion of one execution, including preemption by other tasks of CON-SUP-006 and interrupts, rather than processor execution time of the task excluding them; if processor execution time is required instead, which preemption, interrupt and supervisor time is excluded and how it is measured on the simulator of SYS-TST-001; (b) confirmation that the start and the completion of an execution are the instants at which the task begins and ends the processing of one activation of the scheduler of CON-SUP-006, and how they are observed on the simulator of SYS-TST-001; (c) confirmation that an ongoing execution is declared overdue at the instant the configured maximum execution time is reached without completion, and that this instant is the fault instant from which SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 count the 50 ms (related OP-SYS-029 item a); (d) the controller states in which execution-time supervision applies, for example not before the start-up checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 have passed, not after a failed check (SYS-MEM-003) and not while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is held (related OP-SYS-032 item c, OP-SYS-033 item b); (e) the measurement resolution in ms accepted for the start, completion and fault instants on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 (related OP-SYS-029 item f).

STK-SUP-003 refers to the tasks of 'one control cycle', but CON-SUP-006 gives tasks at 10 ms and 100 ms periods and the inputs define neither a control cycle nor the expected order across both rates, and no approved definition exists in the inputs. SYS-SUP-004 states an author choice that needs confirmation: (a) that a control cycle is the 100 ms interval between consecutive cycle boundaries, the boundaries being the schedule reference instant of OP-SYS-033 item (a) and every whole multiple of 100 ms after it, rather than a 10 ms cycle in which the 100 ms tasks are expected in one of every 10 cycles, or another definition; (b) that the expected activation instances of a cycle are the scheduled activation times of SYS-SUP-002 of each supervised task within that cycle (10 per 10 ms task, 1 per 100 ms task), identified by task and position in time order, and that the configured execution order of SYS-SUP-008 is one sequence of these instances applied to every cycle; whether the tasks of one period have phase offsets within the period is not given in the inputs; (c) that an execution belongs to the cycle of the scheduled activation time of the activation it processes, whatever cycle contains its start; (d) that the order checked is the order of execution starts as defined in SYS-SUP-003, and how starts are observed on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 (related OP-SYS-034 item b); (e) that executions of different cycles are not ordered against each other, or else the cross-cycle rule; (f) that the start of a later instance after a skipped instance is a program-flow fault under SYS-SUP-004 at that start, in addition to the skip fault of SYS-SUP-005, or else which of the two is detected (related OP-SYS-014 for the reported fault code and affected tasks); (g) the first control cycle supervised after each reset, for example the first cycle that begins at or after the alive-supervision start instant of SYS-SUP-001 (OP-SYS-032 item a), and the controller states in which order supervision applies (related OP-SYS-032 item c, OP-SYS-033 item b); (h) that SYS-SUP-005, SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002, which still cite OP-SYS-009, are to use the same control-cycle definition. Refines OP-SYS-009 for SYS-SUP-004.

STK-SUP-003 requires noticing when one of the tasks of a control cycle is skipped, but the inputs say neither which task executions are required in a cycle nor when a missing one counts as skipped, and no approved definition exists in the inputs. SYS-SUP-005 states an author choice that needs confirmation: (a) that it uses the control cycles, expected activation instances and execution-to-instance assignment of SYS-SUP-004 (OP-SYS-035 items a to c, OP-SYS-033 item a); (b) that every expected activation instance is required (10 per supervised 10 ms task and 1 per supervised 100 ms task in each 100 ms cycle), rather than at least one execution per supervised task per cycle; (c) that an instance is skipped when no execution belonging to it has started, as defined in SYS-SUP-003, before the closing boundary of its control cycle, so that a start at or after that boundary does not satisfy it, rather than a separately configured skip deadline per instance (STK-SUP-004) or a completion-based criterion; (d) that the closing boundary of that cycle is the fault instant from which SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 count the 50 ms, those items still citing OP-SYS-009 (related OP-SYS-029 items a and b, OP-SYS-035 item h); (e) that supervised cycles start with the first cycle that begins at or after the alive-supervision start instant of SYS-SUP-001 after each reset, and that no cycle is supervised when no such instant exists (related OP-SYS-032 items a and c, OP-SYS-035 item g); (f) how a single late or missing instance that is also a late-activation fault of SYS-SUP-002 or a program-flow fault of SYS-SUP-004 is to be detected and reported, as one fault or as one fault per item (related OP-SYS-014, OP-SYS-035 item f); (g) the measurement resolution in ms accepted for starts and cycle boundaries on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 (related OP-SYS-029 item f, OP-SYS-034 item e). Refines OP-SYS-009 for SYS-SUP-005.

STK-SUP-015 requires the supervisor to be testable on a simulator including the injection of each fault, and CON-SUP-005 names the Renode simulator with STM32N6 platform descriptions, but the inputs state neither what that simulator models nor which injection means are accepted, and no approved decision exists in the inputs. SYS-TST-002 to SYS-TST-006 state an author choice that needs confirmation, and platform facts are needed: (a) confirmation that fault injection acts only on stimuli outside the detection under test: task executions and the scheduler of CON-SUP-006 for SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005, watchdog servicing for SYS-WDG-002 to SYS-WDG-004, and memory content for SYS-MEM-001, SYS-MEM-002, SYS-MEM-004 and SYS-MEM-006, never an injected detection or check result; (b) whether the STM32N6 platform description of Renode models the IWDG and the WWDG of CON-SUP-003, including the early-servicing window and the reset each causes, and the reset source indication (related OP-SYS-026 item f); if not, the approved scope decision for SYS-TST-003, for example a model extension, other accepted evidence, or a stakeholder-approved exclusion; (c) the means accepted to cause each watchdog event of SYS-TST-003 as the first resetting event and each task fault of SYS-TST-002, for example simulator control of execution or a test configuration of the controller software, and whether a test configuration that differs from the target build is accepted as evidence; (d) whether the simulated memory holding program code and configuration data can be changed before the release of a reset and during operation, and whether the CRC peripheral of CON-SUP-003, if used by the checks, is modelled (platform facts not in the inputs); (e) the set of corruptions to be injected to demonstrate the criteria of OP-SYS-012 and OP-SYS-020, for example per corruption class the number and placement of cases, including corruptions in the memory holding the checks' own code and in code executed during the test, and how a corruption that also causes a task fault is judged; (f) how task starts and completions, the start and completion of the start-up checks and the progress of a full pass of SYS-MEM-004 at the level of memory areas are made observable to the test environment, for example by instrumentation in the controller software, and whether such instrumentation is accepted in the build under test; (g) the time resolution in ms of the simulator time base accepted for the records of SYS-TST-006 (related OP-SYS-029 item f); (h) SYS-SAF-001, SYS-SAF-002, SYS-SAF-003, SYS-REC-001 and SYS-RST-001 cite faults or corruptions injected under SYS-TST-002, which after the split covers only the task faults; those references are to be updated to SYS-TST-002 to SYS-TST-005.

STK-SUP-005 requires that a failure the software does not handle still ends in a hardware reset, and STK-SUP-006 requires an independent watchdog with its own clock, but the inputs give no independent-watchdog timeout, no reference for the first interval after a reset and no platform behaviour of the independent watchdog, and no approved values exist in the inputs. SYS-WDG-002 states an author choice that needs confirmation, and values and platform facts are needed: (a) the approved independent-watchdog timeout range, as a lower and an upper limit in ms, within which the reset of SYS-WDG-002 must occur, counted from the interval reference instant; the lower limit must exceed the longest interval between consecutive servicings in healthy operation under SYS-WDG-005 and the time from the release of a reset to the first servicing in a healthy start-up, including the start-up integrity checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002, unless servicing during those checks is required; whether a separate, longer first-interval timeout after a release is required instead; (b) confirmation that the first interval after every reset, whatever its cause, is counted from the release of that reset as defined in OP-SYS-031 item (b), so that the independent watchdog runs from that release without any software action, or else an approved alternative, for example an interval that begins when the controller software starts the independent watchdog no later than an approved delay in ms after the release, with stakeholder acceptance that failures before that start are not reset by the independent watchdog; (c) platform facts not in the inputs, to be cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page: whether the independent watchdog of the STM32N657X0 can be started at the release of a reset without software, whether it can be stopped or its timeout changed once started, whether each reset of the controller restarts its count, its clock source and the frequency tolerance of that clock, and the prescaler and reload resolution, from which the achievable timeout range follows; (d) confirmation that a servicing is a refresh accepted by the independent watchdog and that each servicing starts the next interval; (e) the intended behaviour after a failed start-up check (SYS-MEM-003) and while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is held: whether the controller software services the independent watchdog in those states or repeated independent-watchdog resets are accepted, consistent with SYS-REC-003 and with the run counting of OP-SYS-023 item (d); (f) the watchdog-event instant from which SYS-SAF-004 and SYS-SAF-005 count the 50 ms for an independent-watchdog timeout in the first interval after a release, without any servicing, those items stating the instant only from the last servicing (related OP-SYS-029 item e); (g) whether the Renode simulator of SYS-TST-001 models the independent watchdog with these behaviours and timeout range, or which other evidence is accepted (related OP-SYS-037 item b), and the measurement resolution in ms accepted for the release, servicing and reset instants (related OP-SYS-029 item f). Refines the independent-watchdog timeout part of OP-SYS-004 for SYS-WDG-002.

STK-SUP-006 requires a window watchdog that detects servicing too early, but the inputs give no window-opening value, no reference from which the opening is counted and no platform behaviour of the window watchdog, and no approved values exist in the inputs. SYS-WDG-003 states an author choice that needs confirmation, and values and platform facts are needed: (a) the approved window-opening range, as a lower and an upper limit in ms counted from the window reference instant, and the configuration data that holds the configured value; the upper limit must be below the shortest interval between consecutive servicings in healthy operation under SYS-WDG-005 and below the time from the start instant of item (b) to the first servicing in a healthy start-up, and below the window closing of SYS-WDG-004; (b) the window-watchdog start instant after the release of each reset of the controller as defined in OP-SYS-031 item (b): whether the window watchdog starts at that release without software or when the controller software enables it, and in the latter case the approved maximum delay in ms from the release to that start and the stakeholder acceptance that early servicing before that start is not detected; (c) confirmation that the trigger is a service attempt, a refresh request written by the controller software, whether or not the window watchdog accepts it, and that each accepted servicing starts the next window; (d) the approved early-service reset latency in ms from a service attempt to the reset of the controller; (e) platform facts not in the inputs, to be cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page: the window-watchdog clock source and its tolerance, the prescaler, counter and window resolution from which the achievable opening range follows, whether a refresh request before the window opens is rejected and causes a reset, the reset latency, whether the window watchdog can be stopped once started and whether each reset of the controller stops or restarts it; (f) confirmation that the SYS-WDG-003 watchdog-event instant of SYS-SAF-004 and SYS-SAF-005 ('serviced before its configured window opens') is the instant of the early service attempt, for the start-up window and subsequent windows (related OP-SYS-029 item e); (g) the intended behaviour after a failed start-up check (SYS-MEM-003) and while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is held (related OP-SYS-038 item e); (h) whether the Renode simulator of SYS-TST-001 models the window watchdog with these behaviours, or which other evidence is accepted (related OP-SYS-037 item b), and the measurement resolution in ms accepted for the start, service-attempt and reset instants (related OP-SYS-029 item f). Refines the window-opening part of OP-SYS-004 for SYS-WDG-003.

STK-SUP-006 requires a window watchdog that detects servicing too late, and STK-SUP-005 makes the hardware reset the reaction, but the inputs give no window-closing value, no configuration holding it and no platform behaviour of the window watchdog at the window closing, and no approved values exist in the inputs. SYS-WDG-004 states an author choice that needs confirmation, and values and platform facts are needed: (a) the approved window-closing range, as a lower and an upper limit in ms counted from the window reference instant of SYS-WDG-003 and SYS-WDG-004; the lower limit must exceed the longest interval between consecutive servicings in healthy operation under SYS-WDG-005 and the time from the window-watchdog start instant of OP-SYS-039 item (b) to the first servicing in a healthy start-up, including the start-up integrity checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 if the window watchdog runs during them, and must exceed the upper limit of the window-opening range of OP-SYS-039 item (a); whether a separate, longer closing time is required for the start-up window; (b) the configuration data that holds the configured window-closing value, and whether it is part of the configuration data checked under SYS-MEM-002; (c) confirmation that the window reference instant is the window-watchdog start instant of OP-SYS-039 item (b) after the release of each reset as defined in OP-SYS-031 item (b) until the first servicing, and from then on the most recent servicing accepted by the window watchdog, so that a rejected refresh request does not start a window (related OP-SYS-039 item c); (d) the approved late-service reset latency in ms from the instant the window-closing time is reached to the reset of the controller, and the platform facts on which the achievable closing range and latency depend, to be cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page: the window-watchdog clock source and its tolerance, the prescaler and counter resolution, and the reset latency; (e) confirmation that the SYS-WDG-004 watchdog-event instant of SYS-SAF-004 and SYS-SAF-005 ('the configured window of the window watchdog closes without servicing') is the instant at which the window-closing time of SYS-WDG-004 is reached, in the start-up window and in subsequent windows (related OP-SYS-029 item e); (f) the intended behaviour after a failed start-up check (SYS-MEM-003) and while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is held (related OP-SYS-038 item e, OP-SYS-039 item g); (g) whether the Renode simulator of SYS-TST-001 models the window-watchdog reset at the window closing, or which other evidence is accepted (related OP-SYS-037 item b), and the measurement resolution in ms accepted for the start, servicing and reset instants (related OP-SYS-029 item f). Refines the window-closing part of OP-SYS-004 for SYS-WDG-004.

STK-SUP-005 permits watchdog servicing only while every supervised task is healthy, but the inputs do not define what evidence makes a task healthy or what servicing is permitted before task health is established after a reset, and no approved definition exists in the inputs. SYS-WDG-005, SYS-WDG-007 and SYS-WDG-008 state an author choice that needs confirmation: (a) the task-health condition of SYS-WDG-005: every supervised task of SYS-SUP-006 has, after the alive-supervision start instant of SYS-SUP-001 that follows the most recent reset, completed at least one execution, at least one supervised control cycle of SYS-SUP-005 has ended, and no fault of SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-003 for that task and no program-flow fault of SYS-SUP-004 or SYS-SUP-005 has been detected since that instant; or else the approved evidence, for example a stated number of completed executions or control cycles; (b) confirmation that neither watchdog is serviced from the release of a reset until that condition is first met (SYS-WDG-008), with the consequence that the independent-watchdog timeout range of OP-SYS-038 item (a) and the window-closing range of OP-SYS-040 item (a) must exceed the time from the release to the first instant of the condition in a healthy start-up, including both start-up checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 and at least one whole control cycle, with its maximum in ms; or else an approved start-up service condition, for example servicing during the start-up checks, with stakeholder acceptance that failures in that interval are not ended by a watchdog reset; (c) confirmation that after a failed start-up check (SYS-MEM-003) and while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is held no servicing occurs and repeated watchdog resets are accepted (related OP-SYS-038 item e, OP-SYS-039 item g, OP-SYS-040 item f, OP-SYS-023 item d); (d) confirmation that memory-integrity faults of SYS-MEM-004 do not end task health (related OP-SYS-004, SYS-REC-001); (e) confirmation that the service bounds of SYS-WDG-005 (below the lower limit of the OP-SYS-038 timeout range) and SYS-WDG-007 (at or above the upper limit of the OP-SYS-039 opening range, below the lower limit of the OP-SYS-040 closing range) are the approved bounds, or the approved margin in ms for clock tolerance within them; (f) OP-SYS-039 item (a), OP-SYS-040 item (a) and SYS-RES-001 refer to window-watchdog servicing under SYS-WDG-005, now stated in SYS-WDG-007, and are to be read or updated accordingly; (g) how the first instant of the task-health condition is computed from the records of the simulator of SYS-TST-001, and the measurement resolution in ms accepted for it (related OP-SYS-029 item f, OP-SYS-032 item e).

STK-SUP-005 permits watchdog servicing only while every supervised task is healthy, but the inputs do not say when the inhibit of servicing starts after a task fault or what permits servicing again, and no approved definition exists in the inputs. SYS-WDG-006 states an author choice that needs confirmation: (a) that the inhibit starts at the instant at which the supervisor detects a fault of SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005, the same detection that ends the task-health condition of SYS-WDG-005 item (d), rather than at the fault instant of SYS-SAF-001; (b) whether an approved maximum delay in ms from the fault instant of SYS-SAF-001 to that detection instant is required, so that the start of the inhibit is bounded from an instant a tester computes without controller instrumentation (related OP-SYS-029 item a); (c) that the only event ending the inhibit is the start of the next reset of the controller as defined in OP-SYS-031 item (b), whatever its cause, and that no fault clearing, resumed task execution, safe-state entry or other state transition before that reset permits servicing again; (d) that after that reset servicing is governed only by SYS-WDG-008, SYS-WDG-005 and SYS-WDG-007, including while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is held (related OP-SYS-041 item c); (e) that the obligation applies to all controller software, and that a window-watchdog service attempt rejected by the window watchdog counts as servicing; (f) that memory-integrity faults of SYS-MEM-004 do not start the inhibit (related OP-SYS-041 item d, OP-SYS-004), and the resulting precedence between the supervisor reset of SYS-REC-001 and the watchdog reset (related OP-SYS-022 item b); (g) how fault detection instants are made observable on the simulator of SYS-TST-001, for example by instrumentation in the controller software, whether that instrumentation is accepted in the build under test, and the measurement resolution in ms (related OP-SYS-037 item f, OP-SYS-029 item f).

STK-SUP-012 requires every detected fault to be reported with a fault code, the affected task or memory area and a time stamp, and CON-SUP-007 gives only the line settings; no approved fault-report contract exists in the inputs, so OP-SYS-014 cannot be resolved by the author. SYS-DIAG-001 states author choices that need confirmation, and the contract is needed: (a) the frame encoding of one fault report on the diagnostic serial line, including its delimitation, its length or maximum length in bytes, and how a receiver recognises a complete frame and discards a frame truncated by a reset, for example a length field and a check field with its algorithm; (b) the fault-code list, with a code for each requirement under which SYS-DIAG-001 makes a detection: alive fault (SYS-SUP-001), late-activation fault (SYS-SUP-002), execution-time fault (SYS-SUP-003), program-flow fault by order (SYS-SUP-004), program-flow fault by skip (SYS-SUP-005), failed start-up program-code check (SYS-MEM-001), failed start-up configuration-data check (SYS-MEM-002) and failed run-time program-code check (SYS-MEM-004), or confirmation of which of them share a code; (c) the encoding of the affected-entity field: the identifier of each supervised task and whether it is taken from the configuration data of SYS-SUP-006, the identifier of each memory area of OP-SYS-012 and OP-SYS-020, and the maximum number of tasks one report carries, which for SYS-SUP-004 must not be below the number of supervised tasks; (d) confirmation of the involved-task rule of SYS-DIAG-001: for SYS-SUP-004 the task whose execution started out of order plus the task of every preceding unstarted instance in the configured execution order, for SYS-SUP-005 the task of the skipped instance; or else an approved alternative, for example one report per involved task, or only the task whose start was out of order (related OP-SYS-035 item f, OP-SYS-036 item f); (e) confirmation that one report is required per detection as counted in SYS-DIAG-001, including simultaneous detections (for example an alive fault for every supervised task when the scheduler of CON-SUP-006 stops) and detections made after the first detected fault and before the recovery reset of SYS-REC-001, and whether the supervisor continues to detect faults in the safe state; or else an approved rule that merges or suppresses reports; (f) the time stamp: confirmation that it gives the detection instant of SYS-DIAG-001 rather than the fault instant of SYS-SAF-001 (which for a run-time corruption the controller cannot know, related OP-SYS-029 item c); its reference, which must let a report completed after a supervisor or watchdog reset identify the detection instant before that reset, for example time since the release of the most recent power-on reset, or time since the release of the reset preceding the detection together with a count of resets; its unit and resolution in ms or us; its accuracy against the simulator time base of SYS-TST-001; and its range and behaviour at wrap-around; (g) for a failed start-up check of SYS-MEM-001 or SYS-MEM-002, confirmation that the time-stamp reference of item (f) exists before that check gives its result; (h) how detection instants and failed check results are made observable on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 for the test of SYS-DIAG-001, whether that instrumentation is accepted in the build under test, and the measurement resolution in ms (related OP-SYS-042 item g, OP-SYS-037 items f and g). Refines OP-SYS-014 for SYS-DIAG-001; OP-SYS-014 remains for SYS-DIAG-005 and SYS-DIAG-006.

STK-SUP-012 gives no time limit for reporting and no approved value exists in the inputs, so OP-SYS-016 cannot be resolved by the author. SYS-DIAG-001 counts the reporting deadline from the detection instant, whether or not a supervisor or watchdog reset starts before the report is completed. Needed: (a) the approved reporting deadline in ms counted from the detection instant of SYS-DIAG-001, or separate approved deadlines for a report completed without and with an intervening reset; (b) the feasibility inputs for that value: the frame length of OP-SYS-043 item (a) in bytes; the transmission time per byte at the line settings of CON-SUP-007, 10 bit times per byte, that is 10 bit divided by 115200 baud, 86.8 us rounded, a calculation and not a measured value; the worst-case number of detections whose reports are pending at one instant (OP-SYS-043 item e); and, for the case with a reset, the time from detection to the reset (OP-SYS-022 item a, OP-SYS-038, OP-SYS-040), the reset and restart time, and the start-up checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 if the retransmission waits for them; (c) platform fact not in the inputs, to be cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page: memory retained across supervisor and watchdog resets that can hold pending fault reports and their detection instants, without which a report pending at a reset cannot be completed after the restart (related OP-SYS-018 item f, OP-SYS-023 item e); (d) whether the recovery reset of SYS-REC-001 may be delayed until pending reports are complete (related OP-SYS-022 item c, OP-SYS-005); (e) confirmation that the obligation of SYS-DIAG-001 lapses when a reset classified as power-on reset by SYS-RST-001 starts before completion, the inputs giving no non-volatile storage (SYS-DIAG-006, SYS-DIAG-008), and how other resets of OP-SYS-026 are treated; (f) confirmation that reporting under SYS-DIAG-001 continues after a failed start-up check (SYS-MEM-003) and while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is held; (g) confirmation that a frame interrupted by a reset is transmitted again in full after the restart, as SYS-DIAG-006 requires, and not resumed from the interrupted byte. Refines OP-SYS-016 for SYS-DIAG-001; OP-SYS-016 remains for SYS-DIAG-005 and SYS-DIAG-006.

STK-SUP-013 requires the service tool to read the current supervision status, but the inputs do not state what happens when a supervision-status request is completely received and a reset of the controller occurs before the response time of OP-SYS-017 ends, and no approved behaviour exists in the inputs. SYS-DIAG-003 excludes that case from its obligation pending a decision. Needed: (a) the expected outcome on the diagnostic line for a reset in that interval, for example no response, a truncated response recognised by the receiver under OP-SYS-017 item (b), or one complete response transmitted after the restart; (b) if a response after the restart is required, the instant its status values are sampled (before the reset, or after the restart per OP-SYS-017 item d), its deadline in ms and from which event it is counted, and the platform fact, to be cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page, that memory retained across supervisor and watchdog resets is available to hold the pending request (related OP-SYS-044 item c, OP-SYS-018 item f); (c) whether the outcome differs by reset kind: supervisor recovery reset of SYS-REC-001, watchdog reset of SYS-WDG-002 to SYS-WDG-004, power-on or other reset classified by SYS-RST-001 and SYS-RST-002 (related OP-SYS-026); (d) whether the recovery reset of SYS-REC-001 may be delayed until a pending status response is complete (related OP-SYS-022 item c); (e) whether the service tool must be able to tell a missing or truncated response caused by a reset from a line fault, for example by a following reset-cause request of SYS-RST-003 (related OP-SYS-027). Refines OP-SYS-017 for the reset case of SYS-DIAG-003.

STK-SUP-013 requires a service tool to read the last faults over the diagnostic serial line, and CON-SUP-007 gives only the line settings; no approved fault-history contract exists in the inputs, so OP-SYS-018 cannot be resolved by the author. SYS-DIAG-004 states author choices that need confirmation, and the contract is needed: (a) the encoding of a valid fault-record request on the diagnostic serial line, including its last byte, which defines the snapshot instant; (b) the encoding of the fault-record response, including how each fault report is represented (for example the fault-report frame of OP-SYS-043 item (a) and of OP-SYS-014 embedded unchanged), the report order (for example latest first), the encoding of an empty response with zero reports, its length or maximum length in bytes, and how a receiver recognises a truncated response; (c) the retained-fault count as a number of fault reports, and confirmation that it is the same count that SYS-DIAG-008 retains under OP-SYS-018 item (c); (d) the response time in ms counted from the snapshot instant, with its feasibility inputs: the maximum response length of item (b) in bytes, the transmission time per byte at the line settings of CON-SUP-007 (10 bit divided by 115200 baud, 86.8 us rounded, a calculation and not a measured value), and the worst-case time the line transmitter is occupied by fault reports of SYS-DIAG-001, SYS-DIAG-005 and SYS-DIAG-006 pending at or after the snapshot instant, including whether a pending fault report may be delayed by the response or must precede it (related OP-SYS-044 item a); (e) confirmation that the snapshot instant is the reception of the last byte of the request, and that both K and the identity of the reports in the response are fixed at that instant, rather than another instant, for example the start of response transmission; (f) confirmation that membership in the fault history is decided by the transmission of the last byte of a complete fault-report frame at or before the snapshot instant, after the start of the most recent power-on reset of SYS-RST-001, and not by the internal recording instant of SYS-DIAG-007, so that a report recorded or transmitted during response preparation or transmission is excluded from that response; that 'most recent' is ordered by the transmission instant of that last byte; and that a report interrupted by a reset and completed after the restart under SYS-DIAG-006 counts once (related OP-SYS-018 item e); (g) the expected outcome when a reset of the controller occurs between the snapshot instant and the end of the response time, which SYS-DIAG-004 excludes pending a decision, for example no response, a truncated response recognised under item (b), or one complete response after the restart with its content and deadline (related OP-SYS-045, OP-SYS-044 item c); (h) the measurement resolution in ms or us accepted for judging whether the last byte of a fault report precedes the snapshot instant, and the verdict when both lie within that resolution; (i) the controller states in which fault-record requests are served: during the start-up checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002, after a failed start-up check (SYS-MEM-003), in the safe state of SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 and while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is held (related OP-SYS-018 item f). Refines OP-SYS-018 items (a) to (d) for SYS-DIAG-004; OP-SYS-018 remains for SYS-DIAG-007 and SYS-DIAG-008.

STK-SUP-012 requires every detected fault to be reported with a fault code, the affected task or memory area and a time stamp, and STK-SUP-006 makes the independent-watchdog timeout, early window-watchdog servicing and late window-watchdog servicing detected events; the inputs give no mapping of these events to report fields and no platform evidence by which the controller identifies after the restart which event reset it, and no approved decision exists in the inputs, so OP-SYS-015 cannot be resolved by the author. SYS-DIAG-005 states author choices that need confirmation, and values and platform facts are needed: (a) confirmation that the three events are reported with three distinct fault codes, one each for SYS-WDG-002, SYS-WDG-003 and SYS-WDG-004, and the code values, distinct from the codes of OP-SYS-043 item (b); or else an approved rule that merges codes, for example one code per watchdog, with stakeholder acceptance that the merged events are not distinguished in the report; (b) confirmation that the affected-entity field names the watchdog that produced the reset (independent watchdog for SYS-WDG-002, window watchdog for SYS-WDG-003 and SYS-WDG-004), and its encoding within the affected-entity field of OP-SYS-043 item (c); or else an approved alternative, for example naming the task whose detected fault stopped servicing under SYS-WDG-006, with the value used when no such task exists; (c) the evidence by which the controller identifies after the restart the event that reset it, and the platform facts it depends on, to be cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page: whether the reset indications of RCC (CON-SUP-003) tell an independent-watchdog reset from a window-watchdog reset (related OP-SYS-026 item c); whether any platform indication tells an early service attempt from a window closing without servicing; and, if information recorded by the controller software before the reset is needed instead, for example the instant and outcome of the last window-watchdog service attempt, whether memory retained across a watchdog reset is available to hold it (related OP-SYS-044 item c); where the platform cannot provide that evidence, the approved scope decision for item (a); (d) confirmation that the time stamp gives the watchdog-event instant as stated in SYS-DIAG-005, consistent with SYS-SAF-004 as read in OP-SYS-038 item (f), OP-SYS-039 item (f) and OP-SYS-040 item (e), rather than the start or the release of the watchdog reset, in the time reference of OP-SYS-043 item (f), which must let a report transmitted after the restart identify an instant before the reset; (e) the time-stamp tolerance in ms, the maximum accepted difference between the time stamp and the watchdog-event instant, with its feasibility inputs: the frequency tolerance of each watchdog clock and the resolution of the timeout and window values (OP-SYS-038 item c, OP-SYS-039 item e, OP-SYS-040 item d), the early-service and late-service reset latencies, and whether the controller can know the event instant or only its last servicing before it; (f) the method accepted for the test of SYS-DIAG-005 to determine the expected event kind and watchdog-event instant from the records of SYS-TST-006 independently of the controller's reports, for example the stimulus applied under SYS-TST-003, the reset source identified by the simulator, the recorded servicings and service attempts together with the configured timeout and window values, or an event instant reported by the simulator watchdog model; whether the Renode simulator of SYS-TST-001 provides it (related OP-SYS-037 items b and f); and the measurement resolution in ms (related OP-SYS-029 item f); (g) confirmation that a watchdog reset that follows a detected task fault, servicing having stopped under SYS-WDG-006, is reported under SYS-DIAG-005 in addition to the SYS-DIAG-001 report of that task fault, each counted once in the fault history of SYS-DIAG-004 (related OP-SYS-043 item e). Refines OP-SYS-015 and the watchdog-event part of OP-SYS-014 for SYS-DIAG-005.

STK-SUP-012 gives no time limit for reporting and no approved value exists in the inputs, so OP-SYS-016 cannot be resolved by the author for SYS-DIAG-005. SYS-DIAG-005 counts the post-restart reporting deadline from the release of the reset caused by the watchdog event. Needed: (a) the approved post-restart reporting deadline in ms counted from that release, as defined in OP-SYS-031 item (b); (b) its feasibility inputs: the frame length of OP-SYS-043 item (a) in bytes; the transmission time per byte at the line settings of CON-SUP-007, 10 bit times per byte, that is 10 bit divided by 115200 baud, 86.8 us rounded, a calculation and not a measured value; whether the report waits for the start-up checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 or for the classification-availability time of OP-SYS-027 item (c); and the reports of SYS-DIAG-001 retransmitted under SYS-DIAG-006 after the same restart that can occupy the line first, with the order between them; (c) the relation of the deadline to the independent-watchdog timeout range of OP-SYS-038 and the window-closing range of OP-SYS-040: with no servicing after a release until task health is established (SYS-WDG-008), a further watchdog reset can start before the report is complete, for example after a failed start-up check (SYS-MEM-003) or while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is held, so for the report to be completed in those states the deadline would have to end before the lower limits of those ranges counted from the release; (d) the expected outcome when a further reset starts between the release and the end of the deadline, which SYS-DIAG-005 excludes pending a decision, for example the report transmitted after the next restart with retention across that reset (related OP-SYS-044 item c), or the report not transmitted, with stakeholder acceptance; and whether a power-on reset in that interval ends the obligation (related OP-SYS-044 item e); (e) confirmation that SYS-DIAG-005 applies in every controller state after the restart, including after a failed start-up check (SYS-MEM-003) and while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is held (related OP-SYS-044 item f, OP-SYS-041 item c); (f) the measurement resolution in ms accepted for the release instant and for the last byte of the report on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 (related OP-SYS-029 item f, OP-SYS-031 item e). Refines OP-SYS-016 for SYS-DIAG-005; OP-SYS-016 remains for SYS-DIAG-006.

STK-SUP-012 requires every detected fault to be reported but the inputs do not state what happens when resets interrupt the transmission of a fault report one or more times, and no approved decision or platform fact exists in the inputs, so OP-SYS-016 cannot be resolved by the author for SYS-DIAG-006. SYS-DIAG-006 states author choices that need confirmation, and values and platform facts are needed: (a) the post-restart retransmission deadline in ms counted from the release of each interrupting reset (OP-SYS-031 item b), or confirmation that it equals the post-restart reporting deadline of OP-SYS-048 item (a), with its feasibility inputs: the frame length of OP-SYS-043 item (a) in bytes, the transmission time per byte at the line settings of CON-SUP-007 (10 bit divided by 115200 baud, 86.8 us rounded, a calculation and not a measured value), the worst-case number of pending reports after one restart including the SYS-DIAG-005 report of the same restart, their transmission order, and whether retransmission waits for the start-up checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002; (b) confirmation that a report is identified by its fault code, affected-entity value and pre-reset detection-instant time stamp, with detections of identical content counted by number of completed frames, or else that the contract of OP-SYS-043 item (a) carries a detection identifier, with its encoding; (c) confirmation of the covered reset classes: supervisor and watchdog resets of SYS-RST-001 and other resets of SYS-RST-002, the obligation lapsing at a power-on reset, consistent with OP-SYS-044 item (e) and the reset causes of OP-SYS-026; (d) confirmation that retransmission continues after every interrupting reset with no limit on the number of attempts and after the SYS-DIAG-001 deadline has passed, SYS-DIAG-001 then being judged failed; or else an approved limit on attempts or time after which the report is abandoned, with stakeholder acceptance that the fault then goes unreported, contrary to STK-SUP-012; (e) feasibility under repeated resets: after a failed start-up check (SYS-MEM-003), while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is held and before task health is established, SYS-WDG-008 permits no servicing, so watchdog resets recur no earlier than the lower limits of OP-SYS-038 item (a) and OP-SYS-040 item (a) after each release; needed is either the required relation that the time from a release to completion of all pending frames is below those limits, or an approved servicing allowance (OP-SYS-041 item b), or stakeholder acceptance that reports pending in those states are not completed; likewise for successive supervisor resets of SYS-REC-001 within the recovery bound of OP-SYS-022 item (a); (f) platform fact, to be cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page: memory retained across supervisor, watchdog and other resets of the STM32N657X0 that can hold, for each detection whose report is not completed, its fault code, affected-entity value, detection instant in the time reference of OP-SYS-043 item (f) and its completion state, with capacity for the worst-case number of pending detections of OP-SYS-043 item (e) (related OP-SYS-044 item c, OP-SYS-018 item f, OP-SYS-023 item e); (g) whether the retained pending-report data must be protected against corruption by the reset or by a fault, and the reaction when it is found inconsistent after a restart, or confirmation that no such protection is required; (h) confirmation that SYS-DIAG-006 applies in every controller state after a release, including after a failed start-up check and while latched (related OP-SYS-044 item f); (i) the measurement resolution in ms or us accepted for the release, reset-start and last-byte instants on the simulator of SYS-TST-001, and the means accepted to start a reset at a chosen instant relative to a frame (related OP-SYS-037 item c, OP-SYS-029 item f). Refines OP-SYS-016 for SYS-DIAG-006.

STK-SUP-013 requires the last faults to be readable but the inputs do not state when a reported fault enters the fault history or how retransmitted reports are counted, and no approved decision exists in the inputs, so OP-SYS-018 item (e) cannot be resolved by the author.
