SYS-DIAG-007 states author choices that need confirmation, and platform facts are needed: (a) confirmation that the completion of a fault report as defined in SYS-DIAG-001 and SYS-DIAG-005 is the one event that commits a fault-history entry, so that no entry exists before that completion and a frame interrupted by a reset commits none; (b) confirmation that all frames transmitted for one detection under SYS-DIAG-006 share the one entry committed at the completion of its one fault report, with detections of identical content counted by completed frames (related OP-SYS-049 item b); (c) platform fact, to be cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page: whether the USART of CON-SUP-003 gives the controller an indication that the last byte of a frame has been transmitted on the line, and the delay between that transmission and the indication, which bounds how closely the commit follows the completion; (d) the required behaviour when a reset starts between the transmission of the last byte and the commit of its entry, for example a commit state kept with the completion state of SYS-DIAG-006 in memory retained across the reset so that after the restart the entry is committed and no further frame is begun, together with whether that platform memory exists (related OP-SYS-049 items f and g, OP-SYS-018 item f); (e) confirmation that the measurement resolution of OP-SYS-046 item (h) applies to judging whether an entry is present at a snapshot instant close to the last byte of a fault report. Refines OP-SYS-018 item (e) for SYS-DIAG-007; OP-SYS-018 is not changed.

STK-SUP-013 requires a service tool to read the last faults, and SYS-DIAG-004 counts the fault history from the most recent power-on reset across every other reset, but the inputs give no retained count, no confirmed list of reset causes with their classes and no platform fact on memory preserved across resets of the STM32N657X0 (CON-SUP-001), and no approved decision exists in the inputs, so the retention parts of OP-SYS-018 items (c) and (f), OP-SYS-016 and OP-SYS-026 item (e) cannot be resolved by the author. SYS-DIAG-008 and SYS-DIAG-009 state author choices that need approval, and values and platform facts are needed: (a) approval of the retained depth: that the depth stored across supervisor, watchdog and other resets is the one retained-fault count R of OP-SYS-046 item (c), as a number of fault reports, for every covered class; or else an approved depth per reset class, with the consequence that the history of SYS-DIAG-004, counted from the most recent power-on reset, and its K would have to be changed accordingly; with its feasibility inputs: the size in bytes of one entry (fault code and affected-entity field of OP-SYS-043 items b and c, including the maximum number of tasks per report, and the time stamp of OP-SYS-043 item f), times R, plus any consistency data of item (d), against the capacity of the memory of item (c); (b) approval of the retention boundary by reset class: storage required across the supervisor-reset and watchdog-reset classes of SYS-RST-001 (SYS-DIAG-008) and the other-reset class of SYS-RST-002 (SYS-DIAG-009), and not required across a power-on reset, including the power cycle that releases the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 (OP-SYS-024); for each reset cause of OP-SYS-026 item (a), its class under OP-SYS-026 item (b), in particular a brown-out or supply-monitor reset and an external reset pin, and therefore whether storage across it is required; and whether stakeholders need records across power cycles, for which the inputs give no non-volatile storage (CON-SUP-003, SYS-PLT-002); (c) platform evidence, to be cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page: for each reset cause in the classes of item (b) that require storage, a memory of the STM32N657X0 whose content is preserved from the start of that reset to its release, is not cleared or initialised by the platform before the controller software runs after that release, and is accessible to the controller software within the peripheral set of SYS-PLT-002 or an approved change to it; its capacity in bytes; and, for any cause for which no such memory exists, the approved decision: reclassification, exclusion with the matching change to SYS-DIAG-004 and SYS-DIAG-007, or another approved means (related OP-SYS-044 item c, OP-SYS-049 item f, OP-SYS-023 item e); (d) consistency of the stored entries when a reset starts while an entry is being committed under SYS-DIAG-007 or while the stored set is being updated or read for a fault-record response (related OP-SYS-050 item d), and whether the stored data must be protected against corruption by a reset or a fault, with the reaction when it is found inconsistent after a release, for example discarding it with a stated effect on the K of SYS-DIAG-004 (related OP-SYS-049 item g); (e) the evidence accepted that identity and recency survive each covered reset: whether the Renode simulator of SYS-TST-001 models the preservation or loss of that memory for each covered reset cause, the reset indication of each cause (OP-SYS-026 item f) and a means to start each reset at a chosen instant relative to a frame (OP-SYS-037 item c), or which other evidence on the target is required; (f) confirmation that the reference to SYS-DIAG-008 in SYS-DIAG-007 ('as retained under SYS-DIAG-008') and in OP-SYS-046 item (c) is read as SYS-DIAG-008 and SYS-DIAG-009, and that the count named there is R of item (a). Refines the retention parts of OP-SYS-018 items (c) and (f), OP-SYS-016 and OP-SYS-026 item (e) for SYS-DIAG-008 and SYS-DIAG-009; those open points are not changed.

STK-SUP-007 requires the program code to be found intact at start-up but does not say which program code is covered, which corruptions must be found, by when, or how detection is observed. No approved decision exists in the inputs, so SYS-MEM-001 cannot be verified by injection until a reviewer decides the following: (a) the program-code areas covered by the start-up check, identified for the STM32N657X0 (CON-SUP-001) with memory facts cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page. This includes where the program code is held at the release of a reset and, if it is copied before execution, which copy is checked; whether the areas include the start-up code executed before the check, the check's own code and unused or padding parts of the program image; and their relation to the run-time coverage of OP-SYS-020 item (a). (b) the corruption classes the check must detect in every case, for example any single-bit error, or any burst error up to a stated length in bits, or any error up to a stated number of bits, each with its unit. Also state whether an accepted residual probability of an undetected corruption outside those classes is required; if it is, it is verified by analysis, not by the injection test. (c) the start-up detection deadline in ms, counted from the release of the reset as defined in OP-SYS-031, and its consistency with the 50 ms counted from that release under SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 (OP-SYS-029). (d) confirmation of the observed detection event. The author's proposal: the instant at which the start-up program-code check gives its failed result, observed on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 by instrumentation of the check result accepted under OP-SYS-037 item (f), with the SYS-DIAG-001 fault report carrying the fault code mapped to SYS-MEM-001 as boundary evidence. SYS-TST-006 records the start and completion of the start-up checks but not their result, so a set-level change to SYS-TST-006 is needed; it is not made in this item rework. Otherwise, give an approved boundary-observable alternative. (e) corruptions within items (a) and (b) that stop or divert execution before the check gives any result, for example in the start-up code or in the check's own code. Decide whether SYS-MEM-001 must still detect them or whether they are accepted as detected by another approved means, for example a watchdog reset of SYS-WDG-002 to SYS-WDG-004. If another means is accepted, decide which observed event counts as their detection and how they are selected in the injection set of OP-SYS-037 item (e). (f) confirmation that the check and its deadline apply after every release of a reset, whatever its class under SYS-RST-001 or SYS-RST-002. Refines OP-SYS-012 for SYS-MEM-001; OP-SYS-012 is not changed.

STK-SUP-007 requires the configuration data to be found intact at start-up but does not say which configuration data is covered, which corruptions must be found, by when, or how detection is observed. No approved decision exists in the inputs, so SYS-MEM-002 cannot be verified by injection until a reviewer decides the following: (a) the configuration data covered by the start-up check: its content, at least the supervised-task set, timing and order of STK-SUP-004, and whether other settings (for example watchdog, diagnostic-line or status-signal settings) are included; and where it is held at the release of a reset on the STM32N657X0 (CON-SUP-001), with memory facts cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page, including whether it is part of the program image covered by OP-SYS-052 item (a), and, if it is copied before use, which copy is checked. (b) the corruption classes the check must detect in every case, for example any single-bit error, or any burst error up to a stated length in bits, or any error up to a stated number of bits, each with its unit. Also state whether an accepted residual probability of an undetected corruption outside those classes is required; if it is, it is verified by analysis, not by the injection test. (c) the start-up detection deadline in ms, counted from the release of the reset as defined in OP-SYS-031, and its consistency with the deadline of OP-SYS-052 item (c) and with the 50 ms counted from that release under SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 (OP-SYS-029). (d) confirmation of the observed detection event. The author's proposal: the instant at which the start-up configuration-data check gives its failed result, observed on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 by instrumentation of the check result accepted under OP-SYS-037 item (f), with the SYS-DIAG-001 fault report carrying the fault code mapped to SYS-MEM-002 as boundary evidence. SYS-TST-006 records the start and completion of the start-up checks but not their result, so a set-level change to SYS-TST-006 is needed; it is not made in this item rework. Otherwise, give an approved boundary-observable alternative. (e) corruptions within items (a) and (b) that alter data the check itself uses (for example its coverage limits or reference value, if held in the configuration data), or that are used by code executed before the check gives a result. Decide whether SYS-MEM-002 must still detect them or whether they are accepted as detected by another approved means, and if so which observed event counts as their detection and how they are selected in the injection set of OP-SYS-037 item (e). (f) when the program-code check of SYS-MEM-001 fails in the same start-up, whether the configuration-data check must still run and give its result, or whether the SYS-MEM-001 detection is accepted for that start-up; and confirmation that the injection test of SYS-MEM-002 corrupts configuration data only. (g) confirmation that the check and its deadline apply after every release of a reset, whatever its class under SYS-RST-001 or SYS-RST-002. Refines OP-SYS-012 for SYS-MEM-002; OP-SYS-012 is not changed.

STK-SUP-008 requires the run-time program-code check not to disturb 'the application timing' but gives no measurable criterion, workload, baseline or accepted evidence, and no approved decision exists in the inputs. SYS-MEM-005 cannot be given a verdict until a reviewer decides the following: (a) the protected application tasks. The author's proposal: every application task run by the scheduler of CON-SUP-006 at the 10 ms and 100 ms periods, supervised or not. Otherwise, a stated subset. Also state whether interrupt handlers or the scheduler time base are protected. (b) the reference workload under which the limits apply: the application task set with its scheduled execution sequence and the execution demand of each task, the supervised-task configuration of SYS-SUP-006 to SYS-SUP-008, and the supervisor activity running at the same time, for example service-tool requests of SYS-DIAG-003 and SYS-DIAG-004 in requests per s. Also state whether it is the reference workload of OP-SYS-025 item (b). (c) the protected timing quantities per task, each with its definition and unit, for example the delay in ms from the scheduled activation instant to the start of the execution, the time in ms from the scheduled activation instant to the completion of the execution, or the activation-to-activation jitter in ms. SYS-TST-006 records the start and completion of task executions but not the scheduled activation instant, so a quantity that needs that instant also needs a set-level change to SYS-TST-006; that change is not made in this item rework. (d) the baseline: either the same quantity of the same task activation in a paired run of the same scheduled execution sequence and workload with no full pass of SYS-MEM-004 in progress, or no baseline, with the limits of item (e) used as absolute values. SYS-MEM-004 runs full passes back to back from the first application-task start, so a paired baseline needs a test configuration in which the check does not run; state whether that configuration is accepted as evidence for the target build (related OP-SYS-037 item c). (e) the timing-interference limit per task and quantity with its unit, for example in ms or in % of the task period, or confirmation that zero increase is required. (f) the evidence accepted for the timing of the STM32N657X0 (CON-SUP-001). Candidates: measurement on the target board; timing measured on the Renode simulator of SYS-TST-001 with an approved argument that the simulator represents the instruction, memory-access and bus timing of the target for this measurement (platform facts not in the inputs; modelling of the CRC peripheral is OP-SYS-037 item d); worst-case timing analysis of the target that includes the memory accesses of the check; or an approved combination. CON-SUP-005 states that real hardware is not required, so if target measurement is the only accepted evidence, that conflict needs a stakeholder decision (related OP-SYS-011 and OP-SYS-025 item f). (g) the paired-run test design for the evidence accepted in item (f): the time source and its resolution in ms or core clock cycles (related OP-SYS-037 item g); the observation interval as a number of complete full passes of SYS-MEM-004 or a duration in ms; how the task activations of the two runs are paired, for example by the index of the scheduled activation; and how variation between repeated runs is handled, for example a stated number of repetitions with the largest observed difference used for the verdict. Refines OP-SYS-021 for SYS-MEM-005; OP-SYS-021 is not changed.

STK-SUP-008 requires the run-time program-code check to find corruption but does not say which program code is covered, which corruptions must be found, how detection is observed, or where a pass ends when it finds a corruption. No approved decision exists in the inputs, so SYS-MEM-006 cannot be verified by injection until a reviewer decides the following: (a) the program-code areas covered by the run-time check, identified for the STM32N657X0 (CON-SUP-001) with memory facts cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page, including which copy is checked if the program code is copied before execution, whether the areas include the check's own code and unused or padding parts of the program image, and whether they equal the start-up areas of OP-SYS-052 item (a); this decision also answers OP-SYS-020 item (a) for SYS-MEM-004. (b) the corruption classes the run-time check must detect in every case, for example any single-bit error, or any burst error up to a stated length in bits, or any error up to a stated number of bits, each with its unit. Also state whether an accepted residual probability of an undetected corruption outside those classes is required; if it is, it is verified by analysis, not by the injection test. (c) confirmation of the observed detection event. The author's proposal: the instant at which the run-time check gives its failed result, observed on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 by instrumentation of the check result accepted under OP-SYS-037 item (f), with the SYS-DIAG-001 fault report carrying the fault code mapped to SYS-MEM-004 as boundary evidence. SYS-TST-006 records the start and completion of a full pass but not the check result, so a set-level change to SYS-TST-006 is needed; it is not made in this item rework. Otherwise, give an approved boundary-observable alternative. (d) confirmation of the pass endpoints: a pass in which the check gives no failed result ends at its completion as defined in SYS-MEM-004; a pass in which it gives a failed result ends at that result, is not followed by a further pass because the controller enters the safe state of SYS-SAF-001, and is judged against the OP-SYS-019 bound counted from its start event. Also confirm that such a pass is not a timing failure under the test criterion of SYS-MEM-004, whose second failure case (bound elapsed with no completion derived) applies to runs without a failed result; that needs a set-level change to SYS-MEM-004, not made in this item rework. (e) corruptions within items (a) and (b) that stop or divert execution of the check, or of code executed during the pass, before the check gives a result, for example in the check's own code. Decide whether SYS-MEM-006 must still detect them or whether they are accepted as detected by another approved means, for example task supervision of SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005 or a watchdog reset of SYS-WDG-002 to SYS-WDG-004, and if so which observed event counts as their detection and how they are selected in the injection set of OP-SYS-037 item (e). (f) the injection instant on the simulator. The author's proposal: with simulated execution halted at a start event of a pass of SYS-MEM-004 (the start of the first application task after start-up, or a pass completion derived as in the test criterion of SYS-MEM-004), write the corruption into the program-code memory and resume execution; this depends on OP-SYS-037 item (d). Also state the number and placement of injections per covered area. Refines OP-SYS-020 for SYS-MEM-006; OP-SYS-020 is not changed.

STK-SUP-010 requires recovery by a reset after safe-state entry but gives no time limit, and the inputs give no decision on a reset that starts before safe-state entry is complete. OP-SYS-022 asks these questions but no approved answer exists, and the author cannot supply one. SYS-REC-001 cannot be given a verdict until a reviewer decides the following: (a) the recovery time bound in ms from the safe-state entry instant of SYS-REC-001 to the start, as defined in OP-SYS-031, of the first reset after the fault instant. For a failed start-up check of SYS-MEM-001 or SYS-MEM-002 the fault instant is the release of the preceding reset (SYS-SAF-001), and the safe-state entry instant is that same release when the board holds both indications in their required states from it (OP-SYS-028 item d, OP-SYS-031 item c), so the bound then includes the duration of the start-up checks. State whether one bound applies to every fault type or a separate bound per fault type, or give an approved alternative start event for failed start-up checks, for example the completion of the failed check recorded under SYS-TST-006. Also state whether the bound must allow the SYS-DIAG-001 report to complete (OP-SYS-022 item c, related OP-SYS-016). (b) confirmation of the safe-state entry instant of SYS-REC-001: the first instant at or after the fault instant of SYS-SAF-001 at which every control output of OP-SYS-028 is off and the status signal is at the not-operational indication of OP-SYS-030 at the same time, which is the fault instant itself when both are already in those states. (c) confirmation of the disposition of a watchdog reset that starts after the fault instant and before the safe-state entry instant. The author's proposal: it is the recovery reset of SYS-REC-001 when SYS-RST-001 classifies it as a watchdog reset, and it does not relax the 50 ms obligations of SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 counted from the fault instant, which are then met through the reset state of the pins (OP-SYS-028 item d, OP-SYS-030 item d). Otherwise, an approved alternative, for example that such a reset must be prevented by design. Also state whether such a fault counts as a safe-state entry for the run of SYS-REC-002 (related OP-SYS-023 item d). (d) confirmation that both a supervisor reset and a watchdog reset are permitted recovery paths with no precedence between them (OP-SYS-022 item b, OP-SYS-004). (e) the accepted means of causing, on the simulator of SYS-TST-001, a watchdog reset that starts between the fault instant and the safe-state entry instant, for example a task fault of SYS-TST-002 combined with an independent-watchdog timeout of SYS-TST-003, or confirmation that this case is verified by analysis instead (related OP-SYS-037 items a to c). (f) set-level alignment: SYS-SAF-001, SYS-SAF-002 and SYS-REC-002 describe safe-state entry by the output switch-off and status-signal change events; their update to the safe-state entry instant of SYS-REC-001 is a set-level change not made in this item rework. Refines OP-SYS-022 for SYS-REC-001; OP-SYS-022 is not changed.

STK-SUP-010 requires the controller to stay in the safe state until it is power-cycled when the same fault has repeated a number of times in a row, but gives no number, no rule for the same fault, no events that count or end a run and no power-cycle definition, and no approved decision exists in the inputs; the author cannot approve them. SYS-REC-002 states every rule except the two values of items (a) and (f) as the author's proposal from a literal reading of the inputs, and cannot be given a verdict until a reviewer decides the following: (a) the latch threshold N as a number of consecutive counted entries; STK-SUP-010 says the fault has repeated, so N is at least 2 counted entries unless an approved decision says otherwise; or an approved different counting unit with its definition. (b) confirmation of the fault-equivalence rule of SYS-REC-002: two counted entries are equivalent when their faults, each identified by its detecting requirement among SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005, SYS-MEM-001, SYS-MEM-002 and SYS-MEM-004 and by the tasks or memory area in the affected-entity field of its SYS-DIAG-001 report, form identical sets; this depends on the affected-entity rule of OP-SYS-043 items (c) and (d) for program-flow faults involving more than one task and on the memory areas of OP-SYS-052 item (a), OP-SYS-053 item (a) and OP-SYS-055 item (a); otherwise an approved alternative, for example the same fault code of OP-SYS-043 item (b) only. (c) confirmation of the run-clearing events: a counted entry with a non-equivalent set of faults, the start of a reset classified as power-on reset by SYS-RST-001, and the meeting of the power-cycle release condition; no clearing by supervisor, watchdog or other resets (SYS-RST-002) and no clearing by fault-free operation; otherwise the approved events, for example fault-free operation for a stated time in ms after a restart, and the class under SYS-RST-001 or SYS-RST-002 of brown-out and external-reset-pin resets for this purpose (related OP-SYS-026 item b). (d) confirmation of the counted entries: one per interval from the release of a reset to the start of the next reset in which a fault of SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005 is detected or a check of SYS-MEM-001, SYS-MEM-002 or SYS-MEM-004 fails, its faults being those with the earliest fault instant of SYS-SAF-001 in that interval; a watchdog event of SYS-WDG-002 to SYS-WDG-004 neither counts nor clears; a task fault followed by a watchdog reset before its safe-state entry instant (OP-SYS-056 item c) counts once, as that task fault; otherwise the approved rule, for example watchdog events as counted entries with their own identity (related OP-SYS-047 items a and c). (e) confirmation that a failed start-up check of SYS-MEM-001 or SYS-MEM-002 is a counted entry, with its safe-state entry instant equal to the release of the preceding reset when every control output of OP-SYS-028 and the status signal of OP-SYS-030 are already in their required states at that release (OP-SYS-028 item d, OP-SYS-031 item c), so that a corruption persisting over N start-ups latches at the Nth release; otherwise the approved treatment, for example that failed start-up checks neither count nor clear, with the resulting behaviour of a persisting corruption (repeated resets under SYS-REC-001, related OP-SYS-041 item c). (f) the power-cycle release condition of OP-SYS-024 item (a) and how the controller recognises after restart that it was met (OP-SYS-024 item b); SYS-REC-002 holds the safe state until that condition is met. (g) platform fact, to be cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page: memory retained across supervisor, watchdog and other resets that can hold the run (the identity of the faults of the last counted entry and the count of consecutive equivalent entries), and whether that data must be protected against corruption, with the reaction when it is found inconsistent after a restart (related OP-SYS-023 item e, OP-SYS-049 items f and g, OP-SYS-051 item c). (h) the accepted means on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 to apply the release condition and a power-on reset in the tests of SYS-REC-002, and the measurement resolution in ms for the pin records (related OP-SYS-024 item e, OP-SYS-029 item f). Refines OP-SYS-023 for SYS-REC-002; OP-SYS-023 and OP-SYS-024 are not changed.

STK-SUP-010 keeps the latched safe state until the controller is power-cycled, but the inputs define no power cycle, no reset-time behaviour of the control-output and status-signal pins, no memory preserved across resets and no evidence for reset causes the simulator does not model, and no approved decision exists in the inputs; the author cannot approve them. SYS-REC-003, SYS-REC-005 and SYS-REC-006 cannot be given a verdict until a reviewer decides the following: (a) confirmation of the power-cycle boundary: the hold applies to every reset that starts while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is held, from its start until the earlier of its release (OP-SYS-031) and the instant at which the release condition of OP-SYS-024 item (a) is met; a reset that reaches its release without that condition having been met is non-releasing whatever its class, including supervisor and watchdog resets of SYS-RST-001, other resets of SYS-RST-002 (for example an external reset pin or a software reset not requested by the supervisor, OP-SYS-026 item a) and resets classified as power-on reset whose supply interruption does not meet the condition (for example a brown-out); with the definition of the instant at which the condition is met as observable on the board and on the simulator of SYS-TST-001; otherwise the approved boundary (related OP-SYS-024 items a and b, OP-SYS-057 item f). (b) whether the off state of OP-SYS-028 item (b) and the not-operational indication of OP-SYS-030 item (b) are given at their pins while the controller supply is below its operating range during a reset, from the board circuitry, or an approved supply level in V below which the pins are not observed, with stakeholder acceptance (related OP-SYS-031 item b). (c) board and platform facts, for each reset cause of OP-SYS-026 item (a), cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page, with the board circuitry of each control output: the state of each control-output pin from the start of the reset to its release and from the release until the controller software configures it, whether that is the off state of OP-SYS-028, and if not an approved maximum transient in ms or confirmation that none is allowed (refines OP-SYS-024 item c and OP-SYS-028 item d for SYS-REC-003 and SYS-REC-005; the status-signal pin is OP-SYS-031 item c). (d) platform fact, for each non-releasing reset cause, cited from RM0486 by section and page: a memory that can hold the latch state of SYS-REC-002 (OP-SYS-057 item g), whose content is preserved from the start of that reset to its release and is not cleared or initialised by the platform before the controller software reads it after the release; for a cause without such memory, the approved means by which the latch is kept for that cause, for example a board-level means, or an approved scope decision with stakeholder acceptance that STK-SUP-010 is then not met for that cause (related OP-SYS-023 item e, OP-SYS-051 item c). (e) confirmation that for SYS-REC-003 the analysis of item (c) for every reset cause of OP-SYS-026 item (a) is the primary evidence, and whether simulator pin sampling on SYS-TST-001 is accepted as supporting evidence for modelled causes (related OP-SYS-028 item e, OP-SYS-031 item e). (f) for SYS-REC-005 and SYS-REC-006: which non-releasing reset causes the Renode simulator of SYS-TST-001 models with their reset indication, reset-time pin state and memory preservation (related OP-SYS-026 item f, OP-SYS-051 item e); the means of causing each while the latch is held, in particular a supervisor reset, which SYS-REC-001 does not request while latched, an other reset of SYS-RST-002 and a supply interruption that does not meet the release condition (related OP-SYS-037 item c); and acceptance, for causes not modelled, of the equivalence analysis of SYS-REC-005, by which the simulator test of a modelled cause stands for a cause whose post-release platform state (pin state of item c, memory preservation of item d, reset indication of OP-SYS-026) is shown to be identical. (g) for each confirmed cause with no equivalent modelled cause, whether a test on the target board of CON-SUP-001 with the board of OP-SYS-028 and OP-SYS-030 is required, which needs a stakeholder decision because CON-SUP-005 does not require real hardware, or which other evidence is accepted. (h) the measurement resolution in ms accepted for pin sampling and for the start, release and release-condition instants (related OP-SYS-029 item f, OP-SYS-037 item g). (i) set-level alignment not made in this item rework: the rationale of SYS-REC-002 and SYS-RST-002, OP-SYS-024 and OP-SYS-026 item (e) refer to SYS-REC-003 for the whole continuity across resets, now SYS-REC-003, SYS-REC-005, SYS-REC-006 and SYS-SAF-006; SYS-TST-006 records neither the controller supply level nor the release-condition instant needed for supply-interruption cases. Refines OP-SYS-024 items (b), (c) and (e) for SYS-REC-003, SYS-REC-005 and SYS-REC-006; OP-SYS-024 is not changed.

STK-SUP-010 ends the latched safe state when the controller 'is power-cycled', but the inputs define no power cycle, no event at which the latch ends and no approved decision on either; the author cannot approve them. SYS-REC-004 and SYS-REC-007 cannot be given a verdict until a reviewer decides the following: (a) the power-cycle signature: the approved release condition of OP-SYS-024 item (a), as a named supply of the controller, a level in V on that supply and a minimum duration in ms below that level, and the evidence by which the controller recognises after the release that the condition was met (OP-SYS-024 item b), for example a platform reset indication cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page or the loss of a retained latch state; with the approved treatment of a release at which that evidence is absent or inconsistent (related OP-SYS-057 item g, OP-SYS-058 item d). (b) confirmation of the restart event of SYS-REC-004: the release, as defined in OP-SYS-031, of the reset during which the condition is met; and the platform fact, cited from RM0486 by section and page, that the condition can be met only between the start and the release of a reset, or else the approved restart event when the condition is met outside a reset. (c) confirmation that ending the latch at the restart event restarts the run of SYS-REC-002 there, so that a failed start-up check of SYS-MEM-001 or SYS-MEM-002 after the restart event, including one for the fault that caused the latch, is the first counted entry of a new run and is followed by the reset of SYS-REC-001 when N of OP-SYS-057 item (a) is 2 or more, the hold returning at the Nth equivalent entry counted from the restart event; otherwise the approved treatment, for example that the latch is re-entered at once when the first start-up check after the restart event fails for an equivalent fault. (d) confirmation that the restart event authorises no application-task start on its own, and that application tasks start after it only when both start-up checks of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 have given a passed result (SYS-REC-007); and the means by which a passed result and each application-task start are observed on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 (author's proposal: instrumentation accepted under OP-SYS-037 item f; related OP-SYS-052 item d, OP-SYS-053 item d). (e) whether, after the restart event, every control output of OP-SYS-028 must stay in its off state from the restart event until both start-up checks have passed, rather than reach it no later than 50 ms after the restart event under SYS-SAF-001 when a check fails; the inputs do not require it, and it depends on the pin state from the release until software configures the pin (OP-SYS-058 item c, OP-SYS-028 item d). (f) the means accepted on SYS-TST-001 to apply the release condition and a supply interruption that does not meet it, to record the condition instant and the restart event, the observation interval for the non-releasing control case of SYS-REC-004, and the measurement resolution in ms (related OP-SYS-057 item h, OP-SYS-058 items f, h and i). (g) whether the supervision-status response of SYS-DIAG-003 is to report the latch state, which would give a direct observation of the end of the latch at the restart event apart from the application start; the inputs do not require it (STK-SUP-013 names only the current supervision status; related OP-SYS-017 item c). Refines OP-SYS-024 items (a), (b) and (d) for SYS-REC-004 and SYS-REC-007; OP-SYS-024 is not changed. Set-level alignment not made in this item rework: OP-SYS-023 item (c), OP-SYS-024 item (d) and the rationale of SYS-REC-002 refer to SYS-REC-004 for the whole of the release, which is now SYS-REC-004 and SYS-REC-007.

STK-SUP-014 limits the supervisor to 10 % of the processor time in normal operation, and SYS-RES-001 is verified by analysis against justified upper bounds on execution counts and cycle costs, but the inputs give no reference workload, no measurement window, no core clock frequency and no accepted method or platform facts for target cycle bounds, and the author cannot approve them. SYS-RES-001 cannot be given a verdict until a reviewer decides the following: (a) the approved reference workload: the supervised-task configuration limits of SYS-SUP-006 to SYS-SUP-008 (maximum number of supervised tasks per period of CON-SUP-006 and the timing and order limits that set the supervisor work per period), or confirmation that the largest configuration the supervisor supports is the reference; and the arrival bound for service-tool requests on the diagnostic line, as a minimum time in ms between the starts of two requests or a maximum number of requests per window, or confirmation that the only bound is the line rate of CON-SUP-007 together with the minimum request length in characters from OP-SYS-017 and OP-SYS-018, so that continuous request traffic is analysed. (b) the approved measurement window length in ms (the 100 ms longest task period of CON-SUP-006 is one candidate, not a decision), with confirmation that every window position within normal operation is assessed and that an execution overlapping a window boundary counts as a whole execution. (c) the processor core clock frequency in MHz of the STM32N657X0 in normal operation, and whether it can change during normal operation (platform configuration not in the inputs). (d) the accepted method for upper bounds on core clock cycles per execution of the target binary, for example static worst-case execution-time analysis with a Cortex-M55 timing model of the target memory and cache configuration, or a path-based bound over all feasible paths with a justified per-instruction cycle bound, with the evidence that justifies the model or bound cited by document id, section and page; confirmation that Renode runs on SYS-TST-001 and host unit tests are supporting evidence only and do not establish the bound; and whether a measurement on the target board of CON-SUP-001 is required to confirm the bound, which needs a stakeholder decision because CON-SUP-005 does not require real hardware. (e) platform facts not in the inputs, cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) or the processor documentation by section and page: the worst-case completion time in core clock cycles or in µs of each peripheral operation of CON-SUP-003 whose completion supervisor software waits for; the interrupt entry and exit cycle bound; and the memory wait states and cache configuration of the memory from which the supervisor executes and which it reads; or an approved alternative assumption with its justification. (f) the accepted source of loop iteration bounds, for example the configuration limits of item (a) and the share of the program-code check of SYS-MEM-004 and SYS-MEM-006 done per execution (related OP-SYS-019, OP-SYS-020). Refines OP-SYS-025 items (b), (c), (d) and (f) for SYS-RES-001; OP-SYS-025 items (a) and (e) stay open there; OP-SYS-025 is not changed. Set-level alignment not made in this item rework: OP-SYS-025 item (f) still names Renode execution with a conversion bound as a candidate evidence for worst-case cycles.

STK-SUP-011 requires watchdog, supervisor and power-on resets to be told apart after any reset. SYS-RST-001 states the class for each cause, excludes resets requested by other software from the supervisor class, and gives the class for a combination of causes by reference to this open point; but the inputs give neither the reset-cause evidence available on the platform, nor a precedence decision, nor an approved observation contract, and the author cannot supply them. SYS-RST-001 cannot be given a verdict until a reviewer decides the following: (a) the cause evidence: for each of the three causes, the reset indication of RCC on the STM32N657X0 (CON-SUP-001, CON-SUP-003) that shows it after restart, cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page; whether the independent watchdog and the window watchdog have separate indications (related OP-SYS-015); whether an indication persists across later resets until cleared, and which events clear it; and which indications a power-on sets besides the power-on indication. (b) the supervisor-reset evidence: whether the platform gives an indication that tells a reset requested by the supervisor from a reset requested by other software (application tasks, start-up code, a debugger) and from core-generated resets, cited from RM0486 by section and page; if not, the approved means by which the controller recognises after restart that the supervisor made the request, for example information retained across the reset, with the platform fact on its retention across supervisor, watchdog and power-on resets (related OP-SYS-024 item c); and the list of software-requested resets other than by the supervisor that the system can produce, each with its class under OP-SYS-026 item (b). (c) the precedence rule: for each combination of two or more of the three causes that item (d) lists, the single class assigned, with its justification from STK-SUP-010 and STK-SUP-011 (for example whether a power-on indication together with a watchdog indication is a power-on reset, which decides the latch release of SYS-REC-003 and SYS-REC-004 through OP-SYS-024 item b); and whether a watchdog expiry while the reset requested by the supervisor is in progress is a combination or a watchdog reset only (related OP-SYS-004, SYS-REC-001). (d) the supported combinations: which combinations of the three causes can apply to one reset on the platform and board, with the platform fact cited for each combination recorded as unable to occur, so that the test of SYS-RST-001 covers every combination that can occur and analysis covers the rest. (e) the observation contract: confirmation that the classification of SYS-RST-001 is observed through the reset-cause response of SYS-RST-003, with the observation point, encoding, classification-availability time in ms, response time in ms, controller states and restart instant of OP-SYS-027 items (a) to (f). (f) the evidence accepted for each case of the SYS-RST-001 test criterion: whether the Renode STM32N6 platform description of SYS-TST-001 models each indication of items (a) and (b) and can produce each combination of item (d) and each software-requested reset of item (b); the instrumentation independent of the controller that identifies the actual causes of a reset; and the analysis or other evidence accepted for a case that cannot be caused on the simulator (related OP-SYS-026 item f, OP-SYS-037 items b and c). Refines OP-SYS-026 items (a) to (d) and (f) and OP-SYS-027 for SYS-RST-001; OP-SYS-026 and OP-SYS-027 are not changed. Set-level alignment not made in this item rework: OP-SYS-004 and OP-SYS-026 item (d) still ask for the precedence that item (c) now records for SYS-RST-001.

STK-SUP-011 applies after any reset but names only watchdog, supervisor and power-on resets; SYS-RST-002 classifies every reset to which none of these causes applies as other reset. The inputs give neither the reset causes the controller can experience nor the evidence that distinguishes them, and the author cannot supply or approve them. SYS-RST-002 cannot be given a verdict until a reviewer decides the following: (a) the applicable reset causes: the confirmed list of every reset cause that the STM32N657X0 (CON-SUP-001) and the board can produce, for example external reset pin, brown-out or other supply-monitor resets, software reset requests not made by the supervisor, lockup and debug resets, with platform causes cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page and board causes from an approved board description. (b) the approved cause-to-class mapping: for each cause of item (a), its class (watchdog reset, supervisor reset, power-on reset or other reset), in particular whether brown-out and supply-monitor resets count as power-on reset, consistent with OP-SYS-061 item (b) for software-requested resets. (c) the distinguishing evidence: for each cause that item (b) assigns to other reset, the reset indication of RCC (CON-SUP-003) or other approved means by which the controller tells after restart that this cause, and none of the causes of SYS-RST-001, caused the reset, cited from RM0486 by section and page; whether two or more causes share one indication; whether the indication persists across later resets and which events clear it; and the combinations of an other-reset cause with a cause of SYS-RST-001 that can apply to one reset, with the platform fact cited for each combination recorded as unable to occur. (d) the accepted evidence per cause: for each cause that item (b) assigns to other reset, whether the Renode STM32N6 platform description of SYS-TST-001 can produce that cause together with its reset indication; for each cause it cannot produce, the accepted evidence, for example a test on the target board, injection of the reset indication on the simulator with an approved justification, or analysis cited from RM0486, so that no applicable cause is left unverified; and the instrumentation independent of the controller that identifies the actual cause of a reset. Refines OP-SYS-026 items (a), (b) and (f) for SYS-RST-002; OP-SYS-026 is not changed. Related OP-SYS-027 (observation contract) and OP-SYS-061 items (a), (b) and (f).

SYS-RST-003 and SYS-RST-004 define when a reset-cause request is answered and what happens when a reset interrupts its response, but the inputs contain no approved observation and timing contract, and the author cannot approve one. SYS-RST-003 and SYS-RST-004 cannot be given a verdict until a reviewer decides the following: (a) the eligibility and lapse rule: confirmation that a request is answered when completely received later than the classification-availability time counted from the release (OP-SYS-031) of the most recent reset, and that the obligation lapses when a reset starts after its complete reception, before a response to it is completed and before the end of the response time, or the approved alternative. (b) the outcome of an interrupted request: confirmation that no reset-cause response is begun after the release of the interrupting reset until a new request is completely received after the release of the most recent reset (SYS-RST-004), or the approved alternative, for example answering the interrupted request after the restart, with the class it then carries; and how this rule applies to any report after restart without a request that OP-SYS-027 item (a) may require. (c) response attribution and truncation: confirmation that a response belongs to the request after whose complete reception and before the next request's complete reception its first byte is transmitted, or whether the contract carries a request identifier; how a receiver recognises a response frame truncated by a reset (refines OP-SYS-027 item b); and the behaviour for a request completely received while a response is being transmitted or before the classification-availability time (related OP-SYS-027 item c). (d) feasibility between recurring resets: for the states in which watchdog resets recur without servicing (SYS-WDG-008, after a failed start-up check of SYS-MEM-003 and while the latched safe state of SYS-REC-002 is held), a comparison of the minimum interval from the release of a reset to the start of the next reset (lower limits of OP-SYS-038 and OP-SYS-040) with the sum of the classification-availability time, the transmission duration of a request at the line settings of CON-SUP-007 and the response time, and the approved outcome if the class cannot be observed in that interval (related OP-SYS-027 item e). (e) the absence-observation interval in ms after a release during which the absence of a reset-cause response is checked for SYS-RST-004. (f) the means accepted to start a supervisor, watchdog or power-on reset at a controlled instant relative to the last byte of a request and to the first and last byte of a response on the simulator of SYS-TST-001, and the measurement resolution in ms for those instants (related OP-SYS-037 items c and g). Refines OP-SYS-027 items (b), (c) and (f) for SYS-RST-003 and SYS-RST-004; OP-SYS-027 is not changed.

STK-SUP-009 requires the control outputs to be switched off within 50 ms of the fault. The inputs give no control-output list, no off state and no approved fault instants (OP-SYS-028, OP-SYS-029). They also give no fault instant for a task that has completed no execution, no verdict for outputs already off at the fault instant, and no means to have an output on at a fault instant during a test. The author cannot approve these. SYS-SAF-001 cannot be given a verdict until a reviewer decides the following: (a) the control outputs, their pins and off states of OP-SYS-028 items (a) to (c), and confirmation of the fault instants of OP-SYS-029 items (a) to (d) as now stated in SYS-SAF-001; (b) confirmation that the SYS-SUP-001 fault instant for a task that has completed no execution since the alive-supervision start instant is its configured maximum interval elapsed from that instant, or else the separate first-completion limit of OP-SYS-032 item (b) with its unit; (c) confirmation that the off state is reached at the fault instant itself when every control output is already in its off state at that instant, so that such an injection passes with a measured reaction of 0 ms, in particular for a failed start-up check of SYS-MEM-001 or SYS-MEM-002, whose fault instant is the release of the reset at which the pins have the reset-time state of OP-SYS-028 item (d); (d) whether the off state, once reached, must also be held until the start of the next reset of SYS-REC-001, which SYS-SAF-001 does not require; (e) the means accepted to have at least one control output not in its off state at the fault instant for task faults of SYS-TST-002 and run-time corruptions of SYS-TST-005, in particular before the first completed execution of a supervised task, for example a test configuration of the application (related OP-SYS-037 item c), and the minimum number of such injections per fault class; or confirmation that injections with every output already off are accepted as the only evidence for a missing first completion when the application under test switches no output on before it; (f) confirmation that the injection instant recorded under SYS-TST-006 is accepted as the first presence of a run-time corruption placed under SYS-TST-005; (g) SYS-SAF-002 still states the SYS-SUP-001 fault instant only from a preceding completed execution and cites OP-SYS-009 for SYS-SUP-005; it is to be aligned with the fault instants of SYS-SAF-001 at set level. Refines OP-SYS-028, OP-SYS-029 and OP-SYS-032 item (d) for SYS-SAF-001.

STK-SUP-009 requires a status signal that shows the controller is not operational within 50 ms of the fault. The inputs give no status-signal pin, no indications and no approved fault instants (OP-SYS-029, OP-SYS-030), and the author cannot approve them. SYS-SAF-002 cannot be given a verdict until a reviewer decides the following: (a) the pin and the not-operational and operational indications of OP-SYS-030 items (a) to (c), and the simulator evidence accepted under OP-SYS-030 item (e); (b) confirmation that the fault instants now stated in SYS-SAF-002, identical to those of SYS-SAF-001, are the approved start events for the status indication, including both alive-fault expiry events of SYS-SUP-001 (the configured maximum interval counted from the alive-supervision start instant when the task has completed no execution since that instant, otherwise from its most recent completed execution, or the first-completion limit of OP-SYS-032 item b), or else approved alternatives to be applied to SYS-SAF-001 and SYS-SAF-002 alike (OP-SYS-029 items a to d, OP-SYS-030 item f, OP-SYS-032 item d, OP-SYS-064 item b); (c) whether the controller is to show the operational indication between the passing of both start-up checks, which ends the hold of SYS-SAF-003, and the first completed execution of the supervised tasks, and the means accepted to have the status signal at the operational indication at the fault instant of a missing first completion during a test (related OP-SYS-037 item c, OP-SYS-064 item e); or confirmation that injections with the not-operational indication already shown are accepted as the only evidence for a missing first completion; (d) confirmation that the not-operational state is reached at the fault instant itself when the status signal already shows the not-operational indication at that instant, so that such an injection passes with a measured reaction of 0 ms, in particular for a failed start-up check under the hold of SYS-SAF-003; (e) the minimum number of injections per fault class with the status signal at the operational indication at the fault instant; (f) whether the not-operational indication, once reached, must also be held until the start of the next reset, which SYS-SAF-002 does not require. Refines OP-SYS-029, OP-SYS-030 item (f) and OP-SYS-064 item (g) for SYS-SAF-002.

STK-SUP-007 and STK-SUP-009 imply that the status signal must not show the controller as operational from the release of a reset until both start-up checks have passed. The inputs give no status-signal pin, no indication, no board circuitry, no reset-time pin state and no definition of the release of a reset, and the author cannot approve them or the evidence. SYS-SAF-003 cannot be given a verdict until a reviewer decides the following: (a) the GPIO pin of CON-SUP-003 that drives the status signal and its not-operational indication at that pin (OP-SYS-030 items a to c), and confirmation that this indication is a static state the pin presents without software running, for example a stated logic level or voltage range in V or the driver disabled with a stated board-side pull; if only a pattern-type indication is approved, the approved treatment of the interval from the release until software configures the pin (OP-SYS-031 item d); (b) for each class of SYS-RST-001 and SYS-RST-002 (power-on reset, watchdog reset, supervisor reset, other reset) and each cause of other reset confirmed in OP-SYS-026 item (a), the definition of the release of the reset as observable at the board and on the simulator of SYS-TST-001, including for a power-on the controller supply level in V from which the not-operational indication is required (refines OP-SYS-031 item b; related OP-SYS-027 item f); (c) the platform reset state of the status-signal pin from the release until software configures it, cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page, the board circuitry on the status signal, and confirmation that together they present the not-operational indication of item (a) with no transient away from it; if a transient cannot be avoided, the approved maximum transient in ms, with which SYS-SAF-003 is to be reworded (refines OP-SYS-031 item c); (d) the evidence accepted for the interval from the release until software configures the pin: analysis of the pin reset state and the board circuitry, the pin state reported by the Renode simulator of SYS-TST-001, or both, and whether that makes analysis the verification method of SYS-SAF-003 for that interval (refines OP-SYS-030 item e and OP-SYS-031 item e); (e) for each class and cause of item (b), whether it can be produced on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 (related OP-SYS-026 item f, OP-SYS-037 items b and c, OP-SYS-061 item f) and, for each that cannot, the evidence accepted instead; (f) the means by which the instant at which each start-up check of SYS-MEM-001 and SYS-MEM-002 has passed is observed on the simulator, and whether instrumentation for it is accepted in the build under test (related OP-SYS-032 item e, OP-SYS-037 item f); (g) for a failed start-up check after which no reset starts, the observation window in ms counted from the release, over which the hold is verified. Refines OP-SYS-030 items (a) to (e) and OP-SYS-031 items (a) to (e) for SYS-SAF-003; OP-SYS-030 and OP-SYS-031 are not changed.

STK-SUP-009 requires the control outputs to be switched off within 50 ms of each fault, and STK-SUP-006 makes the watchdog events faults. The inputs give no control-output list, no off state, no approved watchdog-event instants and no means to have an output on at a watchdog-event instant during a test, and the author cannot approve them. SYS-SAF-004 cannot be given a verdict until a reviewer decides the following: (a) the control outputs, their pins and off states of OP-SYS-028 items (a) to (c), the reset-time pin state of OP-SYS-028 item (d) and the simulator evidence accepted under OP-SYS-028 item (e), these off states being the output-off indication against which SYS-SAF-004 is judged; (b) confirmation that the SYS-WDG-002 event instant is the instant at which the time elapsed since the interval reference instant of SYS-WDG-002 reaches the independent-watchdog timeout, including the first interval after a release without any servicing (resolves OP-SYS-038 item f for SYS-SAF-004), and which timeout value the tester uses to compute it, the configured value or the lower limit of the approved range of OP-SYS-038 item (a), given the clock tolerance of OP-SYS-038 item (c); (c) confirmation that the SYS-WDG-003 event instant is the instant of the early service attempt, whether or not the window watchdog accepts it, in the start-up window and in later windows (resolves OP-SYS-039 item f for SYS-SAF-004); (d) confirmation that the SYS-WDG-004 event instant is the instant at which the window-closing time is reached from the window reference instant of SYS-WDG-004 (resolves OP-SYS-040 item e for SYS-SAF-004); (e) the means accepted to have at least one control output not in its off state at the event instant, in particular for a first-interval timeout and an early attempt in the start-up window, where no application task may yet have switched an output on, and the minimum number of such injections per event class (related OP-SYS-037 item c, OP-SYS-064 item e); (f) whether the window watchdog of the STM32N657X0 rejects a refresh request made before the window opens (OP-SYS-039 item e, to be cited from CON-SUP-002 RM0486 by section and page), how acceptance or rejection of each service attempt is made observable on the simulator of SYS-TST-001 (OP-SYS-037 item f), and, if no rejected attempt can be produced, the approved evidence for the rejected-attempt case; (g) confirmation that reaching the off state through the watchdog reset is the approved behaviour (OP-SYS-029 item e), and whether the off state must also be held until the next reset; (h) SYS-SAF-005 and SYS-TST-003 still state the SYS-WDG-002 event from the last servicing and the SYS-WDG-003 event as a servicing before the window opens; whether they are to use the event instants of SYS-SAF-004. Refines OP-SYS-028, OP-SYS-029 item (e), OP-SYS-038 item (f), OP-SYS-039 item (f) and OP-SYS-040 item (e) for SYS-SAF-004.

STK-SUP-009 requires a status signal showing that the controller is not operational within 50 ms of each fault, and STK-SUP-006 makes the watchdog events faults. SYS-SAF-005 now uses the watchdog-event instants of SYS-SAF-004 (resolves OP-SYS-067 item h for SYS-SAF-005; SYS-TST-003 is not changed). The inputs give no status-signal pin, no indication, no approved event instants and no means to show the operational indication at a watchdog-event instant during a test, and the author cannot approve them. SYS-SAF-005 cannot be given a verdict until a reviewer decides the following: (a) the GPIO pin of CON-SUP-003 that drives the status signal and its not-operational indication (OP-SYS-030 items a to c), this being the approved indication against which SYS-SAF-005 is judged, and confirmation that OP-SYS-030 item (b) and OP-SYS-066 item (a) name the same indication; (b) confirmation that the decisions of OP-SYS-067 items (b), (c), (d) and (f) on the SYS-WDG-002, SYS-WDG-003 and SYS-WDG-004 event instants, including the first interval after a release without any servicing, the rejected early attempt, the timeout value used to compute the SYS-WDG-002 instant and the evidence for a rejected attempt, apply to SYS-SAF-005 unchanged; (c) the reset-time state of the status-signal pin and the time from a watchdog-event instant to the restart software setting the not-operational indication (OP-SYS-030 item d, OP-SYS-066 item c), which decide whether SYS-SAF-005 is met through the watchdog reset or after the restart and whether the restart path meets 50 ms; (d) the means accepted to have the status-signal pin at the operational indication at the event instant, in particular for a first-interval timeout and an early attempt in the start-up window, where SYS-SAF-003 holds the not-operational indication until both start-up checks have passed, including whether the controller shows the operational indication between the passed start-up checks and the first instant of the task-health condition of SYS-WDG-005, and the minimum number of such injections per event class of SYS-SAF-005 test cases (a) to (e) (related OP-SYS-037 item c, OP-SYS-067 item e); (e) whether the status-signal pin state reported by the Renode simulator of SYS-TST-001 is accepted as evidence, including through the reset and restart (OP-SYS-030 item e, OP-SYS-066 item d); (f) confirmation that reaching the not-operational indication through the watchdog reset or the restart is the approved behaviour (OP-SYS-029 item e, OP-SYS-030 item f). Refines OP-SYS-030 items (a) to (f) and OP-SYS-067 items (b) to (d), (f) and (h) for SYS-SAF-005; those open points are not changed.

STK-SUP-007 and STK-SUP-009 imply that the status signal must not show the controller as operational while a reset is in progress. The inputs give no status-signal pin, no indication, no reset boundaries, no supply threshold, no reset-time pin behaviour and no board circuitry, and the author cannot approve them or the evidence. SYS-SAF-006 cannot be given a verdict until a reviewer decides the following: (a) the GPIO pin of CON-SUP-003 that drives the status signal and its not-operational indication (OP-SYS-030 items a to c), confirmation that it is the indication of OP-SYS-066 item (a), and confirmation that it is a static state the pin presents during a reset without software running, for example a stated logic level or voltage range in V or the driver disabled with a stated board-side pull; if only a pattern-type indication is approved, the approved treatment of the reset interval (OP-SYS-031 item d); (b) for each class of SYS-RST-001 and SYS-RST-002 and each cause of other reset confirmed in OP-SYS-026 item (a), the definition of the start and of the release of the reset as observable at the board and on the simulator of SYS-TST-001, including for a power-on the controller supply level in V from which the not-operational indication is required, and confirmation that the release is the instant of OP-SYS-066 item (b) (refines OP-SYS-031 item b); (c) the transition allowance: the approved maximum time in ms from the start of a reset until the pin presents the not-operational indication, per class or cause if they differ, or confirmation that no transition time is allowed (refines OP-SYS-031 item c); (d) the platform behaviour of the status-signal pin, cited from CON-SUP-002 (RM0486) by section and page, for each class and cause: when after the start of the reset the output driver leaves its software-configured state, the pin state during the reset, and at power-on the pin state below and above the supply level of item (b); (e) the board circuitry on the status signal (pull, load, any external driver or monitoring circuit) and the resulting worst-case transition time in ms from the operational to the not-operational indication; (f) the evidence accepted for each class and cause: analysis of items (d) and (e), the pin state reported by the Renode simulator of SYS-TST-001 including whether it models the reset-time pin state and the transition, or both, and for each class or cause the simulator cannot produce, the evidence accepted instead (refines OP-SYS-030 item e and OP-SYS-031 item e; related OP-SYS-026 item f); (g) for each class and cause, the indication the analysis and the test assume at the start of the reset, the operational indication as worst case or confirmation that a cause such as the supervisor reset of SYS-REC-001 always starts from the not-operational indication set under SYS-SAF-002, and the means to have the pin at the operational indication at the start of a reset on the simulator (related OP-SYS-068 item d). Refines OP-SYS-030 items (a) to (e) and OP-SYS-031 items (b) to (e) for SYS-SAF-006; those open points are not changed.
